title: Its beautiful.
body:
Ive had this tv for a couple of months now so here's my thoughts.

The TV itself is built nicely, the base is a solid plate of steel and the tv has a small metal bezel running around the edges but other wise its a standard flatscreen tv with a plastic screen and a plastic back. it won't stand up to any abuse whatsoever and even putting pressure on the screen (according to the manual) can break it. That can be an issue if you're using the tv with its base on the lowest setting when you're trying to move it since it has no handles and you HAVE to hold it by the edges. The I/o at the back has two panels covering it with some extra ports at the side, nothing to note here although this tv does have A/V inputs! however you need a dongle to use this it and the tv DOES NOT INCLUDE THIS DONGLE! for the price? thats unwelcome, the dongle itself isn't a standard so you may have to trial and error it until you get the right connection. the speakers they advertised are okay for casual viewing they sound about as good as a budget soundbar but otherwise nothing remarkable, although there's a sudo surround sound feature but your mileage will vary there, I didn't personally hear a difference. the remote is also nice, it lights up whenever you pick it up, and interestingly you can control this tv with an older Sony receiver from 2006 and up! nothing else to note here, its a solid piece of hardware.

Software is a completely different story, this is a smart tv and upon setting it up you will be greeted by an uncomfortable amount of terms and conditions, you will have to agree to 2 screens worth of terms and conditions naturally I couldn't read them all but I imagine they aren't nice, mostly likely about how their gonna watch everything you do and of course you HAVE to agree or its no tv for you! after agreeing you have the option to set this tv up as a basic tv or a smart tv, as a basic tv you still need an account to set it up (annoyingly). once the tv is setup you get an advertisement for your home screen, yeah they couldn't just leave it a solid colour or something it HAS to be an ad. I personally wanted another dumb tv, but because every oled on the market is a smart tv this is best I could get, so I just run this tv disconnected from the internet. that doesn't get rid of the ad on the home screen by the way, but at least its not watching me. Using this tv with your devices is pretty straightforward although this tv will BEG you to use the included set up tool the first time you hook up a device and won't stop bothering you until you do, and something to note about this tool is that it won't actually set a device up all the way when using devices that support 4k HDR, you have to go into the tvs settings to change the HDMI "input mode" so you can actually run 4k in HDR on your device, otherwise you will either get to run 4k or HDR separately, I had this issue on my switch 2. on the topic of settings the tv gives you many of them you can change RGB values and so on, lots of video processing it can do although thats a matter of preference, you can pretty much set the tv however you like.

It's a good TV, picture quality is excellent and to me anyway it was worth the money although i don't enjoy the smart tv aspects of it at all.

EDIT: I changed the review since the original review left out a lot of detail on what it's like to actually live with and it felt more like a fluff piece than anything and on a device this expensive I wanted to make sure you know what to expect.

title: Fantastic Picture, Build Quality, Interface - Highly Recommended!
body:
*This review is for the 42" XR42A90K.*

We recently finished a major remodel of our kitchen and capped off the project by ordering the Sony XR42A90K. Our kitchen gets a lot of traffic and frequently doubles as my wife's office, so we wanted a TV in the room but not something that would overwhelm the space. The 42" A90K is a fantastic option, having installed it and used it for a bit.

My house is a Sony TV house, having moved away from Samsung products and their awful app environment, short support windows, and subpar performance (in my opinion). This is the fourth Sony TV in our home, and the second OLED. I know LG OLEDs also receive very good reviews, but having a common platform in my house, and one my wife and kids are already familiar with pushed us to the Sony OLED.

►Picture Quality:

I am not a professional TV reviewer, but in my estimation it's hard to beat the picture on a Sony OLED. Our A90K is located in a very bright kitchen and performs terrifically! The picture is very bright, while still offering excellent deep blacks and contrast. Any worry about glare was washed away shortly after powering the TV on for the first time.

→Concerns about burn-in:

I've owned a Sony Master-series OLED in my home theater for years and the TV has not experienced any burn-in at all. I frequently game on that set, for reference, and it's worked great for four years without any noticable burn-in. So, I have no concerns with the A90K at all.

►Google TV:

One of the biggest selling points on Sony TVs is the integration with Google TV. It's incredibly easy to setup (using the Google Home App), and use. My wife and I have Google's Pixel series Android phones, and the integration with our phones is fantastic - for example, we display a rotating album of our favorite family pictures on all of our Sony TVs when they enter stand-by mode. It's one of our favorite features and requires very little user input to get it set up.

The next best thing is the responsiveness of Sony TVs. Switching from app to app, or from cable is a breeze and the A90K responds immediately. I contrast that experience with our awful Samsung TVs that had noticeable lag when pressing any button.

►I/O:

→ 4 × HDMI -- 2 × @ HDMI 2.1 (inputs 3, 4); 2 × @ HDMI 2.0 (inputs 1, 2)

→ 2 × USB 3.0

→ 1 × Optical out

→ 1 × Ethernet

→ 1 × IR (input)

→ 1 × RS232C

→ 1 × Composite (requires adapter, not included in the box)

►Other Things:

→ The A90K comes removeable plastic backplates that cover areas like the cord and I/O. They're great for completing a clean, minimalist look. I have my TV mounted on our kitchen wall but still installed the plates since they cover up part of the side panel too. Again, purely aesthetic, but I love the finished look.

→ There's a mic mute toggle on the side of the TV. If you want a more privacy and aren't interested in using the Google Voice Assistant, turn the mic to mute.

→ I do not use the included stand but I do appreciate that it's made out of metal and not flimsy plastic.

→ The TV does use on-screen ads (unfortunately). I believe that most TVs these days have them, and it sucks. At least they're unobtrusive and you can opt out of personalized ads when you perform the first-time configuration.

→ The remote is compact but excellent. It feels great in-hand and sturdy. It has a minimalist approach to buttons which is great in a household with kids.

►In the Box:

→ A90K TV

→ Remote control

→ 2 × AAA batteries

→ Base plate and metal legs

→ 2 × Cable management straps

→ Manual, user guides, and warranty information

►Closing:

That's it! This TV is fantastic and I'm very pleased with my purchase. The picture quality is fantastic, The user interface, sound, inputs are all the top-notch Sony quality I'm used too! This is definitely a TV I recommend!

title: High end OLED for smaller spaces.
body:
I have always been happy with Sony products. More expensive but they hold up for years. I have a 48 inch Bravira that I bought 15 years ago and it still works like new. If your looking for an inexpensive 42” set just to watch TV in a small room, look elsewhere. The picture is absolutely beautiful and perfect. OLED displays may not beat LCDs in overall brightness but the image is hard to describe adequately. Colors are pure and rich. Blacks go fully black but show remarkable detail in the dark ranges. No brightness or image shift when you move off center of the screen. Very good up-conversion from SD and HD sources.

While it is a high end Google TV, it plays well with Apple devices too. It has only 3 HDMI inputs, one is high speed for a gamer’s PlayStation. This is a great unit for gamers. Low lag and no smear.

This set is really a natural born streamer. HBO Max, Apple TV, Amazon Prime, Google TV, Disney, and almost all services just work well and play 4K UHD without a hiccup. I didn’t need to hook up my Apple TV or Amazon box. It almost magically controls my cable box. It’s not a universal remote, the set itself links the cable box on my network. The remote is small and solid and appears very minimal button wise but works with the set where most remote functions are on screen. There is a mic in the remote with Google assistant. I push a button ask for a specific movie. The set finds the film and connects to the service that is carrying it. Functions switch to whatever source you are watching. This is a smart TV but setting it up requires a steep learning curve. The instructions are a bit vague on details and assume you understand about connecting things to your home network and understand the different sources and connecting services. I’m a broadcast engineer and understand all this but it still took a while to set everything up and if I’m complaining about complexity, I can imagine what it would be like for the average consumer.

The sound is quite good for a small flat panel TV. Because of the thin OLED screen, Sony is able to use it as the speaker surface as well. There is a rear facing woofer for decent Bass. This is the first flat panel set I bought where I feel I didn’t need a sound bar just to watch. This is not rumble your guts surround sound but just decent sound on its own. It has a good equalizer and even a dialogue enhance setting. It connected nicely to my Bluetooth headset.

It’s expensive but it holds its own with the larger high end OLED sets. Perfect for watching from 6 feet away at my kitchen table.

title: Stunning Picture Quality, Seamless Performance – Best TV I’ve Ever Owned
body: I didn’t buy this Sony Bravia XR-42A90K OLED from Amazon—I picked it up from a local retailer—but I wanted to share my experience for others considering this model. To put it simply, this is the best television I’ve ever owned. One of my initial concerns before purchasing was brightness. I had owned a previous Sony TV that really struggled in bright environments, so I was cautious about moving to OLED, which some say can lack punch in well-lit rooms. I needn’t have worried. This television absolutely shines—literally. When set to Vivid picture mode, it’s actually too bright to watch comfortably in a dark room! It handles daylight and brightly lit spaces far better than expected, with clarity and richness that’s seriously impressive. Out of the box, I haven’t felt the need to tweak the colour settings. The default calibration is excellent, delivering vibrant yet natural tones. The combination of OLED technology and Sony’s processing makes for jaw-dropping contrast, inky blacks, and a level of colour accuracy that makes everything—from movies to sports—feel more lifelike. The included remote is also worth mentioning—it's incredibly high quality. It has a premium metal finish, is backlit for nighttime use, and the layout is smart and intuitive. The buttons feel great, and it even has a built-in finder function in case it gets lost. This is the kind of remote you actually enjoy using, which isn’t something I say often. I also paired the TV with a Sony Bravia CMU-BC1 Cam and the HT-A3000 soundbar. Everything works seamlessly together in the Bravia ecosystem, creating a very slick and integrated experience. The interface is intuitive, the connectivity is reliable, and the picture and sound pairing elevates the home theater setup to something truly special. I do have two suggestions for new owners: First, turn off the Eco settings in the Eco Dashboard when you first set the TV up. This will let you see what the television is really capable of before it starts limiting brightness and performance. We found that with Eco features turned off, the image quality improved dramatically—and we decided to leave them off. Second, invest in certified HDMI 2.1 cables for your accessories (I chose Silkland 8K cables). Initially, we ran into strange issues with our old model cable box and brand new Apple TV. Swapping in proper 2.1 cables fixed everything. It’s a simple upgrade that makes a big difference, especially if you’re using high-bandwidth devices. In short: if you’re on the fence about OLED, or about the brightness of a smaller screen, this TV will blow your expectations away. Rich colors, outstanding contrast, surprising brightness, and seamless integration make this an easy recommendation. A phenomenal television.

The picture is great as expected for a high tier TV, I don't think anyone expected any different. Some things I really appreciated about this TV that I think would fly below other people's radar: During setup you can ignore accepting the TOS and EULAs for the streaming software if you don't plan on using them. The controller is nice. It's backlit and feels nice to use. When you turn on the TV it defaults to the last used input method. It has an input button directly on the controller. As someone who swaps between several computers, it's nice to not have to navigate a menu to do it. It's snappy and responsive. title: Great picture, lots of features but very pricey for its size!
body: I recently bought the 42 inch version of A90K and wanted to share some my thoughts about this TV with others who are maybe thinking of purchasing it. It's an extremely expensive TV for its size (it's probably the most expensive small TV out there right now) but for those of us who want the latest and greatest features in a small size this TV is one of the only 2 small OLEDs offered right now. Picture quality: Probably the best thing about the TV, I'm really impressed by the quality of the picture coming from an older Sony LCD TV. The colors are really accurate out of the box and I didn't really tinker with the settings too much (I'm using the Custom picture mode, with Brightness set to 30-35 and Peak Luminance set to Low, contrast at 90, gamma at 0 and black level at 50) to get the picture I'm comfortable with (the picture settings are very customizable so most people should be able to adjust the picture to their liking). I've watched a variety of content so far (sports, movies/shows, news programs, etc.) and haven't noticed any issues as of yet. I'm keeping the Peak Luminance setting at Low to avoid the dreaded Automatic Brightness Limiter (ABL) from kicking in and changing brightness as I'm watching stuff. Reflections: My small living room has bunch of windows (w/blinds) so reflection handling is important to me. During the day I keep the blinds mostly in the closed position (lots of light still gets through, though) and the picture quality is actually pretty decent and I have no trouble watching any type of content (you can adjust Peak Luminance/brightness in the settings to your liking but be wary of ABL at higher brightness settings). However, if I open the blinds it's a different story as the TV can't really get bright enough to overcome all of the reflections so it can be annoying. The screen finish on the TV is semi-gloss/semi-matte (similar to A80J and A80K) and NOT glossy/mirror-like like most other OLEDs (LG C2, for example) which I think is probably better for my environment as the mirror-like reflections would probably drive me crazy during the day. On this TV the reflections are more duller and not widely diffused. Something to keep in mind if you have a really bright room where you can't control the amount of light coming in or a room where you have light fixtures directly opposite the TV. Sound: I don't have a soundbar so I'm using the TV's built-in speakers. The default sound mode on the TV is set to Standard but I've run into numerous issues with this mode on. For example, dialogue between people in movies/shows is way off. There are other sound modes like Dolby and Cinema that are a bit better but still not great. It is possible to customize the settings for each mode and I'm still playing around with them to try and fix the sound issues I'm experiencing (UPDATE: I solved my sound issues by adjusting the 125Hz and 250Hz equalizer under "Sound settings — Sound Customization — Equalizer" so try this if voices are difficult to hear or sound is uneven). Remote: It's backlit which is a very nice feature. It's also lightweight but it doesn't include the physical number pad which might be a problem for some people who watch cable and like to input channel numbers. I'm streaming all my stuff so this remote works very well for me. PlayStation/Gaming: The TV works seamlessly with my PlayStation 5 and supports VRR. There are 4 HDMI ports but only 2 support HDMI 2.1 (one of them is also for eARC), so keep that in mind if you have multiple devices that need 2.1. Smart features: I have a YouTube TV subscription and use other Google services so the fact this TV comes with Google TV as the smart OS is perfect. Navigating through the menus is fairly smooth and I haven't run into any issues as of yet. Build quality: I feel like the build quality is poor, particularly in the back of the TV where everything is made out of plastic, including the top plastic plate. There are clearly visible manufacturing marks on the plastic plate. For a premium TV from their Master Series line and a TV priced at ~$1400 this is not acceptable in my opinion and this is one of the things where they could and should've done much better. Price: As I said earlier, it's way overpriced given its small size and is another thing I don't like. Maybe in the future these small OLEDs will be cheaper but right now the prices very high. As a PC/Mac monitor: Haven't had a chance to hook up the TV to my Mac but plan to do it so I can't really comment on the TV as a monitor yet. I'll try to update the review once I've played around with it a bit more. (UPDATE: I had no issues hooking up the TV to my 2021 Macbook Pro 16 inch but it's limited to 60Hz refresh rate and VRR doesn't work).

title: Its beautiful.
body:
Ive had this tv for a couple of months now so here's my thoughts.

The TV itself is built nicely, the base is a solid plate of steel and the tv has a small metal bezel running around the edges but other wise its a standard flatscreen tv with a plastic screen and a plastic back. it won't stand up to any abuse whatsoever and even putting pressure on the screen (according to the manual) can break it. The I/o at the back has two panels covering it with some extra ports at the side, nothing to note here although this tv does have A/V inputs! however you need a dongle to use this it and the tv DOES NOT INCLUDE THIS DONGLE! for the price? thats unwelcome, the dongle itself isn't a standard so you may have to trial and error it until you get the right connection. the speakers they advertised are okay for casual viewing they sound about as good as a budget soundbar but otherwise nothing remarkable, although there's a sudo surround sound feature but your mileage will vary there, I didn't personally hear a difference. the remote is also nice, it lights up whenever you pick it up, and interestingly you can control this tv with an older Sony receiver from 2006 and up! nothing else to note here, its a solid piece of hardware.

Software is a completely different story, this is a smart tv and upon setting it up you will be greeted by an uncomfortable amount of terms and conditions, you will have to agree to 2 screens worth of terms and conditions naturally I couldn't read them all but I imagine they aren't nice, mostly likely about how their gonna watch everything you do and of course you HAVE to agree or its no tv for you! after agreeing you have the option to set this tv up as a basic tv or a smart tv, as a basic tv you still need an account to set it up (annoyingly). once the tv is setup you get an advertisement for your home screen, yeah they couldn't just leave it a solid colour or something it HAS to be an ad. I personally wanted another dumb tv, but because every oled on the market is a smart tv this is best I could get, so I just run this tv disconnected from the internet. that doesn't get rid of the ad on the home screen by the way, but at least its not watching me. Using this tv with your devices is pretty straightforward although this tv will BEG you to use the included set up tool the first time you hook up a device and won't stop bothering you until you do, and something to note about this tool is that it won't actually set a device up all the way when using devices that support 4k HDR, you have to go into the tvs settings to change the HDMI "input mode" so you can actually run 4k in HDR on your device, otherwise you will either get to run 4k or HDR separately, I had this issue on my switch 2. on the topic of settings the tv gives you many of them you can change RGB values and so on, lots of video processing it can do although thats a matter of preference, you can pretty much set the tv however you like.

It's a good TV, picture quality is excellent and to me anyway it was worth the money although i don't enjoy the smart tv aspects of it at all.

EDIT: I changed the review since the original review left out a lot of detail on what it's like to actually live with and it felt more like a fluff piece than anything and on a device this expensive I wanted to make sure you know what to expect.

title: Fantastic Picture, Build Quality, Interface - Highly Recommended!
body:
*This review is for the 42" XR42A90K.*

We recently finished a major remodel of our kitchen and capped off the project by ordering the Sony XR42A90K. Our kitchen gets a lot of traffic and frequently doubles as my wife's office, so we wanted a TV in the room but not something that would overwhelm the space. The 42" A90K is a fantastic option, having installed it and used it for a bit.

My house is a Sony TV house, having moved away from Samsung products and their awful app environment, short support windows, and subpar performance (in my opinion). This is the fourth Sony TV in our home, and the second OLED. I know LG OLEDs also receive very good reviews, but having a common platform in my house, and one my wife and kids are already familiar with pushed us to the Sony OLED.

►Picture Quality:

I am not a professional TV reviewer, but in my estimation it's hard to beat the picture on a Sony OLED. Our A90K is located in a very bright kitchen and performs terrifically! The picture is very bright, while still offering excellent deep blacks and contrast. Any worry about glare was washed away shortly after powering the TV on for the first time.

→Concerns about burn-in:

I've owned a Sony Master-series OLED in my home theater for years and the TV has not experienced any burn-in at all. I frequently game on that set, for reference, and it's worked great for four years without any noticable burn-in. So, I have no concerns with the A90K at all.

►Google TV:

One of the biggest selling points on Sony TVs is the integration with Google TV. It's incredibly easy to setup (using the Google Home App), and use. My wife and I have Google's Pixel series Android phones, and the integration with our phones is fantastic - for example, we display a rotating album of our favorite family pictures on all of our Sony TVs when they enter stand-by mode. It's one of our favorite features and requires very little user input to get it set up.

The next best thing is the responsiveness of Sony TVs. Switching from app to app, or from cable is a breeze and the A90K responds immediately. I contrast that experience with our awful Samsung TVs that had noticeable lag when pressing any button.

►I/O:

→ 4 × HDMI -- 2 × @ HDMI 2.1 (inputs 3, 4); 2 × @ HDMI 2.0 (inputs 1, 2)

→ 2 × USB 3.0

→ 1 × Optical out

→ 1 × Ethernet

→ 1 × IR (input)

→ 1 × RS232C

→ 1 × Composite (requires adapter, not included in the box)

►Other Things:

→ The A90K comes removeable plastic backplates that cover areas like the cord and I/O. They're great for completing a clean, minimalist look. I have my TV mounted on our kitchen wall but still installed the plates since they cover up part of the side panel too. Again, purely aesthetic, but I love the finished look.

→ There's a mic mute toggle on the side of the TV. If you want a more privacy and aren't interested in using the Google Voice Assistant, turn the mic to mute.

→ I do not use the included stand but I do appreciate that it's made out of metal and not flimsy plastic.

→ The TV does use on-screen ads (unfortunately). I believe that most TVs these days have them, and it sucks. At least they're unobtrusive and you can opt out of personalized ads when you perform the first-time configuration.

→ The remote is compact but excellent. It feels great in-hand and sturdy. It has a minimalist approach to buttons which is great in a household with kids.

►In the Box:

→ A90K TV

→ Remote control

→ 2 × AAA batteries

→ Base plate and metal legs

→ 2 × Cable management straps

→ Manual, user guides, and warranty information

►Closing:

title: High end OLED for smaller spaces.
body:
I have always been happy with Sony products. More expensive but they hold up for years. I have a 48 inch Bravira that I bought 15 years ago and it still works like new. If your looking for an inexpensive 42” set just to watch TV in a small room, look elsewhere. The picture is absolutely beautiful and perfect. OLED displays may not beat LCDs in overall brightness but the image is hard to describe adequately. Colors are pure and rich. Blacks go fully black but show remarkable detail in the dark ranges. No brightness or image shift when you move off center of the screen. Very good up-conversion from SD and HD sources.

While it is a high end Google TV, it plays well with Apple devices too. It has only 3 HDMI inputs, one is high speed for a gamer’s PlayStation. This is a great unit for gamers. Low lag and no smear.

This set is really a natural born streamer. HBO Max, Apple TV, Amazon Prime, Google TV, Disney, and almost all services just work well and play 4K UHD without a hiccup. I didn’t need to hook up my Apple TV or Amazon box. It almost magically controls my cable box. It’s not a universal remote, the set itself links the cable box on my network. The remote is small and solid and appears very minimal button wise but works with the set where most remote functions are on screen. There is a mic in the remote with Google assistant. I push a button ask for a specific movie. The set finds the film and connects to the service that is carrying it. Functions switch to whatever source you are watching. This is a smart TV but setting it up requires a steep learning curve. The instructions are a bit vague on details and assume you understand about connecting things to your home network and understand the different sources and connecting services. I’m a broadcast engineer and understand all this but it still took a while to set everything up and if I’m complaining about complexity, I can imagine what it would be like for the average consumer.

The sound is quite good for a small flat panel TV. Because of the thin OLED screen, Sony is able to use it as the speaker surface as well. There is a rear facing woofer for decent Bass. This is the first flat panel set I bought where I feel I didn’t need a sound bar just to watch. This is not rumble your guts surround sound but just decent sound on its own. It has a good equalizer and even a dialogue enhance setting. It connected nicely to my Bluetooth headset.

It’s expensive but it holds its own with the larger high end OLED sets. Perfect for watching from 6 feet away at my kitchen table.

title: Stunning Picture Quality, Seamless Performance – Best TV I’ve Ever Owned
body: I didn’t buy this Sony Bravia XR-42A90K OLED from Amazon—I picked it up from a local retailer—but I wanted to share my experience for others considering this model. To put it simply, this is the best television I’ve ever owned. One of my initial concerns before purchasing was brightness. I had owned a previous Sony TV that really struggled in bright environments, so I was cautious about moving to OLED, which some say can lack punch in well-lit rooms. I needn’t have worried. This television absolutely shines—literally. When set to Vivid picture mode, it’s actually too bright to watch comfortably in a dark room! It handles daylight and brightly lit spaces far better than expected, with clarity and richness that’s seriously impressive. Out of the box, I haven’t felt the need to tweak the colour settings. The default calibration is excellent, delivering vibrant yet natural tones. The combination of OLED technology and Sony’s processing makes for jaw-dropping contrast, inky blacks, and a level of colour accuracy that makes everything—from movies to sports—feel more lifelike. The included remote is also worth mentioning—it's incredibly high quality. It has a premium metal finish, is backlit for nighttime use, and the layout is smart and intuitive. The buttons feel great, and it even has a built-in finder function in case it gets lost. This is the kind of remote you actually enjoy using, which isn’t something I say often. I also paired the TV with a Sony Bravia CMU-BC1 Cam and the HT-A3000 soundbar. Everything works seamlessly together in the Bravia ecosystem, creating a very slick and integrated experience. The interface is intuitive, the connectivity is reliable, and the picture and sound pairing elevates the home theater setup to something truly special. I do have two suggestions for new owners: First, turn off the Eco settings in the Eco Dashboard when you first set the TV up. This will let you see what the television is really capable of before it starts limiting brightness and performance. We found that with Eco features turned off, the image quality improved dramatically—and we decided to leave them off. Second, invest in certified HDMI 2.1 cables for your accessories (I chose Silkland 8K cables). Initially, we ran into strange issues with our old model cable box and brand new Apple TV. Swapping in proper 2.1 cables fixed everything. It’s a simple upgrade that makes a big difference, especially if you’re using high-bandwidth devices. In short: if you’re on the fence about OLED, or about the brightness of a smaller screen, this TV will blow your expectations away. Rich colors, outstanding contrast, surprising brightness, and seamless integration make this an easy recommendation. A phenomenal television.

title: Great picture, lots of features but very pricey for its size!
body: I recently bought the 42 inch version of A90K and wanted to share some my thoughts about this TV with others who are maybe thinking of purchasing it. It's an extremely expensive TV for its size (it's probably the most expensive small TV out there right now) but for those of us who want the latest and greatest features in a small size this TV is one of the only 2 small OLEDs offered right now. Picture quality: Probably the best thing about the TV, I'm really impressed by the quality of the picture coming from an older Sony LCD TV. The colors are really accurate out of the box and I didn't really tinker with the settings too much (I'm using the Custom picture mode, with Brightness set to 30-35 and Peak Luminance set to Low, contrast at 90, gamma at 0 and black level at 50) to get the picture I'm comfortable with (the picture settings are very customizable so most people should be able to adjust the picture to their liking). I've watched a variety of content so far (sports, movies/shows, news programs, etc.) and haven't noticed any issues as of yet. I'm keeping the Peak Luminance setting at Low to avoid the dreaded Automatic Brightness Limiter (ABL) from kicking in and changing brightness as I'm watching stuff. Reflections: My small living room has bunch of windows (w/blinds) so reflection handling is important to me. During the day I keep the blinds mostly in the closed position (lots of light still gets through, though) and the picture quality is actually pretty decent and I have no trouble watching any type of content (you can adjust Peak Luminance/brightness in the settings to your liking but be wary of ABL at higher brightness settings). However, if I open the blinds it's a different story as the TV can't really get bright enough to overcome all of the reflections so it can be annoying. The screen finish on the TV is semi-gloss/semi-matte (similar to A80J and A80K) and NOT glossy/mirror-like like most other OLEDs (LG C2, for example) which I think is probably better for my environment as the mirror-like reflections would probably drive me crazy during the day. On this TV the reflections are more duller and not widely diffused. Something to keep in mind if you have a really bright room where you can't control the amount of light coming in or a room where you have light fixtures directly opposite the TV. Sound: I don't have a soundbar so I'm using the TV's built-in speakers. The default sound mode on the TV is set to Standard but I've run into numerous issues with this mode on. For example, dialogue between people in movies/shows is way off. There are other sound modes like Dolby and Cinema that are a bit better but still not great. It is possible to customize the settings for each mode and I'm still playing around with them to try and fix the sound issues I'm experiencing (UPDATE: I solved my sound issues by adjusting the 125Hz and 250Hz equalizer under "Sound settings — Sound Customization — Equalizer" so try this if voices are difficult to hear or sound is uneven). Remote: It's backlit which is a very nice feature. It's also lightweight but it doesn't include the physical number pad which might be a problem for some people who watch cable and like to input channel numbers. I'm streaming all my stuff so this remote works very well for me. PlayStation/Gaming: The TV works seamlessly with my PlayStation 5 and supports VRR. There are 4 HDMI ports but only 2 support HDMI 2.1 (one of them is also for eARC), so keep that in mind if you have multiple devices that need 2.1. Smart features: I have a YouTube TV subscription and use other Google services so the fact this TV comes with Google TV as the smart OS is perfect. Navigating through the menus is fairly smooth and I haven't run into any issues as of yet. Build quality: I feel like the build quality is poor, particularly in the back of the TV where everything is made out of plastic, including the top plastic plate. There are clearly visible manufacturing marks on the plastic plate. For a premium TV from their Master Series line and a TV priced at ~$1400 this is not acceptable in my opinion and this is one of the things where they could and should've done much better. Price: As I said earlier, it's way overpriced given its small size and is another thing I don't like. Maybe in the future these small OLEDs will be cheaper but right now the prices very high. As a PC/Mac monitor: Haven't had a chance to hook up the TV to my Mac but plan to do it so I can't really comment on the TV as a monitor yet. I'll try to update the review once I've played around with it a bit more. (UPDATE: I had no issues hooking up the TV to my 2021 Macbook Pro 16 inch but it's limited to 60Hz refresh rate and VRR doesn't work).

title: Rapport qualité-prix très correct, mais point mauvais sur le son
body:
Globalement, je suis satisfait de cette TCL 43" F7D Series. L’image est belle, les couleurs sont vives et l’interface Fire TV est fluide et agréable à utiliser.

En revanche, le son est clairement son plus gros point faible. Les haut-parleurs manquent de puissance et de profondeur, surtout pour les films et les jeux. Une barre de son est presque indispensable pour profiter pleinement de l’expérience.

J’ai aussi remarqué que la qualité des noirs n’est pas toujours au rendez-vous. Dans certaines scènes sombres, on peut voir des dégradations de couleurs ou un manque d’uniformité, ce qui enlève un peu de réalisme à l’image.

title: Great Art TV that fits in well with any decor of your home, with better than average TV performance
body:
I've always wanted art above the mantle in our living room, but also missed having the ability to have a TV for the odd guest that comes over. Looked into those lifestyle TVs, and after comparing Samsung's Frame, vs Hisense's Canvas, I think I made the right choice with the Canvas.

Likes:

- How everything is in one package, without any satellite box

- Large selection of art work to display

- Motion detector to minimize the always on display

- Google TV and integration with Google Home

- Decent HDR/Dolby Vision Performance, SDR is quite good for a VA panel (post color calibration, and greyscaled to 100 nits)

- Matte display really minimizes the glare from very large nearby windows

- Nice touch with the included aluminum frame

Dislikes:

- SDR picture quality out of the box is quite poor, extremely blue tones (but quite good when calibrated)

- Included wall plate for the 65" TV is only 19" wide, where my studs are 20" apart. Only able to land one anchor in a stud, so cautionary with a nearly 65 lbs TV

- Power cable is angled, but you will still need a recessed outlet (I have one), but even then you won't be perfectly flat to the wall. Wish the power input was more in the upper middle to alleviate this

- Audio lacks any sort of bass. It’s passable, but don’t expect miracles from the DTS 2.0.2 system that’s included

If you need something that is primarily art, but love the ability to have a TV conveniently nearby and don’t expect OLED type viewing, then this really balances the best of both worlds!

title: The perfect "Art TV" without the premium price tag!
body:
I've wanted one of those "frame" style TVs for the longest time to go above my fireplace when we moved to a new house but I just couldn't bring myself to pay the premium price for the name brand version. Since I run a small business from home and spend a lot of time in my living room, I really wanted something that looked like decor rather than just a big black rectangle on the wall. After a lot of research, I went with the 55 inch Hisense CanvasTV, and I am so happy I did!

Installation & Look

The installation was surprisingly straightforward. It comes with an ultra-slim wall mount that lets it sit flush against the wall, which is key for making it actually look like a piece of art. The teak bezel is a really nice feature too; it just snaps on magnetically and instantly elevates the whole look. The 55 inch size is absolutely perfect for the space above my mantle and it fits the proportions of the room without being overwhelming.

The Art Mode & Display

I love that there are so many different art pieces to choose from right out of the box. You can really match the mood of the room or the season. I will say, it does take some picture adjusting to get that perfect matte, "painting" look. The Hi-Matte display is great at cutting out glare from my windows, but you have to play with the brightness and color settings to make it look less like a screen and more like a canvas. A little online research goes a long way here, but once you find the right settings, it looks incredible!

Motion Sensor & Performance

The motion sensor, which controls the auto on and off, can be a bit of a hit or miss sometimes. However, it’s been much more reliable recently, even though I didn’t change any of my settings. I’m wondering if a new firmware update came out that smoothed things over. It’s been great lately at "sleeping" when no one is around and then turning right back on to the canvas mode the second we walk by. It’s so nice to walk into the room and see a beautiful landscape instead of a blank screen.

Overall

If you want that high-end designer look but don't want to break the bank, this is a fantastic option. The picture quality is sharp for movie nights, but the way it transforms into art during the day is what really makes it special. It has been a wonderful addition to my home, and I’ve already had a few guests ask if it was a real painting during visits.

title: It's a great, big TV.
body:
I bought the 85" and have been very impressed with this TV. I agree with comments about the picture quality, both for TV and for art mode. FWIW, at normal brightness, it's obvious that the "art" is on a screen. But if you turn the brightness down in art mode, it looks much more realistic.

I was also pleased to see that there are hundreds of art options available. It may take time for them to load onto your TV after you set it up. I would guess hundreds were added to our library over the first night.

Unpacking and setup weren't that bad, but it did take me a couple of hours. You will definitely need more than one person to hang this TV on the wall. The most tedious part was hanging and leveling the wall brackets. There is a template in the packaging that is very helpful.

As far as things that could be better, I'd start with the sound. I've read several reviews praising the sound quality, but I don't find it that impressive. Voices sound muffled and music doesn't seem to have much depth. It feels like I'm listening to music on a giant phone. I will probably buy additional audio equipment to pair with the TV.

Also, this beast of a TV (around 108 lbs) hangs on two wall brackets. The instructions clearly call for anchoring 4 lag bolts on each plate into solid studs or masonry (no drywall anchors!). The instructions further acknowledge that standard stud spacing is 16" to 18". But the plates are 12" wide. So, unless you're fortunate enough to have tighter stud spacing, you'll only be able to anchor two of the four lag bolts into a stud. It would be great if they'd either make one large plate or make both plates long enough that you actually have a chance at landing all the bolts on a stud. As it is, I'd have to cut my wall open to add extra studs.

Finally, it would be nice if there was a way to search through the artwork for artists or by the name of a particular work. Currently, the art that comes with the TV is classified into four categories (landscapes, modern, still life, and other) and it takes a lot of time to scroll through the options.

Overall, I'm happy with this TV. The picture quality is awesome, but the 85" is huge. In hindsight, I kind of wish I would have gotten the 75". It's in a really big room, but I don't think the extra width (9 inches) has made that much of a difference in the viewing experience, especially for the difference in cost ($600 as I write this).

title: Came for the flush mount, stayed for the artwork
body:
This is a great TV. As a TV itself, the picture quality is good, not as good as a much more expensive OLED but no complaints if you’re not looking for that level of quality and at that kind of price point. The Matt finish is nice, especially if it’s in a more welded room. I mounted mine on the wall and it was relatively straightforward. If you know how to use a level and a yardstick and have some time to really do it right. It’s nearly flushed to the wall and really does look like a hanging art piece.

The controls are very intuitive and relatively easy to navigate. Some of the advanced sound features you need to dig through the menus to find. However, the overall interface makes sense and is not laggy like a lot of smart TVs can be integration into Google home or Apple HomeKit is also very nice. It has all the features and a top smart TV has like Google cast, Apple AirPlay, PC streaming, etc. etc.,and they work just fine. The sound quality by itself is not bad, especially flat against the wall, but I highly recommend at least a sound bar to get a much better audio quality. But if you don’t have anything like that, it’s not too bad.

However, what really makes this TV stand out, especially against the more expensive Samsung Frame, is the vast free library of art pieces available which look amazing on the matte screen. There’s no annoying subscription and it gets updated often with new pieces, literally hundreds. We have turned TV this into a conversation piece with our family where we are not just watching shows and movies together, but we are looking at art and talking about it and enjoying some of the well-known classics from Monet, etc., to many more obscure pieces that are also amazing and beautiful. For better or worse, our modern world tends to dominate our attention by endless screens perpetually seeking to overstimulate us. It’s nice to see a piece of technology that lets you intentionally choose to do the opposite, if you choose. It lets you slow down and be present and take something beautiful in and think about it. This allows you to change the whole feel of the room this TV is in. Rather than just a media box our dopamine addicted brains mindlessly gravitate towards, enslaved by the algorithms, it opens up the possibility of turning the room into a space ofsubtle and peaceful, quiet thoughtfulness. I think if this To only had art on it and wasn’t a real TV I still would enjoy having it in my house for this reason alone.

title: Firmware allows side-loading APK apps. No analogue Audio out. A very good budget TV overall.
body:
The image quality is as expected from a QLED panel. Pretty good, but some blooming is clearly visible in totally dark scenes. Unless you are a pixel-peeper, you'll probably be quite happy with the image quality. Otherwise get a mini-LED TV or better.

I was concerned when I read in another comment that the TCL's version of Fire TV was locked down. I found this to be untrue. I was able to enable Developer Access (by clicking on the About dialogue 7+ times), and allowing Downloader to install unknown APK files, and then it was smooth sailing. You can then side-load individual apps (like KODI) or even alternative app stores (like F-Droid).

Adding a universal remote was super easy, just add new Fire TV device to it, and add the remote through the settings.

The TV consumes 10W of power in standby mode (when it's "turned off"). If turning the TV on from complete "cold" state (i.e. power disconnected), it takes about 30 seconds to boot into Fire TV.

It consumes anywhere between 60W and 150W during playback. While idling in the home screen, it consumes 120W!

I don't like the home screen very much, and hope to replace it with a different launcher soon, but I have not got to it yet.

I'm using the TV with Ethernet connection to the Internet, and it works flawlessly. I can't comment on its WiFi reception since I don't use WiFi.

The interface feels very snappy! There is no perceivable lag between clicks and reactions to the clicks. Feels great.

The sound is what you'd expect from built-in speakers. I'm upset that there are no analogue audio out: only optical. But my amp is analogue.

I mounted my TV to the wall from day 1. There were no surprises. You need M6 screws, about 12mm long. Two screws are provided (they were already in the TV), but two other holes did not have screws in them, so I needed to find two more screws.

My dislikes are related to the Fire TV OS, not the hardware. One dislike is that if I switch TV to an HDMI input, and then turn it off, then, when I turn it on again, it does not remember that it was in an HDMI input mode, and takes me back to the Fire TV home screen. So I need to click through to switch inputs again. Another dislike is that, in my understanding, Amazon resists letting most Google apps into the Fire TV's official app store. So there are no Google apps for Google Photos, for screen casting from a Pixel phone, etc.

title: Massive upgrade to the Hisense 55" Hi-QLED Mini-LED TV
body:
I’ve been using the Hisense 55" Hi‑QLED Mini‑LED AI TV (55U7SG) for a few weeks now, and it punches well above its price for anyone who plays games or watches a lot of HDR content. The mini‑LED backlight delivers very high peak brightness and strong contrast, while the native 165Hz panel makes motion look exceptionally smooth in games and movies.

What I love:

Mini‑LED brightness and contrast: The TV uses thousands of local dimming zones and can reach very high peak brightness, so HDR highlights pop and dark scenes stay detailed without too much blooming.

165Hz gaming performance: With HDMI 2.1 on all four ports, VRR (48-165Hz), AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, and very low input lag, this is one of the best midrange TVs for PS5/PC gaming.

Matte anti‑reflective screen: The anti‑glare coating really helps in bright rooms; reflections are much less distracting than on glossy panels.

Google TV connectivity: The Google TV interface is fast, Wi‑Fi 6E is a nice future‑proof touch, and you get 4x HDMI 2.1, 2x USB, Ethernet, and eARC on HDMI 3.

Sound that’s actually usable: The 2.1.2 speaker setup sounds full and gets loud enough for casual viewing without immediately needing a soundbar.

Trade‑offs to know:

Viewing angles: Like many VA‑style mini‑LEDs, colors and contrast wash out if you sit far off to the side; it’s best for straight‑on viewing.

Default picture processing: Out of the box, some scenes can look a bit over‑processed; a quick tweak of motion and noise reduction settings cleans this up.

Gaming features are PC‑leaning: You can hit 165Hz at 4K with a PC; consoles will still benefit from VRR/ALLM but are capped by their own output limits.

Final Verdict

If you want a bright, high‑refresh‑rate TV for gaming and HDR movies without paying flagship prices, the 55U7SG is an excellent choice. Just plan to sit relatively centered and be ready to tweak picture settings for your taste.

I have a large window in my room where the TV is set up and the light is directly on the TV all day, this has caused some issues for us for the last TV, but this TV performs especially well in a bright living room. HDR movies and shows look detailed and immersive, with bright highlights that really stand out. Dolby Vision IQ and HDR10+ also help scenes look more balanced and realistic.

Gaming experience and performance is also another upgrade for me, especially the native 165Hz refresh rate and Game Booster mode make gameplay feel extremely smooth and responsive. Fast-moving scenes remain sharp, and the enhanced Game Bar makes it easy to check settings such as frame rate, HDR, and VRR without leaving the game. The built-in 2.1.2-channel sound system is better than I expected from a television. Dialogue is clear, bass has some presence, and Dolby Atmos adds a wider, more immersive soundstage. A dedicated soundbar would still provide a more cinematic experience, but the built-in speakers are more than adequate for everyday use.

Overall it feels like a premium television that I'm very satisfied with and would recommend it to anyone looking for a large-screen TV that performs well for movies, sports, streaming, and gaming.

I also enabled Dynamic Color Boost, which made it even better!! If you like your colors to pop, this is the tv for you!! *FAR MORE SETTINGS THAN YOUR AVERAGE FIRE TV!! I was really surprised to see all of the extra settings on this tv compared to my other fire televisions! *A CENTER STAND!!! Yes, a stand that does not have feet several feet apart!! I have a tv stand from the 1990s that is made of pure wood and is still great!! They don't make them like this anymore. Plus, it sits high up, so it's not like the current stands which are quite low. It worked perfectly with this tv. *PREMIUM REMOTE!! Yes, a really nice, backlit remote!! The only thing I don't like is that the little bump on the home screen button is missing. But I guess it's easy to get used to, so it may not really be needed to know where the home button is. *DISPLAYS ARTWORK!! You have the option to display images or artwork on the screen when you are not watching tv. The NOT SO GOOD: *LIGHT LEAKAGE!!! There is, unfortunately, a little bit of light leakage. I see it on the right side center, and left side bottom. It's not terrible, but I know it's there. I don't have this on my older, cheaper televisions, so this was a disappointment. A real disappointment. I would think that there would be better quality control on a tv at this price. But I guess not. I like to watch tv in a totally dark environment, and it is there. But in a brightly lit room, it's not really noticeable at all. *SOUND NOT AS IMPRESSIVE AS I THOUGHT IT WOULD BE!! I use a home theater system from 15+ years ago which still works great. At first I tried the built-in sound system, but it's not as good as the Panasonic home theater. I disabled the tv's internal sound and use the HT. It also automatically turns on when the tv does. *NOT AS GLARE-FREE AS ADVERTISED!! I don't see much difference between this tv's screen finish, and my lower-end 2022 QLED. *PRICE DROP RIGHT AFTER PURCHASE!! Probably the most disappointing thing was that the price dropped just before it went out for delivery. Couldn't get a credit or gift card for the difference. Was told I would have to return it and redorder. I hate to return things, and almost never do. Retuning a big-ticket item like this kind of a tv is not really a good idea if not defective. I guess I could have returned it for the very slight light leakage, but I could get another one that's just the same. Or worse. Or maybe not. Who knows. But I just couldn't disassemble and rebox it. Too much trouble for the newer price. In summation, this is a tv with a fantastic picture, especially in color and brightness. Lots of extra features over your typical fire tv. But the price drop was the most disappointing part of the experience. One star off for the light leakage and two stars off for the price drop. It's just how I feel about it!!

title: Great TV! Horrible delivery!
body:
DELIVERY HORROR STORY BELOW.

I've only worked with this new TV a few hours, but so far I'm very pleased compared to the 4-yr-old Amazon FireTV that this replaces.

PROS: Great picture! Clear, bright, sharp, no motion blurring. The FireTV support is responsive, and all but one of my apps from the old TV (Xfinity Stream, which is a crappy app anyway) ported over automatically. And it has a center stand, so it fits on my location without having to resort to a separate VESA mount stand.

CONS: The built-in sound quality isn't as good as I expected based on the sales info, but my Klipsch soundbar/sub takes care of that. However, the stand doesn't raise the TV body quite high enough, so that the soundbar obscures the Alexa pod and infrared sensor on the bottom of the TV - the stand should be more adjustable for height.

HORROR: I ordered this during Prime Days, and paid extra for the delivery/unboxing service - this service is provided by an outside contractor, not by Amazon itself. I was given a delivery schedule of 2 days after the order, a Friday, between noon and 5pm. I changed my schedule to be home those hours, but had dinner plans for later in the evening. The unit didn't arrive by 5, but at 5:30 I got the "Your package is 10 stops away!" notification from Amazon, so I cancelled the dinner plans and continued to wait. About 10pm the tracking info updated to say there was a problem with delivery. :(:( The next morning, I received a call from an Amazon rep (speaking broken English) saying that I wasn't home for the delivery. I explained that I WAS home, and had changed schedule and plans to be here but the truck never showed up. She asked for the earliest 3 days I could be available for delivery, and I replied the next three days (Sunday thru Tuesday.) She replied that she would get it into their system and I would be emailed with the actual delivery date & time window. On Sunday, I received that email, with a schedule of Wednesday. I complained, but to no avail, and after waiting 3 more days, the TV was finally delivered.

Here's the kicker: When I asked the delivery guys why it wasn't delivered on the original date, they whined that all the Prime Days orders overloaded them and they "ran out of time", so my and some other orders just got hauled back to the depot without even an attempt to deliver!

So let this be a warning: if you buy any large item from Amazon with the delivery/setup service, know that there's a decent chance that you will have headaches, inconvenience and wasted time.

title: Massive upgrade to the Hisense 55" Hi-QLED Mini-LED TV
body:
I’ve been using the Hisense 55" Hi‑QLED Mini‑LED AI TV (55U7SG) for a few weeks now, and it punches well above its price for anyone who plays games or watches a lot of HDR content. The mini‑LED backlight delivers very high peak brightness and strong contrast, while the native 165Hz panel makes motion look exceptionally smooth in games and movies.

What I love:

Mini‑LED brightness and contrast: The TV uses thousands of local dimming zones and can reach very high peak brightness, so HDR highlights pop and dark scenes stay detailed without too much blooming.

165Hz gaming performance: With HDMI 2.1 on all four ports, VRR (48-165Hz), AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, and very low input lag, this is one of the best midrange TVs for PS5/PC gaming.

Matte anti‑reflective screen: The anti‑glare coating really helps in bright rooms; reflections are much less distracting than on glossy panels.

Google TV connectivity: The Google TV interface is fast, Wi‑Fi 6E is a nice future‑proof touch, and you get 4x HDMI 2.1, 2x USB, Ethernet, and eARC on HDMI 3.

Sound that’s actually usable: The 2.1.2 speaker setup sounds full and gets loud enough for casual viewing without immediately needing a soundbar.

Trade‑offs to know:

Viewing angles: Like many VA‑style mini‑LEDs, colors and contrast wash out if you sit far off to the side; it’s best for straight‑on viewing.

Default picture processing: Out of the box, some scenes can look a bit over‑processed; a quick tweak of motion and noise reduction settings cleans this up.

Gaming features are PC‑leaning: You can hit 165Hz at 4K with a PC; consoles will still benefit from VRR/ALLM but are capped by their own output limits.

Final Verdict

If you want a bright, high‑refresh‑rate TV for gaming and HDR movies without paying flagship prices, the 55U7SG is an excellent choice. Just plan to sit relatively centered and be ready to tweak picture settings for your taste.

title: Very satisfied, premium feeling!
body:
I recently purchased the Hisense 75-inch U7 Mini-LED ULED 4K Smart Fire TV, and my first impressions have been excellent. My wife and I set it up pretty easily. The picture quality is the biggest highlight. The Mini-LED backlighting produces impressive brightness, deep black levels, and strong contrast, while the Hi-QLED panel delivers rich, vibrant colors without making the image look overly artificial. I like the quality of the remote control, very premium feel and responsive.

I have a large window in my room where the TV is set up and the light is directly on the TV all day, this has caused some issues for us for the last TV, but this TV performs especially well in a bright living room. The anti-reflection screen significantly reduces glare from windows and overhead lighting, picture remains clear during daytime viewing. HDR movies and shows look detailed and immersive, with bright highlights that really stand out. Dolby Vision IQ and HDR10+ also help scenes look more balanced and realistic.

Gaming experience and performance is also another upgrade for me, especially the native 165Hz refresh rate and Game Booster mode make gameplay feel extremely smooth and responsive. Fast-moving scenes remain sharp, and the enhanced Game Bar makes it easy to check settings such as frame rate, HDR, and VRR without leaving the game. It is a great match for modern gaming consoles and high-performance PCs.

The built-in 2.1.2-channel sound system is better than I expected from a television. Dialogue is clear, bass has some presence, and Dolby Atmos adds a wider, more immersive soundstage. A dedicated soundbar would still provide a more cinematic experience, but the built-in speakers are more than adequate for everyday use.

Overall it feels like a premium television that I'm very satisfied with and would recommend it to anyone looking for a large-screen TV that performs well for movies, sports, streaming, and gaming.

title: Hisense U7SF: The Great, the Not So Good, and the Downright Disappointing!!
body: I recently bought a Hisense QD7 to replace a 2021 tv for my kitchen table. Even though it's a lower-end model, I was quite impressed with it. I was also looking to replace a QLED tv from 2022 as my main tv. Looking at the current offerings, I chose the Hisense U7SF, as it is a newly released tv. If the QD7 was quite good, I was expecting the U7SF to be much better. And it some ways, I was absolutely right. But, not everyting was perfect. Pros: *EASY SET-UP. It was flawless, unlike my QD7, which stalled during registration and required an unplugging and replugging. *FANTASTIC PICTURE!! Wow, totally amazing. However, at first, the tv is set to "energy saving" mode. Which is terrible. I quickly changed it to VIVID, and the colors are truly incredible. I also enabled Dynamic Color Boost, which made it even better!! If you like your colors to pop, this is the tv for you!! *FAR MORE SETTINGS THAN YOUR AVERAGE FIRE TV!! I was really surprised to see all of the extra settings on this tv compared to my other fire televisions! *A CENTER STAND!!! Yes, a stand that does not have feet several feet apart!! I have a tv stand from the 1990s that is made of pure wood and is still great!! They don't make them like this anymore. Plus, it sits high up, so it's not like the current stands which are quite low. It worked perfectly with this tv. *PREMIUM REMOTE!! Yes, a really nice, backlit remote!! The only thing I don't like is that the little bump on the home screen button is missing. But I guess it's easy to get used to, so it may not really be needed to know where the home button is. *DISPLAYS ARTWORK!! You have the option to display images or artwork on the screen when you are not watching tv. The NOT SO GOOD: *LIGHT LEAKAGE!!! There is, unfortunately, a little bit of light leakage. I see it on the right side center, and left side bottom. It's not terrible, but I know it's there. I don't have this on my older, cheaper televisions, so this was a disappointment. A real disappointment. I would think that there would be better quality control on a tv at this price. But I guess not. I like to watch tv in a totally dark environment, and it is there. But in a brightly lit room, it's not really noticeable at all. *SOUND NOT AS IMPRESSIVE AS I THOUGHT IT WOULD BE!! I use a home theater system from 15+ years ago which still works great. At first I tried the built-in sound system, but it's not as good as the Panasonic home theater. I disabled the tv's internal sound and use the HT. It also automatically turns on when the tv does. *NOT AS GLARE-FREE AS ADVERTISED!! I don't see much difference between this tv's screen finish, and my lower-end 2022 QLED. *PRICE DROP RIGHT AFTER PURCHASE!! Probably the most disappointing thing was that the price dropped just before it went out for delivery. Couldn't get a credit or gift card for the difference. Was told I would have to return it and redorder. I hate to return things, and almost never do. Retuning a big-ticket item like this kind of a tv is not really a good idea if not defective. I guess I could have returned it for the very slight light leakage, but I could get another one that's just the same. Or worse. Or maybe not. Who knows. But I just couldn't disassemble and rebox it. Too much trouble for the newer price. In summation, this is a tv with a fantastic picture, especially in color and brightness. Lots of extra features over your typical fire tv. But the price drop was the most disappointing part of the experience. One star off for the light leakage and two stars off for the price drop. It's just how I feel about it!!

title: Great TV! Horrible delivery!
body:
DELIVERY HORROR STORY BELOW.

I've only worked with this new TV a few hours, but so far I'm very pleased compared to the 4-yr-old Amazon FireTV that this replaces.

PROS: Great picture! Clear, bright, sharp, no motion blurring. The FireTV support is responsive, and all but one of my apps from the old TV (Xfinity Stream, which is a crappy app anyway) ported over automatically. And it has a center stand, so it fits on my location without having to resort to a separate VESA mount stand.

CONS: The built-in sound quality isn't as good as I expected based on the sales info, but my Klipsch soundbar/sub takes care of that. However, the stand doesn't raise the TV body quite high enough, so that the soundbar obscures the Alexa pod and infrared sensor on the bottom of the TV - the stand should be more adjustable for height.

HORROR: I ordered this during Prime Days, and paid extra for the delivery/unboxing service - this service is provided by an outside contractor, not by Amazon itself. I was given a delivery schedule of 2 days after the order, a Friday, between noon and 5pm. I changed my schedule to be home those hours, but had dinner plans for later in the evening. The unit didn't arrive by 5, but at 5:30 I got the "Your package is 10 stops away!" notification from Amazon, so I cancelled the dinner plans and continued to wait. About 10pm the tracking info updated to say there was a problem with delivery. :(:( The next morning, I received a call from an Amazon rep (speaking broken English) saying that I wasn't home for the delivery. I explained that I WAS home, and had changed schedule and plans to be here but the truck never showed up. She asked for the earliest 3 days I could be available for delivery, and I replied the next three days (Sunday thru Tuesday.) She replied that she would get it into their system and I would be emailed with the actual delivery date & time window. On Sunday, I received that email, with a schedule of Wednesday. I complained, but to no avail, and after waiting 3 more days, the TV was finally delivered.

Here's the kicker: When I asked the delivery guys why it wasn't delivered on the original date, they whined that all the Prime Days orders overloaded them and they "ran out of time", so my and some other orders just got hauled back to the depot without even an attempt to deliver!

So let this be a warning: if you buy any large item from Amazon with the delivery/setup service, know that there's a decent chance that you will have headaches, inconvenience and wasted time.

title: Firmware allows side-loading APK apps. No analogue Audio out. A very good budget TV overall.
body:
The image quality is as expected from a QLED panel. Pretty good, but some blooming is clearly visible in totally dark scenes. Unless you are a pixel-peeper, you'll probably be quite happy with the image quality. Otherwise get a mini-LED TV or better.

I was concerned when I read in another comment that the TCL's version of Fire TV was locked down. I found this to be untrue. I was able to enable Developer Access (by clicking on the About dialogue 7+ times), and allowing Downloader to install unknown APK files, and then it was smooth sailing. You can then side-load individual apps (like KODI) or even alternative app stores (like F-Droid).

Adding a universal remote was super easy, just add new Fire TV device to it, and add the remote through the settings.

The TV consumes 10W of power in standby mode (when it's "turned off"). If turning the TV on from complete "cold" state (i.e. power disconnected), it takes about 30 seconds to boot into Fire TV.

It consumes anywhere between 60W and 150W during playback. While idling in the home screen, it consumes 120W!

I don't like the home screen very much, and hope to replace it with a different launcher soon, but I have not got to it yet.

I'm using the TV with Ethernet connection to the Internet, and it works flawlessly. I can't comment on its WiFi reception since I don't use WiFi.

The interface feels very snappy! There is no perceivable lag between clicks and reactions to the clicks. Feels great.

The sound is what you'd expect from built-in speakers. I'm upset that there are no analogue audio out: only optical. But my amp is analogue.

I mounted my TV to the wall from day 1. There were no surprises. You need M6 screws, about 12mm long. Two screws are provided (they were already in the TV), but two other holes did not have screws in them, so I needed to find two more screws.

My dislikes are related to the Fire TV OS, not the hardware. One dislike is that if I switch TV to an HDMI input, and then turn it off, then, when I turn it on again, it does not remember that it was in an HDMI input mode, and takes me back to the Fire TV home screen. So I need to click through to switch inputs again. Another dislike is that, in my understanding, Amazon resists letting most Google apps into the Fire TV's official app store. So there are no Google apps for Google Photos, for screen casting from a Pixel phone, etc.

title: Massive upgrade to the Hisense 55" Hi-QLED Mini-LED TV
body:
I’ve been using the Hisense 55" Hi‑QLED Mini‑LED AI TV (55U7SG) for a few weeks now, and it punches well above its price for anyone who plays games or watches a lot of HDR content. The mini‑LED backlight delivers very high peak brightness and strong contrast, while the native 165Hz panel makes motion look exceptionally smooth in games and movies.

What I love:

Mini‑LED brightness and contrast: The TV uses thousands of local dimming zones and can reach very high peak brightness, so HDR highlights pop and dark scenes stay detailed without too much blooming.

165Hz gaming performance: With HDMI 2.1 on all four ports, VRR (48-165Hz), AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, and very low input lag, this is one of the best midrange TVs for PS5/PC gaming.

Matte anti‑reflective screen: The anti‑glare coating really helps in bright rooms; reflections are much less distracting than on glossy panels.

Google TV connectivity: The Google TV interface is fast, Wi‑Fi 6E is a nice future‑proof touch, and you get 4x HDMI 2.1, 2x USB, Ethernet, and eARC on HDMI 3.

Sound that’s actually usable: The 2.1.2 speaker setup sounds full and gets loud enough for casual viewing without immediately needing a soundbar.

Trade‑offs to know:

Viewing angles: Like many VA‑style mini‑LEDs, colors and contrast wash out if you sit far off to the side; it’s best for straight‑on viewing.

Default picture processing: Out of the box, some scenes can look a bit over‑processed; a quick tweak of motion and noise reduction settings cleans this up.

Gaming features are PC‑leaning: You can hit 165Hz at 4K with a PC; consoles will still benefit from VRR/ALLM but are capped by their own output limits.

Final Verdict

If you want a bright, high‑refresh‑rate TV for gaming and HDR movies without paying flagship prices, the 55U7SG is an excellent choice. Just plan to sit relatively centered and be ready to tweak picture settings for your taste.

title: Very satisfied, premium feeling!
body:
I recently purchased the Hisense 75-inch U7 Mini-LED ULED 4K Smart Fire TV, and my first impressions have been excellent. My wife and I set it up pretty easily. The picture quality is the biggest highlight. The Mini-LED backlighting produces impressive brightness, deep black levels, and strong contrast, while the Hi-QLED panel delivers rich, vibrant colors without making the image look overly artificial. I like the quality of the remote control, very premium feel and responsive.

I have a large window in my room where the TV is set up and the light is directly on the TV all day, this has caused some issues for us for the last TV, but this TV performs especially well in a bright living room. The anti-reflection screen significantly reduces glare from windows and overhead lighting, picture remains clear during daytime viewing. HDR movies and shows look detailed and immersive, with bright highlights that really stand out. Dolby Vision IQ and HDR10+ also help scenes look more balanced and realistic.

Gaming experience and performance is also another upgrade for me, especially the native 165Hz refresh rate and Game Booster mode make gameplay feel extremely smooth and responsive. Fast-moving scenes remain sharp, and the enhanced Game Bar makes it easy to check settings such as frame rate, HDR, and VRR without leaving the game. It is a great match for modern gaming consoles and high-performance PCs.

The built-in 2.1.2-channel sound system is better than I expected from a television. Dialogue is clear, bass has some presence, and Dolby Atmos adds a wider, more immersive soundstage. A dedicated soundbar would still provide a more cinematic experience, but the built-in speakers are more than adequate for everyday use.

Overall it feels like a premium television that I'm very satisfied with and would recommend it to anyone looking for a large-screen TV that performs well for movies, sports, streaming, and gaming.

title: Hisense U7SF: The Great, the Not So Good, and the Downright Disappointing!!
body: I recently bought a Hisense QD7 to replace a 2021 tv for my kitchen table. Even though it's a lower-end model, I was quite impressed with it. I was also looking to replace a QLED tv from 2022 as my main tv. Looking at the current offerings, I chose the Hisense U7SF, as it is a newly released tv. If the QD7 was quite good, I was expecting the U7SF to be much better. And it some ways, I was absolutely right. But, not everyting was perfect. Pros: *EASY SET-UP. It was flawless, unlike my QD7, which stalled during registration and required an unplugging and replugging. *FANTASTIC PICTURE!! Wow, totally amazing. However, at first, the tv is set to "energy saving" mode. Which is terrible. I quickly changed it to VIVID, and the colors are truly incredible. I also enabled Dynamic Color Boost, which made it even better!! If you like your colors to pop, this is the tv for you!! *FAR MORE SETTINGS THAN YOUR AVERAGE FIRE TV!! I was really surprised to see all of the extra settings on this tv compared to my other fire televisions! *A CENTER STAND!!! Yes, a stand that does not have feet several feet apart!! I have a tv stand from the 1990s that is made of pure wood and is still great!! They don't make them like this anymore. Plus, it sits high up, so it's not like the current stands which are quite low. It worked perfectly with this tv. *PREMIUM REMOTE!! Yes, a really nice, backlit remote!! The only thing I don't like is that the little bump on the home screen button is missing. But I guess it's easy to get used to, so it may not really be needed to know where the home button is. *DISPLAYS ARTWORK!! You have the option to display images or artwork on the screen when you are not watching tv. The NOT SO GOOD: *LIGHT LEAKAGE!!! There is, unfortunately, a little bit of light leakage. I see it on the right side center, and left side bottom. It's not terrible, but I know it's there. I don't have this on my older, cheaper televisions, so this was a disappointment. A real disappointment. I would think that there would be better quality control on a tv at this price. But I guess not. I like to watch tv in a totally dark environment, and it is there. But in a brightly lit room, it's not really noticeable at all. *SOUND NOT AS IMPRESSIVE AS I THOUGHT IT WOULD BE!! I use a home theater system from 15+ years ago which still works great. At first I tried the built-in sound system, but it's not as good as the Panasonic home theater. I disabled the tv's internal sound and use the HT. It also automatically turns on when the tv does. *NOT AS GLARE-FREE AS ADVERTISED!! I don't see much difference between this tv's screen finish, and my lower-end 2022 QLED. *PRICE DROP RIGHT AFTER PURCHASE!! Probably the most disappointing thing was that the price dropped just before it went out for delivery. Couldn't get a credit or gift card for the difference. Was told I would have to return it and redorder. I hate to return things, and almost never do. Retuning a big-ticket item like this kind of a tv is not really a good idea if not defective. I guess I could have returned it for the very slight light leakage, but I could get another one that's just the same. Or worse. Or maybe not. Who knows. But I just couldn't disassemble and rebox it. Too much trouble for the newer price. In summation, this is a tv with a fantastic picture, especially in color and brightness. Lots of extra features over your typical fire tv. But the price drop was the most disappointing part of the experience. One star off for the light leakage and two stars off for the price drop. It's just how I feel about it!!

The image quality is as expected from a QLED panel. Pretty good, but some blooming is clearly visible in totally dark scenes. Unless you are a pixel-peeper, you'll probably be quite happy with the image quality. Otherwise get a mini-LED TV or better.

I was concerned when I read in another comment that the TCL's version of Fire TV was locked down. I found this to be untrue. I was able to enable Developer Access (by clicking on the About dialogue 7+ times), and allowing Downloader to install unknown APK files, and then it was smooth sailing. You can then side-load individual apps (like KODI) or even alternative app stores (like F-Droid).

Adding a universal remote was super easy, just add new Fire TV device to it, and add the remote through the settings.

The TV consumes 10W of power in standby mode (when it's "turned off"). If turning the TV on from complete "cold" state (i.e. power disconnected), it takes about 30 seconds to boot into Fire TV.

It consumes anywhere between 60W and 150W during playback. While idling in the home screen, it consumes 120W!

I don't like the home screen very much, and hope to replace it with a different launcher soon, but I have not got to it yet.

I'm using the TV with Ethernet connection to the Internet, and it works flawlessly. I can't comment on its WiFi reception since I don't use WiFi.

The interface feels very snappy! There is no perceivable lag between clicks and reactions to the clicks. Feels great.

The sound is what you'd expect from built-in speakers. I'm upset that there are no analogue audio out: only optical. But my amp is analogue.

I mounted my TV to the wall from day 1. There were no surprises. You need M6 screws, about 12mm long. Two screws are provided (they were already in the TV), but two other holes did not have screws in them, so I needed to find two more screws.

My dislikes are related to the Fire TV OS, not the hardware. One dislike is that if I switch TV to an HDMI input, and then turn it off, then, when I turn it on again, it does not remember that it was in an HDMI input mode, and takes me back to the Fire TV home screen. So I need to click through to switch inputs again. Another dislike is that, in my understanding, Amazon resists letting most Google apps into the Fire TV's official app store. So there are no Google apps for Google Photos, for screen casting from a Pixel phone, etc.
