title: Good backup remote for my Tv's
body:
I got this replacement voice remote mainly to keep as a backup because remotes always seem to disappear right when you need them. I have two Hisense TVs, so I liked the idea of having an extra one around in case the original gets lost, dropped, or just stops working. It is one of those things you do not think you need until the main remote is missing under the couch or someone walks off with it.

The remote feels pretty close to the original style. It has the same kind of slim shape, and the buttons are laid out in a way that makes sense if you are already used to a Hisense remote. The shortcut buttons are nice to have too, especially for Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video, and Disney. I like not having to scroll through menus every time I want to open an app. The buttons have a decent click to them and do not feel overly mushy.

The voice button is also a nice feature if your TV supports it. It makes searching for shows or opening apps quicker than typing everything out with the arrow buttons. That is probably one of the biggest reasons I wanted a voice remote instead of just a very basic replacement. It makes the TV feel like normal again instead of feeling like you are using a cheap backup remote.

Setup was simple for me. I mainly wanted this as a spare, so I was not looking for anything complicated. Once it was paired, it worked like I expected. The navigation ring works well, the volume and channel buttons are easy to reach, and the home button is in a good spot. It is also lightweight, which is nice for daily use, though it does mean it does not feel quite as heavy or premium as some original remotes.

One thing I would say is to make sure your Hisense model is actually compatible before buying. Replacement remotes can be hit or miss depending on the TV model, so it is worth double checking instead of assuming it will work with every Hisense TV. Also, since this is a backup remote for me, I cannot say how it will hold up after years of heavy use, but so far it seems fine for normal everyday use.

Overall, I am happy with it. It is a good remote to have around as a spare, especially if you have more than one Hisense TV or you have kids, pets, or anyone in the house who tends to misplace remotes. It does what I needed it to do, the buttons are easy to use, and it is much better than being stuck using the TV buttons or a phone app when the main remote goes missing.

title: It fell short of expectations. I was very disappointed.
body:
I had wanted to buy this for a long time, but held off because of the price. I finally grabbed the 48-inch model during a sale, taking advantage of a good discount and Amazon’s 5-month installment plan. However, the quality fell short of my expectations. I expected it to be lightweight, but it actually weighs 20kg. On the positive side, I was very satisfied with the build quality, finish, and design, all of which felt premium. Since I bought it strictly to use as a computer monitor, I can't comment on its performance as a TV.

I am currently using a 48-inch QLED monitor from another brand, and its overall quality feels superior to the OLED C6. It is much brighter and sharper, yet it cost only a fraction of the price (about one-fifth). The color reproduction doesn't seem to differ much from the OLED, either. Feeling the OLED screen was a bit dim, I asked an AI about increasing the brightness, and it advised against going above 70% to prevent the self-emissive pixels from overheating, which can shorten their lifespan and increase the risk of burn-in. I had assumed burn-in and brightness issues were largely resolved in the OLED C6, but that turned out not to be the case. I was dismayed to find that, despite the high price, I couldn't fully utilize the OLED due to these concerns, and it offered no real advantage over the cheaper QLED.

After agonizing over the decision for a few days, I decided to return it. Amazon's return process was swift, and the refund was issued immediately. I used Purolator for the pickup—I requested a home collection, and they picked it up within four hours. I truly trust Amazon and am always grateful for their excellent service. My fantasy about OLED technology is officially over.

title: An Amazing TV with Incredible Picture Quality and Worth Every Penny!
body:
I'm genuinely impressed with this TV. From the moment I first turned it on, the picture quality blew me away. The blacks are incredibly deep, the colours are rich and vibrant without looking artificial, and everything looks amazingly sharp and detailed.

Watching movies on this TV is a fantastic experience. It really gives you that home theatre feeling. Sports look excellent, too, and gaming has been just as impressive. Everything feels smooth and responsive, and the high refresh rate and VRR support are great features for anyone who enjoys gaming.

It's definitely an expensive TV, but I knew I was buying a premium product, and so far, it has absolutely lived up to my expectations. I wanted a TV that would genuinely impress me every time I turned it on, and that's exactly what I got.

UPDATE: A few thoughts on privacy

I've noticed some people raising concerns about privacy with LG Smart TVs, so I decided to look into it myself and share what I found.

According to LG, features such as Automatic Content Recognition (ACR), voice recognition, and personalized advertising can be managed through the TV's privacy settings. LG also states that its TVs are not continuously recording your conversations.

LG explains that ACR uses audio fingerprinting to identify supported content rather than taking screenshots or recording everything displayed on your screen. Depending on which features you enable, certain viewing habits and device information may be collected and processed.

Personally, I think the important thing is understanding what you're agreeing to and knowing which settings you can change. Everyone has different comfort levels when it comes to privacy, so I'd suggest spending a few minutes reviewing the privacy settings during the initial setup rather than simply accepting everything without looking.

My final thoughts

I'm still extremely happy with my LG G6. The picture quality is outstanding, gaming has been fantastic, and watching movies and sports is an absolute pleasure. Yes, it's expensive, but for me, the experience has been worth it.

If you're considering this TV and want a premium OLED experience, I highly recommend it. I couldn't be happier with my purchase!

title: Awesome, but could be more.
body:
This 27-inch Samsung movable screen changed the way I consume media. Ironically, I use it a lot for music.

The box it came in is very heavy and had to be delivered by two people. The rolling base is what makes it so heavy. I struggled a bit to handle it on my own, so be careful not to lift it with your arm extended and your back straight, as you could hurt yourself.

Once everything is set up, which is pretty easy, it took me a little while to understand where the cables needed to go. There's a cable that plugs directly into the base and into the wall to keep it powered and charge the monitor's internal battery. There's also a USB-C port behind the monitor if you ever need to charge it without the base.

The rolling base moves really well and is easy to reposition, and the monitor arm is also easy to manipulate to get the screen exactly where you want it. It's possible to use the monitor in both portrait and landscape mode.

On first power-up, the setup is quick and easy, though it took me a few tries for my SmartThings app to successfully connect to the monitor. I don't know why.

The touch navigation takes some getting used to, but the included remote works like a charm. The UI is fast and responsive, though a bit bloated with ads and recommendations.

The 2560×1440 screen resolution feels borderline on such a big display, but it still looks beautiful for media consumption. It's just a little grainy, and combined with the matte screen, it can sometimes give the impression of a cheaper display. On such an expensive device, I honestly would've liked at least a 4K panel, and OLED would've been a really great addition. The 120Hz refresh rate works well though, and everything feels fluid and smooth.

I chose to limit the battery charge to 85% to extend its lifespan, and I get a little over two hours of use when it's not plugged in. I really wish the battery lasted longer. With everything you can do with a monitor like this, a minimum of five hours of battery life would be appreciated. It replaces a TV, a monitor, and a tablet, so a larger battery would make this device much more convenient and versatile.

The speakers are surprisingly very good. I live in an apartment and cast my Spotify music to the monitor. I usually keep the volume between 10 and 13 because I'm worried anything louder would bother the neighbors.

Talking about Spotify, there are three things I don't like:

1. The device doesn't support Spotify playback in the background. Meaning that if you leave the Spotify app to go somewhere else in the menu, the music stops playing.

2. The album cover page shown on the monitor while music is playing only displays the first song you casted, then stays the same for the entire session. So after the first song, you keep seeing the same cover even if you're listening to something completely different.

3. Once in a while, at least once a day, it randomly stops playing music, almost like it lost connection with Spotify. Sometimes I'm able to reconnect right away, while other times it simply won't work and I have to listen to Spotify on my PC for about an hour before it starts working again on the monitor.

Overall, this is a device that has the potential to completely change how you watch TV, play games (thanks to Xbox Cloud and Amazon Luna support), and work. It performs really well, feels smooth and fluid, but at this price point, I'd expect a bit more in terms of battery life and screen quality.

PS: A retractable cable that you could pull out to plug in, then have roll back into the base when not needed, would be an awesome addition.

title: Great user experience right out of the box
body:
I had high expectations for this product and it delivers!

Setting up is a breeze. The TV and stand can be set up in under 5mins. Once you plug it in, it's ready to go with an invitation to scan a barcode for easy set up. After scanning the barcode, the TV automatically linked with my gmail account. Even with a few software updates, the TV was up and running in under 10 minutes.

It’s definitely easy to use for non-tech people. The screen is intuitive. A light touch with three fingers to return to the home screen, or touch the lower right corner to pull up a menu. The remote is small, but similarly intuitive and looks just like all the other modern samsung TV remotes.. I opted to connect the TV to my phone. When I'm in the same room as the TV, I have the option to use my phone as a remote.

The TV quality is clear and the strong sound quality came as a welcome surprise.

I love the mobility of the TV. It's on a sturdy base with all-direction wheels, plus the screen moves up/ down, side to side, and from panoramic to portrait with ease. The monitor arm is excellent quality. The screen moves with minimal effort and stays in place.

The screen can easily be disconnected from the stand, and sit on the table - which makes it great as a second monitor that connects wirelessly to my laptop. It has over 2.5 hours of use before needing a charge. It can also be charged with a USB C cable (which is provided).

The TV also has a lot of unexpected features that I'm not sure I'll ever use. It can be used as a gaming hub and display artwork from a free catalogue. It can also work as a computer - by logging in to Microsoft Office 365, and using a wireless keyboard and mouse. I suppose this is helpful if you don’t have your laptop around. It could also be used as a wall calendar when not in use as a TV (similar to a Dak Board). These functions all fall into the category of interesting, but not sure I'll ever use. I may in future use it for music.

Overall, I love it as a dual function product as both a TV and second monitor.

Pros

- Setting up is a breeze and it's easy to use a TV screen or a spare monitor

- The screen, sound and the movable base and arm, are all exceptional quality

- Everything is included in the box - cables and remote

- Removing the screen from the base and reattaching it is easy

- It has the potential to replace both my TV and second computer monitor

Cons

- It's delivered in a large box, and the side of the box holding the base is very very heavy. Plan on having two people around on the delivery day

- As with any new piece of smart technology, it can collect large amounts of data from the user. I would suggest immediately opting out of the optional advertising. I also set up a single-use email address for all my smart devices

- One day I will probably drop the screen, and I don't see an option to just repurchase just the screen. That's a risk of having multi-use devices and being naturally clumsy.

- You need to be in the same room to use your phone as a remote. If the TV could be controlled from a different location, this product would be very useful for people supporting aging parents. In the future, it would be nice to be able to set up in a parent's house, then remotely help them watch a movie.

- It has a microphone/ AI listening feature. Although this could be useful, I prefer not to have my screens listening to me.

- It really thinks I want to watch Bay Watch. I'm not sure why, but it frequently starts Bay Watch episodes as I'm scrolling for a TV show. I'm sure this is user error.

- It doesn't support the Tidal app (my preferred music app), but it does support Spotify. This may actually prompt me to switch to Spotify

Overall this is a fantastic purchase of the highest quality, like most Samsung products that I own.

title: Cool hardware, not sure if value is really there though. Horrible Tizen OS experience
body:
Update May 18th 2026:

After reading some other reviews I'd like to comment on few things:

- charging while having the screen in use actually works fine in my case - I guess the other user didn't have the charger strong enough to support the current use and give the screen little extra to charge it,

- the speakers are really disappointing in my opinion. When I put my MacBook Pro 14 next to the screen - the Mac sounds fuller and has more bass. I believe Samsung could do better considering how big the device is.

- refresh rate: I tested this again and sadly I have to confirm that 120Hz doesn't work via HDMI or USB-C cable. 60Hz is the max I can select,

Original Review:

It's a smooth experience scrolling through pages and apps thanks to 120Hz. Resolution is lacking a bit though - why is it only 2560x1440? I think it should be 4K as it looks little grainy especially combined with matte screen surface. It's really up to the user what you prefer, personally I think I'd pick a shiny OLED over this. Also, when the screen is off you can kind of see where you swiped (looking from an angle).

It's a missed opportunity: if the panel itself would be a little better I would totally use it beside my desk as an extended monitor for my laptop and then move it away if I need it elsewhere. I like that it takes USB-C input from my laptop but I'm sad that it doesn't provide touch input at the same time... (cannot control the PC with touch from this screen).

Tizen OS. Oh my, this is a nightmare in my book. It feels to be locked in more than Apple ecosystem. There is no side loading which is a problem with its limited store. They should just allow for Android apps to be installed. I was looking for a better internet browser and there is no way to install Firefox, Chrome or anything proper. And trust me, you really need a proper browser on a big tablet like that. I get that default Tizen browser might be enough on TVs people have in living rooms, but on a tablet-like screen - not a chance this will fly.

So even though this is a top of the shelf screen with smart OS I still need to plug in external devices through HDMI to it. It shouldn't be like that.

That said, I like the hardware overall. Maybe the battery could be a bit bigger. The battery seems to be installed inside the handle. It can give you 3 hours of video playback. I was surprised to find it there, the screen itself is so thick that I was sure the battery is behind the panel.

The portability is a big plus although the base could be little lighter, I don't think it's really possible to tip this screen with current crazy heavy base (and it's a good think, but it also feels over engineered).

The most appealing use case of this screen for me is cloud gaming. It supports a few major providers and many kinds of controllers over Bluetooth.

title: Very interesting design, good picture and sound
body:
The SAMSUNG 27-Inch The Movingstyle LSM7F QHD Touch Interaction Movable Screen is one of the most unique displays I’ve used in a long time. After spending a good amount of time with it, I’d give it 4 stars because it does a lot of things really well, but it also has several limitations that make the very high price hard to justify. The overall design is absolutely gorgeous and feels very premium right out of the box. Samsung clearly put effort into the presentation too — the packaging and instructions are cleverly designed, and the way the box helps line up the parts during assembly makes setup easier than expected. That said, this thing is HEAVY. You may realistically want two people for the initial setup and moving the base around during assembly. Once assembled though, the heavy base becomes one of the product’s biggest strengths because it feels extremely stable and difficult to tip over accidentally.

The screen itself is excellent for casual entertainment use. The 27-inch QHD panel is bright, colorful, and large enough to comfortably watch movies or YouTube from a chair or bed. The touchscreen interface works surprisingly well for navigating apps and menus, and the integrated speakers are much louder and fuller sounding than I expected from something this slim. I especially liked rolling it beside a Lazy Boy chair for casual viewing because the mobility genuinely changes how you use a display like this. The rolling base glides smoothly over hardwood and most flooring surfaces, although the wheels collect dog hair very easily and can struggle on loose rugs or thicker carpet. The heavy-duty rear handle is also very well designed and doubles as a stand/grab point when repositioning the display, although you don’t get any choice in viewing angle when using it that way. The swing arms and hinges move smoothly and feel solid, but the overall range of motion is more limited than I expected considering how flexible the marketing makes it appear.

The smart features are where my feelings became more mixed. Samsung’s Tizen OS works adequately, but it feels restrictive compared to Android TV or even modern streaming boxes. The interface is clean enough, but customization options are very limited and there are basically no advanced-user settings to tweak. You also can’t sideload apps, so you’re completely dependent on Samsung’s app ecosystem. Another annoyance is that the TV always seems to resume the last app or media source instead of simply booting to a neutral home screen. If you paused a video before shutting it off, powering it back on often immediately jumps back into that content, which became irritating pretty quickly. Requiring a Samsung account for full functionality also feels unnecessary on a product at this price point.

Wireless casting support is decent but clearly optimized for Samsung phones. I was able to cast from Android devices, but getting screen mirroring and desktop-style functionality working consistently with my Google Pixel phone was frustrating. The desktop mode experience in particular was not very usable. If you already live heavily in Samsung’s ecosystem, you’ll probably have a much smoother experience than I did. I did appreciate the inclusion of a physical microphone mute switch though — it’s a small detail, but one I always like seeing on smart devices.

Samsung advertises this as a 120Hz display, but this area feels confusing and somewhat misleading. There’s no easy way to verify the refresh rate in normal use, and from my testing it appeared that higher refresh support may only apply within the Tizen environment itself. Over HDMI, I was limited to 4K at 30Hz, QHD at 60Hz, or 1080p at 60Hz, which is disappointing for a product marketed around a 120Hz panel. Gamers or PC users expecting high refresh external input support should definitely research this carefully before buying.

Battery life ended up being better than expected. I consistently got over 3 hours of runtime depending on brightness and usage, and a full recharge took roughly 2 hours. However, the charging behavior is oddly restrictive. The display can charge from a 45W or higher USB-C charger, but only while the display is powered off. If you want to actively use it while charging, you need to use the included base charging system. It works, but it’s another example of the product feeling more closed off than it needs to be.

Overall, this is a very cool product that genuinely feels futuristic and fun to use in the right environment. It looks fantastic, sounds good, rolls around easily, and works great as a casual movable entertainment screen. At the same time, the extremely high price, restrictive software ecosystem, limited advanced functionality, and unclear refresh rate support keep it from being an easy recommendation. If you specifically want a stylish movable smart display and are already invested in Samsung’s ecosystem, you’ll probably love it. If you’re expecting a flexible high-end monitor/TV hybrid with open functionality, you may find the limitations frustrating.

Pros:

- Premium modern design that looks fantastic.

- Solar powered remote is a fantastic idea.

- Large, bright QHD touchscreen display.

- Heavy stable base is difficult to tip over.

- Wheels roll smoothly on most hard surfaces.

- Loud, surprisingly good built-in speakers.

- Secure locking mechanism between display and base.

- Smooth swing arm movement and sturdy handle design.

- Physical microphone mute switch.

- Battery lasts over 3 hours in real-world use.

- Setup instructions and packaging are very well designed.

Cons:

- Extremely expensive for what it offers.

- Very heavy and awkward during setup.

- Tizen OS feels restrictive and lacks advanced settings.

- Limited app ecosystem with no sideloading support.

- Wireless casting works best only with Samsung phones.

- Desktop mode support was disappointing with Pixel devices.

- HDMI refresh rate support appears limited despite 120Hz marketing.

- Cannot easily boot directly to the home screen.

- Rollers collect pet hair easily.

- Limited adjustment range on hinges and swing arms.

- USB-C charging limitations while the display is in use.

Compared to some of last year’s OLEDs, like the Samsung S90F and LG C5 OLED TVs, the M70H is not really in the same performance category. Since the OLEDs are closer to $2000 and the M70H is under $1000, the M70H makes more sense if price is your main priority. title: Good Budget Mini LED, But the M80H Is Worth Upgrading to
body: The Samsung M70H is a good budget Mini LED TV for anyone who wants one of Samsung's new 2026 line-up of Mini LED TV while staying under $1000. The picture is bright, colourful, and sharp enough for everyday streaming, and watching TV. It provides a nice upgrade for anyone coming from an older LED TV, while giving you the benefits of Mini LED brightness over basic LED models. That said, this is clearly the more budget-focused option from Samsung’s 2026 Mini LED line-up. The 60Hz panel, cheaper processor, and lower overall picture quality make it less ideal if you are looking to for a premium home theatre TV or a better gaming display. Compared to some of last year’s OLEDs, like the Samsung S90F and LG C5 OLED TVs, the M70H is not really in the same performance category. OLEDs have much better black levels, more precise contrast, and a much more premium picture overall because each pixel can turn off individually. This is especially noticeable in darker scenes or when watching movies at night. However, the M70H is also much cheaper. Since the OLEDs are closer to $2000 and the M70H is under $1000, the M70H makes more sense if price is your main priority. If this is going in a bedroom, basement, garage, or casual living space, it can still be a good choice, but if this is your main TV, I would try to stretch your budget a bit to the M80H. Compared to Samsung’s higher-end Mini LEDs, like the M80H and QN80H, the M70H is clearly the entry-level option. The M80H is the model I would usually recommend upgrading to because it has a better picture, a better processor, and 144Hz support instead of only a 60Hz panel. Since the M80H is under $1200, the price difference is usually worth it unless the M70H is heavily discounted or you really cannot afford to spend any more. The QN80H is a much better TV again, thanks to its a more refined Quantum Mini LED picture, stronger contrast, and much more premium quality image, but it is also much more expensive. Setup was mostly straightforward, but like the other Samsung TVs, the account and SmartThings process can slow things down if you do not already have everything ready. If you have a Samsung account ready and a Samsung device connected to the WiFi, setup can be fairly quick, but creating a new account without any connected devices can make it take closer to 15-20 minutes. I do like that the 65" and larger sizes has two or more different positions for the feet, which makes it easier to place on a smaller table. Samsung’s Tizen software is responsive and has most of the major streaming apps, but I wish it supported popular VPN apps like you can get on Google TV. That said, if you want to use a VPN, you will need to use one of the supported options or use an external Google TV streaming box. Overall, the M70H is a solid budget Mini LED TV, but I would only go with it if the price difference from the M80H is too steep. It is good for casual viewing and works well as a secondary TV, but the M80H is worth the upgrade for most people because of its better picture quality, 144Hz support, and stronger overall performance. Pros: - Good budget Mini LED TV under $1000. - Bright, colourful, and sharp picture for everyday viewing. - Nice upgrade over older basic LED TVs. - Flexible placement for the legs/feet for the 65"+ models is helpful for smaller TV stands. Cons: - Only has a 60Hz panel, making it worse for gaming and motion. - Cheaper processor and worse overall picture quality than the slightly more expensive M80H. - AI display modes seem to make the picture look washed out. - Samsung account/SmartThings creation can slow down setup if not created ahead of time. - Most popular VPN apps require an external Google TV box.

title: Smooth Upgrade with Impressive Picture & Performance
body: Setup was honestly very easy—plug, connect, and you’re pretty much ready to go. I upgraded from a two-year-old LG QNED, and right away this Samsung feels faster and more refined. The interface is smooth, apps open quickly, and everything just feels responsive without lag. The video quality is where this TV really stands out. The Mini LED panel brings better brightness and more detailed contrast compared to a regular LED, so scenes look more alive and sharp. Colors are vibrant but still natural thanks to Samsung’s Pure Colour Spectrum, and the 4K upscaling does a great job making even older content look clean and crisp. Sound quality is also surprisingly solid. It’s not just loud—it actually adapts to what you’re watching, so dialogue is clear and effects feel more immersive. Features like Object Tracking Sound Lite and adaptive audio tuning help make everything feel more balanced. For gaming and everyday use, it performs really well. Motion handling is smooth, and the Gaming Hub is a nice addition if you’re into cloud gaming or switching between consoles. Overall, it’s a great mix of performance, picture quality, and ease of use. If you’re coming from an older TV like I did, this definitely feels like a proper upgrade—fast, clean, and enjoyable to use every day.

title: Pretty good
body: I own several TV’s including OLED’s, laser projectors, etc. and for me, this is a nice entry level unit that certainly has its place. Usually, I go very in-depth with TV reviews, but for this one I will try to keep it short. Picture During my testing, I found the M70 to have a great picture when it came to sharpness and colour, but the blacks are definitely lacking. Don’t get me wrong, it does a decent job with dark scenes, but when pushed (The Dark Knight, 1917, The Batman, Gravity, etc.), you can definitely see the light bleed and the blacks tend to be a bit grey. However, bright scenes and colours look excellent for the most part (Furiosa was a standout) and regular TV/sports work well. Speaking of sports, even though this maxes at 60hz, I found it handled hockey pretty well and blur was not overly distracting. Sound Sound was decent and certainly great for a bedroom or garage, but it can’t compete with a full surround system or a sound bar like this one (https://www.amazon.ca/dp/B0DQ2T15GJ). Stand/Remote The stand is fine and it is easy to attach the legs, but personally, I prefer a centre/pedestal stand since it gives you more placement options (smaller TV stands for example). The remote is minimalistic, works well as a universal and gets the job done, but it lacks lighting. Overall, this is an excellent TV for a bedroom, garage, or living room where you are not looking for a cinema experience. It has a great overall picture, decent sound, and has a reasonable $998 price tag. However, if you are willing to spend a bit more to get those OLED blacks, the well reviewed entry level LG B5 is currently ~$400 more (https://www.amazon.ca/LG-65-Inch-OLED-Smart-Built/dp/B0F8DMQWM2) and the brighter, higher end C5 is ~$950 more (https://www.amazon.ca/LG-65-Inch-OLED-Smart-Built/dp/B0F7J14C5Q). For me this is a great secondary TV for my bedroom and I am more than happy with the picture/price. As promised, I kept it pretty short and hopefully made your decision a bit easier. Recommended Good luck with your decision/purchase

title: Good Budget Mini LED, But the M80H Is Worth Upgrading to
body: The Samsung M70H is a good budget Mini LED TV for anyone who wants one of Samsung's new 2026 line-up of Mini LED TV while staying under $1000. The picture is bright, colourful, and sharp enough for everyday streaming, and watching TV. It provides a nice upgrade for anyone coming from an older LED TV, while giving you the benefits of Mini LED brightness over basic LED models. That said, this is clearly the more budget-focused option from Samsung’s 2026 Mini LED line-up. The 60Hz panel, cheaper processor, and lower overall picture quality make it less ideal if you are looking to for a premium home theatre TV or a better gaming display. Compared to some of last year’s OLEDs, like the Samsung S90F and LG C5 OLED TVs, the M70H is not really in the same performance category. OLEDs have much better black levels, more precise contrast, and a much more premium picture overall because each pixel can turn off individually. This is especially noticeable in darker scenes or when watching movies at night. However, the M70H is also much cheaper. Since the OLEDs are closer to $2000 and the M70H is under $1000, the M70H makes more sense if price is your main priority. If this is going in a bedroom, basement, garage, or casual living space, it can still be a good choice, but if this is your main TV, I would try to stretch your budget a bit to the M80H. Compared to Samsung’s higher-end Mini LEDs, like the M80H and QN80H, the M70H is clearly the entry-level option. The M80H is the model I would usually recommend upgrading to because it has a better picture, a better processor, and 144Hz support instead of only a 60Hz panel. Since the M80H is under $1200, the price difference is usually worth it unless the M70H is heavily discounted or you really cannot afford to spend any more. The QN80H is a much better TV again, thanks to its a more refined Quantum Mini LED picture, stronger contrast, and much more premium quality image, but it is also much more expensive. Setup was mostly straightforward, but like the other Samsung TVs, the account and SmartThings process can slow things down if you do not already have everything ready. If you have a Samsung account ready and a Samsung device connected to the WiFi, setup can be fairly quick, but creating a new account without any connected devices can make it take closer to 15-20 minutes. I do like that the 65" and larger sizes has two or more different positions for the feet, which makes it easier to place on a smaller table. Samsung’s Tizen software is responsive and has most of the major streaming apps, but I wish it supported popular VPN apps like you can get on Google TV. That said, if you want to use a VPN, you will need to use one of the supported options or use an external Google TV streaming box. Overall, the M70H is a solid budget Mini LED TV, but I would only go with it if the price difference from the M80H is too steep. It is good for casual viewing and works well as a secondary TV, but the M80H is worth the upgrade for most people because of its better picture quality, 144Hz support, and stronger overall performance. Pros: - Good budget Mini LED TV under $1000. - Bright, colourful, and sharp picture for everyday viewing. - Nice upgrade over older basic LED TVs. - Flexible placement for the legs/feet for the 65"+ models is helpful for smaller TV stands. Cons: - Only has a 60Hz panel, making it worse for gaming and motion. - Cheaper processor and worse overall picture quality than the slightly more expensive M80H. - AI display modes seem to make the picture look washed out. - Samsung account/SmartThings creation can slow down setup if not created ahead of time. - Most popular VPN apps require an external Google TV box.

title: Smooth Upgrade with Impressive Picture & Performance
body: Setup was honestly very easy—plug, connect, and you’re pretty much ready to go. I upgraded from a two-year-old LG QNED, and right away this Samsung feels faster and more refined. The interface is smooth, apps open quickly, and everything just feels responsive without lag. The video quality is where this TV really stands out. The Mini LED panel brings better brightness and more detailed contrast compared to a regular LED, so scenes look more alive and sharp. Colors are vibrant but still natural thanks to Samsung’s Pure Colour Spectrum, and the 4K upscaling does a great job making even older content look clean and crisp. Sound quality is also surprisingly solid. It’s not just loud—it actually adapts to what you’re watching, so dialogue is clear and effects feel more immersive. Features like Object Tracking Sound Lite and adaptive audio tuning help make everything feel more balanced. For gaming and everyday use, it performs really well. Motion handling is smooth, and the Gaming Hub is a nice addition if you’re into cloud gaming or switching between consoles. Overall, it’s a great mix of performance, picture quality, and ease of use. If you’re coming from an older TV like I did, this definitely feels like a proper upgrade—fast, clean, and enjoyable to use every day.

title: Pretty good
body: I own several TV’s including OLED’s, laser projectors, etc. and for me, this is a nice entry level unit that certainly has its place. Usually, I go very in-depth with TV reviews, but for this one I will try to keep it short. Picture During my testing, I found the M70 to have a great picture when it came to sharpness and colour, but the blacks are definitely lacking. Don’t get me wrong, it does a decent job with dark scenes, but when pushed (The Dark Knight, 1917, The Batman, Gravity, etc.), you can definitely see the light bleed and the blacks tend to be a bit grey. However, bright scenes and colours look excellent for the most part (Furiosa was a standout) and regular TV/sports work well. Speaking of sports, even though this maxes at 60hz, I found it handled hockey pretty well and blur was not overly distracting. Sound Sound was decent and certainly great for a bedroom or garage, but it can’t compete with a full surround system or a sound bar like this one (https://www.amazon.ca/dp/B0DQ2T15GJ). Stand/Remote The stand is fine and it is easy to attach the legs, but personally, I prefer a centre/pedestal stand since it gives you more placement options (smaller TV stands for example). The remote is minimalistic, works well as a universal and gets the job done, but it lacks lighting. Overall, this is an excellent TV for a bedroom, garage, or living room where you are not looking for a cinema experience. It has a great overall picture, decent sound, and has a reasonable $998 price tag. However, if you are willing to spend a bit more to get those OLED blacks, the well reviewed entry level LG B5 is currently ~$400 more (https://www.amazon.ca/LG-65-Inch-OLED-Smart-Built/dp/B0F8DMQWM2) and the brighter, higher end C5 is ~$950 more (https://www.amazon.ca/LG-65-Inch-OLED-Smart-Built/dp/B0F7J14C5Q). For me this is a great secondary TV for my bedroom and I am more than happy with the picture/price. As promised, I kept it pretty short and hopefully made your decision a bit easier. Recommended Good luck with your decision/purchase

title: Great product, secure packaging and easy to setup and use

Plastic cover was scratched and I thought for sure I would have scratches on the screen itself it not worse but thankfully once the plastic was peeled off everything was perfect underneath. Kudos to Samsung for going the extra mile in packaging it. Setup is easy and straight forward, if you have a Samsung account you can even use your phone as a remote with smart things which is useful if it gets misplaced (Note the remote is small, slender and sleek which makes it easy for little children to hide/lose). Picture quality is good, the AI enhancement is hit or miss as 80% of the time it makes the picture better but sometimes it appears to backfire and make the image a bit more grainier. title: Good Budget Mini LED, But the M80H Is Worth Upgrading to
body: The Samsung M70H is a good budget Mini LED TV for anyone who wants one of Samsung's new 2026 line-up of Mini LED TV while staying under $1000. The picture is bright, colourful, and sharp enough for everyday streaming, and watching TV. It provides a nice upgrade for anyone coming from an older LED TV, while giving you the benefits of Mini LED brightness over basic LED models. That said, this is clearly the more budget-focused option from Samsung’s 2026 Mini LED line-up. The 60Hz panel, cheaper processor, and lower overall picture quality make it less ideal if you are looking to for a premium home theatre TV or a better gaming display. Compared to some of last year’s OLEDs, like the Samsung S90F and LG C5 OLED TVs, the M70H is not really in the same performance category. OLEDs have much better black levels, more precise contrast, and a much more premium picture overall because each pixel can turn off individually. This is especially noticeable in darker scenes or when watching movies at night. However, the M70H is also much cheaper. Since the OLEDs are closer to $2000 and the M70H is under $1000, the M70H makes more sense if price is your main priority. If this is going in a bedroom, basement, garage, or casual living space, it can still be a good choice, but if this is your main TV, I would try to stretch your budget a bit to the M80H. Compared to Samsung’s higher-end Mini LEDs, like the M80H and QN80H, the M70H is clearly the entry-level option. The M80H is the model I would usually recommend upgrading to because it has a better picture, a better processor, and 144Hz support instead of only a 60Hz panel. Since the M80H is under $1200, the price difference is usually worth it unless the M70H is heavily discounted or you really cannot afford to spend any more. The QN80H is a much better TV again, thanks to its a more refined Quantum Mini LED picture, stronger contrast, and much more premium quality image, but it is also much more expensive. Setup was mostly straightforward, but like the other Samsung TVs, the account and SmartThings process can slow things down if you do not already have everything ready. If you have a Samsung account ready and a Samsung device connected to the WiFi, setup can be fairly quick, but creating a new account without any connected devices can make it take closer to 15-20 minutes. I do like that the 65" and larger sizes has two or more different positions for the feet, which makes it easier to place on a smaller table. Samsung’s Tizen software is responsive and has most of the major streaming apps, but I wish it supported popular VPN apps like you can get on Google TV. That said, if you want to use a VPN, you will need to use one of the supported options or use an external Google TV streaming box. Overall, the M70H is a solid budget Mini LED TV, but I would only go with it if the price difference from the M80H is too steep. It is good for casual viewing and works well as a secondary TV, but the M80H is worth the upgrade for most people because of its better picture quality, 144Hz support, and stronger overall performance. Pros: - Good budget Mini LED TV under $1000. - Bright, colourful, and sharp picture for everyday viewing. - Nice upgrade over older basic LED TVs. - Flexible placement for the legs/feet for the 65"+ models is helpful for smaller TV stands. Cons: - Only has a 60Hz panel, making it worse for gaming and motion. - Cheaper processor and worse overall picture quality than the slightly more expensive M80H. - AI display modes seem to make the picture look washed out. - Samsung account/SmartThings creation can slow down setup if not created ahead of time. - Most popular VPN apps require an external Google TV box.

title: Smooth Upgrade with Impressive Picture & Performance
body: Setup was honestly very easy—plug, connect, and you’re pretty much ready to go. I upgraded from a two-year-old LG QNED, and right away this Samsung feels faster and more refined. The interface is smooth, apps open quickly, and everything just feels responsive without lag. The video quality is where this TV really stands out. The Mini LED panel brings better brightness and more detailed contrast compared to a regular LED, so scenes look more alive and sharp. Colors are vibrant but still natural thanks to Samsung’s Pure Colour Spectrum, and the 4K upscaling does a great job making even older content look clean and crisp. Sound quality is also surprisingly solid. It’s not just loud—it actually adapts to what you’re watching, so dialogue is clear and effects feel more immersive. Features like Object Tracking Sound Lite and adaptive audio tuning help make everything feel more balanced. For gaming and everyday use, it performs really well. Motion handling is smooth, and the Gaming Hub is a nice addition if you’re into cloud gaming or switching between consoles. Overall, it’s a great mix of performance, picture quality, and ease of use. If you’re coming from an older TV like I did, this definitely feels like a proper upgrade—fast, clean, and enjoyable to use every day.

title: Pretty good
body: I own several TV’s including OLED’s, laser projectors, etc. and for me, this is a nice entry level unit that certainly has its place. Usually, I go very in-depth with TV reviews, but for this one I will try to keep it short. Picture During my testing, I found the M70 to have a great picture when it came to sharpness and colour, but the blacks are definitely lacking. Don’t get me wrong, it does a decent job with dark scenes, but when pushed (The Dark Knight, 1917, The Batman, Gravity, etc.), you can definitely see the light bleed and the blacks tend to be a bit grey. However, bright scenes and colours look excellent for the most part (Furiosa was a standout) and regular TV/sports work well. Speaking of sports, even though this maxes at 60hz, I found it handled hockey pretty well and blur was not overly distracting. Sound Sound was decent and certainly great for a bedroom or garage, but it can’t compete with a full surround system or a sound bar like this one (https://www.amazon.ca/dp/B0DQ2T15GJ). Stand/Remote The stand is fine and it is easy to attach the legs, but personally, I prefer a centre/pedestal stand since it gives you more placement options (smaller TV stands for example). The remote is minimalistic, works well as a universal and gets the job done, but it lacks lighting. Overall, this is an excellent TV for a bedroom, garage, or living room where you are not looking for a cinema experience. It has a great overall picture, decent sound, and has a reasonable $998 price tag. However, if you are willing to spend a bit more to get those OLED blacks, the well reviewed entry level LG B5 is currently ~$400 more (https://www.amazon.ca/LG-65-Inch-OLED-Smart-Built/dp/B0F8DMQWM2) and the brighter, higher end C5 is ~$950 more (https://www.amazon.ca/LG-65-Inch-OLED-Smart-Built/dp/B0F7J14C5Q). For me this is a great secondary TV for my bedroom and I am more than happy with the picture/price. As promised, I kept it pretty short and hopefully made your decision a bit easier. Recommended Good luck with your decision/purchase

title: Good Budget Mini LED, But the M80H Is Worth Upgrading to
body: The Samsung M70H is a good budget Mini LED TV for anyone who wants one of Samsung's new 2026 line-up of Mini LED TV while staying under $1000. The picture is bright, colourful, and sharp enough for everyday streaming, and watching TV. It provides a nice upgrade for anyone coming from an older LED TV, while giving you the benefits of Mini LED brightness over basic LED models. That said, this is clearly the more budget-focused option from Samsung’s 2026 Mini LED line-up. The 60Hz panel, cheaper processor, and lower overall picture quality make it less ideal if you are looking to for a premium home theatre TV or a better gaming display. Compared to some of last year’s OLEDs, like the Samsung S90F and LG C5 OLED TVs, the M70H is not really in the same performance category. OLEDs have much better black levels, more precise contrast, and a much more premium picture overall because each pixel can turn off individually. This is especially noticeable in darker scenes or when watching movies at night. However, the M70H is also much cheaper. Since the OLEDs are closer to $2000 and the M70H is under $1000, the M70H makes more sense if price is your main priority. If this is going in a bedroom, basement, garage, or casual living space, it can still be a good choice, but if this is your main TV, I would try to stretch your budget a bit to the M80H. Compared to Samsung’s higher-end Mini LEDs, like the M80H and QN80H, the M70H is clearly the entry-level option. The M80H is the model I would usually recommend upgrading to because it has a better picture, a better processor, and 144Hz support instead of only a 60Hz panel. Since the M80H is under $1200, the price difference is usually worth it unless the M70H is heavily discounted or you really cannot afford to spend any more. The QN80H is a much better TV again, thanks to its a more refined Quantum Mini LED picture, stronger contrast, and much more premium quality image, but it is also much more expensive. Setup was mostly straightforward, but like the other Samsung TVs, the account and SmartThings process can slow things down if you do not already have everything ready. If you have a Samsung account ready and a Samsung device connected to the WiFi, setup can be fairly quick, but creating a new account without any connected devices can make it take closer to 15-20 minutes. I do like that the 65" and larger sizes has two or more different positions for the feet, which makes it easier to place on a smaller table. Samsung’s Tizen software is responsive and has most of the major streaming apps, but I wish it supported popular VPN apps like you can get on Google TV. That said, if you want to use a VPN, you will need to use one of the supported options or use an external Google TV streaming box. Overall, the M70H is a solid budget Mini LED TV, but I would only go with it if the price difference from the M80H is too steep. It is good for casual viewing and works well as a secondary TV, but the M80H is worth the upgrade for most people because of its better picture quality, 144Hz support, and stronger overall performance. Pros: - Good budget Mini LED TV under $1000. - Bright, colourful, and sharp picture for everyday viewing. - Nice upgrade over older basic LED TVs. - Flexible placement for the legs/feet for the 65"+ models is helpful for smaller TV stands. Cons: - Only has a 60Hz panel, making it worse for gaming and motion. - Cheaper processor and worse overall picture quality than the slightly more expensive M80H. - AI display modes seem to make the picture look washed out. - Samsung account/SmartThings creation can slow down setup if not created ahead of time. - Most popular VPN apps require an external Google TV box.

title: Smooth Upgrade with Impressive Picture & Performance
body: Setup was honestly very easy—plug, connect, and you’re pretty much ready to go. I upgraded from a two-year-old LG QNED, and right away this Samsung feels faster and more refined. The interface is smooth, apps open quickly, and everything just feels responsive without lag. The video quality is where this TV really stands out. The Mini LED panel brings better brightness and more detailed contrast compared to a regular LED, so scenes look more alive and sharp. Colors are vibrant but still natural thanks to Samsung’s Pure Colour Spectrum, and the 4K upscaling does a great job making even older content look clean and crisp. Sound quality is also surprisingly solid. It’s not just loud—it actually adapts to what you’re watching, so dialogue is clear and effects feel more immersive. Features like Object Tracking Sound Lite and adaptive audio tuning help make everything feel more balanced. For gaming and everyday use, it performs really well. Motion handling is smooth, and the Gaming Hub is a nice addition if you’re into cloud gaming or switching between consoles. Overall, it’s a great mix of performance, picture quality, and ease of use. If you’re coming from an older TV like I did, this definitely feels like a proper upgrade—fast, clean, and enjoyable to use every day.

title: Pretty good
body: I own several TV’s including OLED’s, laser projectors, etc. and for me, this is a nice entry level unit that certainly has its place. Usually, I go very in-depth with TV reviews, but for this one I will try to keep it short. Picture During my testing, I found the M70 to have a great picture when it came to sharpness and colour, but the blacks are definitely lacking. Don’t get me wrong, it does a decent job with dark scenes, but when pushed (The Dark Knight, 1917, The Batman, Gravity, etc.), you can definitely see the light bleed and the blacks tend to be a bit grey. However, bright scenes and colours look excellent for the most part (Furiosa was a standout) and regular TV/sports work well. Speaking of sports, even though this maxes at 60hz, I found it handled hockey pretty well and blur was not overly distracting. Sound Sound was decent and certainly great for a bedroom or garage, but it can’t compete with a full surround system or a sound bar like this one (https://www.amazon.ca/dp/B0DQ2T15GJ). Stand/Remote The stand is fine and it is easy to attach the legs, but personally, I prefer a centre/pedestal stand since it gives you more placement options (smaller TV stands for example). The remote is minimalistic, works well as a universal and gets the job done, but it lacks lighting. Overall, this is an excellent TV for a bedroom, garage, or living room where you are not looking for a cinema experience. It has a great overall picture, decent sound, and has a reasonable $998 price tag. However, if you are willing to spend a bit more to get those OLED blacks, the well reviewed entry level LG B5 is currently ~$400 more (https://www.amazon.ca/LG-65-Inch-OLED-Smart-Built/dp/B0F8DMQWM2) and the brighter, higher end C5 is ~$950 more (https://www.amazon.ca/LG-65-Inch-OLED-Smart-Built/dp/B0F7J14C5Q). For me this is a great secondary TV for my bedroom and I am more than happy with the picture/price. As promised, I kept it pretty short and hopefully made your decision a bit easier. Recommended Good luck with your decision/purchase

title: I regret my purchase. Image retention after 1 yr.
body:
I now have significant image retention after only a year and a half of use. I follow the exact same viewing habits on my 2017 OLED--which still performs perfectly--so there’s no excuse for this kind of degradation from a flagship LG display. 

My usage has been very light: just 1 to 2 hours of varied news content, 4 to 5 days a week. then 1 to 2 hours/day of varied content the rest of the time. All OLED care settings are turned on and I have never used the TV at max brightness. Pixel cleaning helped slightly but did not solve the problem. This level of performance is completely unacceptable for a premium television in this price range. 

I contacted LG several weeks ago and have received no response. Yes, the picture quality was excellent, until the screen became unusable. But what’s the point of a high-end TV if you’re afraid to use it because the pixels degrade so quickly? Sadly, I regret my purchase.

title: Good image quality, but you will never own your TV
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Pros:
 - Surprisingly good image quality on recorded/saved media playback. 
 - Sound is loud enough to use without a soundbar.
 - There is a toggle to choose no advertisement banners on your home-screen. 

Cons:
 - An LG account is not optional, it is a requirement. To use any Internet connections or apps that connect to the Internet. 
 - TV Remote is cluttered with many unnecessary buttons and feels cheap.
 - AirPlay/Google Cast will not work without an LG account. 

To utilize any Internet functionality you must be connected to LG servers at all times. In other words, this TV does not allow you to use it without creating an LG account. Apps cannot be installed until you create the account and agree to the invasive ToS. Everything you do on your TV gets tracked by them when connected to the Internet.

Apple AirPlay and Google Cast do not work without an LG account. When connected to your own home network you can always cast from your phone or tablet to another device without an Internet connection. This TV strictly forbids casting and will not appear as a usable device. 

For those seeking a TV that only plays recorded media and do not plan to use an LG account, this TV will do the tasks well and it is worth it. Just make sure to never install any updates and have auto-update turned off. Otherwise, you may lose the little remaining functionality. 

Anyone who lives in an area with poor-or-no Internet connection will be disappointed and frustrated when they realize the new TV cannot use Google Cast or Apple AirPlay from their phone or device which is why it is not recommended.

title: Not built to last.
body:
I bought this TV in August 2022 and it met all my expectations at the time.  But now the screen is having issues with ghosting everything I see on Home screen of my Amazon Fire TV Stick 4k Max.  When this problem started a few months ago I hoped it was just a problem with the Firestick, so I bought a new one, but the problem persists.  The ghosting eventually does go away and the picture goes back to looking good.  It's just a shame that the TV couldn't even make it to 3 years without a problem.  The old Toshiba TV that this LG one replaced lasted me 16 years.

This was my first and probably last LG TV.  I had high hopes since I had great luck with LG computer monitors for several decades, but the TV's quality is a dissapointment.

title: Great Visuals and Sound but Steep Learning Curve
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I recently purchased the 75-inch LG QNED 2023 TV from Best Buy, and overall, I’m pleased with the experience. The colors are vibrant, with deep contrasts and natural tones, bringing a truly cinematic feel to movies and shows. The sound quality is equally impressive, with clear audio that fills the room well, even without a soundbar.

However, the remote's mouse function and navigating through all the features come with a steep learning curve. While the interface is feature-rich, it can be a bit overwhelming for new users, and it took me some time to get the hang of it.

Overall, if you're looking for exceptional picture quality and sound, this LG QNED TV is a great choice, but be prepared to spend some time getting used to its controls.

title: Skyworth 40" Google TV is better than I expected
body:
This 40-inch TV has great resolution and is one of the most affordable for its size. It has a  great set of features too. The Skyworth TV has a terrific display with a super-thin design-the frame is only 2.6mm thick and invisible from the side. The panel has a decent contrast ratio. It displays a wide range of colors, and the black levels are also quite good. This makes it suitable for watching in high definition. With the built-in Wi-Fi, and you can connect to the internet wirelessly with access to the internet with many apps and games you can download.
I was particularly impressed with it's connectivity options, including Bluetooth, USB, MHL, and Ethernet. This makes it easy to connect to other devices, like your smartphone or tablet. It also has a pretty solid audio system and it's speakers will produce a decent amount of sound, and they’re designed to fit snugly in your living room.

title: Poor Quality TV - Even Worse Support
body:
After this TV stopped turning on within a short 4 months of use, I was incorrectly directed to the manufacturer for a warranty claim by my local CT store even though it states a 1 year exchange warranty from CT on the website.  I diligently provided Westinghouse with the required info to file my warranty claim.  Now, 4 months after providing that information, I have yet to receive the warranty refund cheque they promised I would get within 45 days.  Numerous calls and hours of wasted time on the phone to Westinghouse gets me nowhere.  Even a corporate customer service case manager from Canadian Tire gets the runaround from Westinghouse when inquiring about my warranty refund on my behalf.

Please don't waste your money on Westinghouse products!  This TV was a great way to throw away hundreds of dollars for me.

I really hope CT reads this review and questions whether on not they want to sell a product that reflects so poorly on them as a retailer.

title: Excellent Value in a QLED TV
body: I recently upgraded to the 2025 Hisense 55QD6QF, and it has completely exceeded my expectations, delivering premium features at an unbelievable price point.  The QLED display truly makes colors pop. Everything I watch are incredibly vibrant and lifelike, far surpassing my previous TV. The blacks are deep, and the brightness is impressive, making viewing comfortable even in a well-lit room.  The integrated Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos support is the heart of the cinematic experience. Movies are breathtakingly detailed with dynamic HDR, and the sound quality is rich and enveloping. It genuinely feels like I have a budget home theater built right into the set.  Finally, the Fire TV operating system is fast and intuitive. Apps load quickly, and the built-in Alexa voice control makes searching for content effortless. The AI 4K Upscaler also deserves praise; it does a surprisingly good job of cleaning up older, lower-resolution content, making almost everything look crisp.

title: Hisense 32QD4SV 32” Hi-QLED Smart TV
body: I purchased the Hisense 32QD4SV 32” Hi-QLED Smart TV for use in our RV, and it has been an excellent choice. The 32-inch size is perfect for smaller spaces while still providing a clear, vibrant picture. The Hi-QLED display delivers impressive colour and image quality, making movies and TV shows look great.  I was also pleasantly surprised by the sound quality. The built-in speakers provide clear, full sound that is more than adequate for an RV or smaller room without needing a separate sound system.  The TV is packed with features, and the VIDAA smart platform is easy to navigate and use. Setup was straightforward, and streaming apps work smoothly.  My only minor complaint is that the mounting screws and spacers needed for attaching a wall mount were not included. It would have been helpful if Hisense had provided these accessories with the TV.  Overall, this is an excellent value for the price, with great picture quality, sound, and features. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a compact smart TV for an RV, bedroom, or smaller living space.

title: Hisense 32QD4SV 32” Hi-QLED Smart TV
body: I purchased the Hisense 32QD4SV 32” Hi-QLED Smart TV for use in our RV, and it has been an excellent choice. The 32-inch size is perfect for smaller spaces while still providing a clear, vibrant picture. The Hi-QLED display delivers impressive colour and image quality, making movies and TV shows look great.  I was also pleasantly surprised by the sound quality. The built-in speakers provide clear, full sound that is more than adequate for an RV or smaller room without needing a separate sound system.  The TV is packed with features, and the VIDAA smart platform is easy to navigate and use. Setup was straightforward, and streaming apps work smoothly.  My only minor complaint is that the mounting screws and spacers needed for attaching a wall mount were not included. It would have been helpful if Hisense had provided these accessories with the TV.  Overall, this is an excellent value for the price, with great picture quality, sound, and features. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a compact smart TV for an RV, bedroom, or smaller living space.

body:

It says it's 4k, but I would question that (although I haven't searched for a 4k signal or movie to test).
When you first start it up, it IS slow to respond with the remote but after a few minutes, it's ok.
If you're planning on connecting a streaming device, the TV would do fine.
All in all, I'd buy another one, but not as a main TV.

body: Overall, the 85" Crystal UHD 4K Smart TV is a good tv. The colour is decent (7.5 out of 10) and the in-tv speakers are impressive.  One criticism is that sometimes the tv will turn itself on within seconds of me turning it off. So when I'm going out for more than a couple of hours, I will unplug the tv. Also -- and this is my main complaint -- the remote the tv comes with needs more buttons like the older-style Samsung remotes have. The remote that came with this tv is terrible. It allows you to switch from Netflix, Prime and YouTube to cable tv or vice versa, but that's all it's really able to do well. Unlike the older remotes, this one has no numbers or Pause/Play/Rewind/Fast Forward buttons. I've attached a photo of the old remote (on the right) and the new remote (on the left). Luckily, the older-style remote will work with this tv.

title: It was great experience
body:
Overall Rating: 7.5/10
What I Like 👍
Sharp 4K picture for Netflix, YouTube, and regular TV.
Good color quality with Samsung's Pure color technology.
Easy-to-use Tizen smart TV system with apps like Netflix, Disney+, Prime Video, and YouTube.
Supports HDR10+ and 4K upscaling for older content.
Slim, modern design that looks nice in a bedroom or living room. 
Samsung
What I Don't Like 
Only a 60Hz panel, so it is not great for competitive gaming.
Brightness is fairly low, making it less impressive in very sunny rooms.
No local dimming, so black levels and HDR performance are average.
Only 2 HDMI ports, which can be limiting if you have a game console, soundbar, and streaming device.
Viewing angles are narrow; the picture looks best when viewed straight on. 
RTINGS.com +2
Who Should Buy It?
People who want an affordable Samsung 4K TV for movies, streaming, and everyday use.
Who Should Skip It?
 Gamers wanting 120Hz gaming.
People looking for strong HDR performance or a premium home-theater experience.
 Bright-room viewers who need a very bright screen. 
RTINGS.com +1
Final Verdict
If you can find the 43" U7900F on sale, it's a solid budget TV from Samsung. The picture is good for the price, the smart features are excellent, and it works well for casual viewing. However, if your budget allows, stepping up to a better QLED model from Samsung, TCL, or Hisense will give noticeably better brightness and HDR performance.

title: Amazing TV, Remote Been to War, Came Back Laughing
body:
My family and I have bought our 2nd Samsung TV and am still nothing but impressed with how great brand is.

Our 1st TV is still banging along, we just wanted to go a bit bigger.

The colours are sharp, the sound is great, and to be 100% honest, the TV makes family movie time just that much better.

Amazingly, the 1st TV remote was one reason we chose to stick with Samsung.

The remote you say? YES!

My family and I had done everything we could to completely obliterate this remote, mostly by accident.

It was dropped, chucked, spilled on, and so on.

Everytime, it popped open and the batteries flew out, we would piece it back together and it worked fine!

If a company can put together a unit that can stand the everyday abuse of a rowdy family, the TVs? Those things will probably survive getting run over by a bus!

I love both our TV's and am a Samsung customer for life.

title: Bluetooth stopped working after a month
body: Bought this about a month ago, had the tv connected to my Bluetooth speaker but the Bluetooth stopped working. Thi was quite surprised to find out the TV does not have an optic cable port for audio. I thought it would be standard since my previous TV that was a decade old had the optic port. Also disappointed that it only had two HDMI ports. I can use an hdmi splitter of course, but that changes the quality a bit I find. Given the sale price I’m satisfied with the purchase but I might not buy this product again

title: Excellent Picture Quality for a 70 inch 4K TV
body:
I’ve been using the Samsung 70” U7900 Crystal UHD TV for a little while now and I’m honestly really impressed with it for the price. The picture quality is sharp, bright, and the 4K upscaling makes even older shows and sports look much better than expected. Colours look natural and HDR content really stands out, especially when watching movies at night.

The size is perfect for a living room setup and the slim metal design gives it a much more premium look than I expected. Setup was quick and easy, and the Tizen smart system runs smoothly with Netflix, YouTube, Disney+, and everything else I use daily. Overall, this TV feels like an excellent value if you want a big 70-inch 4K smart TV without spending a fortune. Definitely happy with the purchase so far.

title: Awesome Upgrade to 'Movie Theatre" experience!
body: It is hard to believe that we finally upgraded from our 43" SAMSUNG Plasma TV from the old days to this awesome 65" Samsung smart TV. Such a great choice as we were considering a 55" at first but glad we went with the 65". Having a young child in the family we take advantage of the Kareoke and games, everything is so sharp and clear and we love the interactive interface. We love that we can navigate the TV from our phone, no more Google Chrome that is consistently inconsistent. We love the variety of shows and movies on Samsung Plus and how easy it was to sign in to all of our Media streaming platforms.  The color is perfect and can be adjusted depending on what we are watching. The brightness is also good and can be adjusted based on our preferences. Of course going from an old small Plasma TV to this giant "movie theatre" style screen had been an adjustment, but a very positive one, when taking into account the resolution and how crisp everything is. Overall we are very satisfied with this awesome immersive experience and how easy it was to set everything up when we first turned on the TV.

When I got it home and unpacked it, I discovered it had no optical cable port and could not connect to my Bose soundbar. I’m faced with either purchasing a HDMI/Optical cable converter (which may have less than optimal performance) or purchasing a different soundbar. I am not impressed.

title: Great tv—but no Magic Remote is a serious issue.
body:
Just bought this tv yesterday and it is, in fact, fantastic. However, as others have pointed out, there's no Magic Remote. I'm not just disappointed, I'm actually concerned that this borders on misleading advertising: ALL the marketing material focuses on AI functions WITH the Magic Remote. Unlike added functionalities available with an LG soundbar, there is no asterisk warning that the remote isn't included on the model I purchased (65in). The standard remote is listed in the specs, but that's far too easy to miss when you've just been bombarded by images of the Magic Remote as a main selling point. 

So, I now own a television that effectively locks me out of most of its touted, standout features. For me (and others who bought this tv based on ad copy), all the promotional videos on this page, and on the store's web page where I made the purchase, are simply not true. In fact, I can't even find this remote model listed anywhere. I read the reply about the Magic Remote being available to "further enhance" the experience but, with all due respect, that's not how you present it. At all. The promotional material even says "your Magic Remote" not "a Magic Remote". That doesn't sound like an add-on.

As I said: the UA77 is a wonderful television. It really is. I would've given it 4 stars, easily. But I'm just profoundly disappointed with LG. This isn't right.

title: great picture, terrible user interface
body:
Two stars only because the clarity is very good.  The TV picture is great.  However, the user interface running the device is terrible.  It barely responds to the remote control.  Instead of a button in the center of the directional arrows, there is a scroll wheel.  But the scroll wheel does not do what you expect it to do, instead of moving from icon to icon, it activates a remote pointer mouse.  Well the pointer mouses accuracy is horrendous.  It jumps all over the screen, it clicks where you don't want it to, and doesn't click where you want it to.

My recommendation for you before buying any television is to get the remote from sales and operate the tv, not just watch the high-resolution picture on display.  This tv is very difficult to navigate. And there is no place to disable this annoying feature. 

Also, do not be fooled by the AI tag, this is NOT AI.  The help feature they call chatbot, does not give prompts, it is merely a pre-defined set of questions and answers.  Maybe they have some AI running in the background recording all you do so it can present content you are interested in, but even that is NOT AI, but simply maching learning and recording. 

don't be fooled, get the remote from sales, operate the TV.  Make sure you are good with how this works.

Also, the chromecast and apple air play barely work.  I was finally able to use them both, but it seems to hang on to the connection after disconnection, so a second user cannot also cast via apple.  The response time is slow and laggy when it finally does connect.

It’s also been great for sports, especially watching games like the NBA Finals. The 65 inch size gives it that theater feel without being too much for a living room, and the viewing angles are really nice too. Even from the side, the picture still looks great. Also setting all picture modes to +20 cold and color saturation to 60 is made everything look neon and the AI settings mode used tiny blurry images.  The sound AI audio clips where so compressed and muddy that through the terrible built in speakers I just got a headache.  Guys, please offer a better range of picture presets so we can have a good out of the box experience.  Please fix the software updates.  Please fix the mute button fiasco. title: Don’t Buy!
body: This TV was a nightmare. The remote is almost impossible to use. It has a cursor that you must point at the TV to click on apps like an old school laser pointer. It’s truly an infuriating interface. There are no play, pause, fast forward or mute buttons. When we googled how to use the remote LG suggested downloading an app to teach us how to use the remote. You shouldn’t need a class to use a remote. That’s a wild choice by LG. The remote is technically replaceable but you have to make a second purchase. The ultimate reason we decided to return this TV was because every SINGLE time we turned it on it wouldn’t connect to WiFi without first “forgetting” our network and then reconnecting. What’s the use of a nice screen quality if it’s such a pain to simply use the TV.

I use an app that works fine on my Firestick but throws an error when running natively on the TV, so I've had to plug my Firestick into the TV's HDMI just to work around it. title: Hisense 75-Inch 4K TV Review
body: I have been using the Hisense 75-inch 4K TV for a few weeks now, and it has been an outstanding upgrade for my living room. The picture quality is sharp and vibrant, especially in 4K HDR content — colors pop without looking oversaturated, and dark scenes hold up surprisingly well thanks to its strong contrast and local dimming.  The size alone makes a huge difference for movies and sports. It delivers a true theater-like experience, and the wide viewing angles make it great for gatherings. The sound quality is decent for built-in speakers — clear dialogue and a bit of bass — though I paired it with a soundbar for more immersion.  Hisense’s smart TV interface is easy to navigate. Apps like Netflix, Prime Video, and YouTube load quickly, and it supports both Alexa and Google Assistant. Connectivity has been rock solid through Wi-Fi and HDMI (it includes multiple HDMI 2.1 ports, perfect for gaming).  If you want a massive, high-quality TV without paying premium-brand prices, the Hisense 75-inch is hard to beat. It delivers excellent performance, simple setup, and a feature set that rivals more expensive models.

title: Hisense 75-Inch 4K TV Review
body: I have been using the Hisense 75-inch 4K TV for a few weeks now, and it has been an outstanding upgrade for my living room. The picture quality is sharp and vibrant, especially in 4K HDR content — colors pop without looking oversaturated, and dark scenes hold up surprisingly well thanks to its strong contrast and local dimming.  The size alone makes a huge difference for movies and sports. It delivers a true theater-like experience, and the wide viewing angles make it great for gatherings. The sound quality is decent for built-in speakers — clear dialogue and a bit of bass — though I paired it with a soundbar for more immersion.  Hisense’s smart TV interface is easy to navigate. Apps like Netflix, Prime Video, and YouTube load quickly, and it supports both Alexa and Google Assistant. Connectivity has been rock solid through Wi-Fi and HDMI (it includes multiple HDMI 2.1 ports, perfect for gaming).  If you want a massive, high-quality TV without paying premium-brand prices, the Hisense 75-inch is hard to beat. It delivers excellent performance, simple setup, and a feature set that rivals more expensive models.

title: Perfect Choice for a Sunny Room
body: I was excited to find this TV on sale at a local store, and I have not been disappointed. The QLED display is perfect for our extra sunny living room. Where OLED displays might refract and reflect light, this one just stops it in its tracks! I'll show one of our windows in the photo I'm including. This is a vast improvement over our old TV! I'm still getting used to some of the settings, and I'll need to upgrade my HDMI cables to get the most out of my game consoles, but I am super pleased so far. I was able to hook up the TV to my soundbar with no problem using HDMI eARC, though the sound from the TV itself is really nice. I might not even need the soundbar anymore. My one wishlist item would be an easier way to switch the display to a night-specific setting. I found it way too bright in the evening, when the room's lights were low. After fiddling with all kinds of picture settings and turning off the auto light sensor, I found a comfortable enough spot. I figured out that if I make my changes in one picture mode (like Standard), the TV will remember my settings. That means I can switch back to Game or FilmMaker mode during the day, then switch to Standard at night. That should do the trick! On a related note, the settings change really slowly, which is weird. It doesn't matter if I press the remote buttons repeatedly or just hold them down. Maybe there's a way to do this with an app? Overall, though, I'm still really happy with this choice.

Gaming performance is a standout thanks to a 165Hz panel, VRR, ALLM, and very low input lag. title: My DREAM TV Upgrade for 2026!!! 📺
body:
I’ve been looking for a new premium TV to upgrade my living room for the new year, and I didn’t want to spend an arm and a leg for one so I got the 65” Hisense U88QG, which is one of the top premium MiniLED options on the market!

Now the first thing I noticed using this new TV was the crazy 5000 nits of peak brightness which means it gets plenty bright for daytime watching, not to mention having an anti-reflective coating so it still looks good from the side for when you have friends over! It’s also a MiniLED panel that uses quantum dots which if you don’t know what that is, basically means you get some really rich vibrant colours, that are actually accurate too so your favourite movies don’t look washed out! But as much as you might wanna binge watch, gaming is an epic experience too thanks to the 165hz refresh rate that actually supports AMD Freesync so everything feels smooth! There are even built-in top firing speakers with subwoofers in the back for Dolby Atmos surround sound which actually sounds shockingly good and cool, but not as cool as the built-in USB-C DisplayPort so I can easily plug my laptop in to use with the TV, or even a full on gaming PC if you wanna game on the TV!

Genuinely so happy with this TV upgrade and if you want something real nice for your living room this year, this is the one guys! Special shoutout and thanks to Hisense Canada for sending this TV over! 😊
