title: 85Inch TV 85U88QG
body: I upgraded to the 85” Hisense U88QG after owning an OLED for a long time, and I was honestly nervous about losing those perfect blacks.  I can confidently say: I was surprised in the best possible way.  The black levels on this TV are outstanding for an LED. Local dimming is very aggressive, blooming is minimal, and in real content the contrast looks fantastic. In many scenes I simply stop thinking about the technology and just enjoy the image.  Where this TV really shocked me is brightness. HDR highlights, reflections, explosions, daylight scenes — they have an intensity my OLED simply could not reach. It makes movies and games feel incredibly dynamic.  Gaming is excellent. The Game Bar gives you real information, VRR works perfectly, motion is super smooth, and input lag feels very low. Playing on an 85” screen completely changes immersion.  Google TV runs fast, apps load quickly, and the overall experience feels premium.  Sound is also much better than I expected from built-in speakers.  Is OLED still king in a fully dark room for absolute black? Yes. But this TV fights back with size, brightness, and impact — and it does it very, very well.  For anyone afraid of moving from OLED to high-end Mini-LED: don’t be. This set delivers.  Highly recommended.

title: Hisense 32QD4SV 32” Hi-QLED Smart TV
body: I purchased the Hisense 32QD4SV 32” Hi-QLED Smart TV for use in our RV, and it has been an excellent choice. The 32-inch size is perfect for smaller spaces while still providing a clear, vibrant picture. The Hi-QLED display delivers impressive colour and image quality, making movies and TV shows look great.  I was also pleasantly surprised by the sound quality. The built-in speakers provide clear, full sound that is more than adequate for an RV or smaller room without needing a separate sound system.  The TV is packed with features, and the VIDAA smart platform is easy to navigate and use. Setup was straightforward, and streaming apps work smoothly.  My only minor complaint is that the mounting screws and spacers needed for attaching a wall mount were not included. It would have been helpful if Hisense had provided these accessories with the TV.  Overall, this is an excellent value for the price, with great picture quality, sound, and features. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a compact smart TV for an RV, bedroom, or smaller living space.

title: Hisense 75-Inch 4K TV Review
body: I have been using the Hisense 75-inch 4K TV for a few weeks now, and it has been an outstanding upgrade for my living room. The picture quality is sharp and vibrant, especially in 4K HDR content — colors pop without looking oversaturated, and dark scenes hold up surprisingly well thanks to its strong contrast and local dimming.  The size alone makes a huge difference for movies and sports. It delivers a true theater-like experience, and the wide viewing angles make it great for gatherings. The sound quality is decent for built-in speakers — clear dialogue and a bit of bass — though I paired it with a soundbar for more immersion.  Hisense’s smart TV interface is easy to navigate. Apps like Netflix, Prime Video, and YouTube load quickly, and it supports both Alexa and Google Assistant. Connectivity has been rock solid through Wi-Fi and HDMI (it includes multiple HDMI 2.1 ports, perfect for gaming).  If you want a massive, high-quality TV without paying premium-brand prices, the Hisense 75-inch is hard to beat. It delivers excellent performance, simple setup, and a feature set that rivals more expensive models.

I'm excited to spend more time with it and see everything it can do. One of my favorite things about this TV is the overall design. The Gallery style look feels much more intentional than a traditional TV, and it blends into the room nicely. I tried the included snow white magnetic frame, but I actually preferred the look without it. For my space, I think one of the wood-look frame options would complement the room better. 
The picture quality is a huge upgrade from my old TV. Everything I've watched so far has looked incredibly sharp and clear. Colors appear vibrant, details are easy to see, and the matte display does a great job reducing glare from nearby windows and lighting. 
The sound has also impressed me. I wasn't expecting much from built-in TV speakers, but audio has been clear and full enough that I haven't felt the need to connect external speakers right away. 
Another feature I've really enjoyed is the AI Magic Remote. Being able to point at the screen and click where you want to go feels much more intuitive than repeatedly pressing navigation buttons. It makes browsing apps and menus quick and easy.

title: Beautiful Art Frame TV Held Back by Software
body:
I had been waiting for months for this TV to finally become available and was excited to see it finally available for purchase. The mini-LED display is superior to any other artwork TV I've seen. The matte display really is impressive and there is practically no glare. The artwork looks great and it works wonderfully as a TV as well.

I was hoping there would be more than one frame option, but I guess maybe these will come with time. It's easy enough to install the magnetic frame, so changing it later won't be a problem. The included white frame looks okay, just very basic.

There are a few things that are a little frustrating though. Firstly, I bought this mainly to display artwork, but the TV automatically shuts off after an hour. To find the timer, you have to press the center wheel button while the artwork is actively running, navigate to a hidden three-dots "Options" menu, and change the power-off timer. Unfortunately, the firmware limits you to a maximum of 1 hour with no option to disable the timer entirely. For a dedicated art TV, not having a true "always-on" mode is highly frustrating. What I would like to see is the ability to create a schedule for artwork to be displayed. 

Additionally, it's really annoying that the gallery-mode screensaver is only available with a membership. Such a basic feature should not require additional fees when it's already a premium model TV.  It's not possible to disable the screensaver. I would much rather the TV just automatically enter always-ready mode instead of activating the screensaver. 

The included flush-mount bracket is not particularly easy to use. It takes a lot of attempts to find the bracket while it's hidden behind the TV. We found it worked best to have three people to hang it; one on each end of the TV and the third to help guide us to where they bracket should be. Once up, it does look nice, but now we need to repaint where we scratched up the wall during the hanging process.

There isn't much room behind the TV for cable management. Just two tiny pockets in the back of the TV. This makes it frustratingly difficult to try to hide the cables and get the TV sitting flat against the wall. It would be nice if you could tilt the TV away from the wall to access the cables to tidy it up. The power cord is on the opposite side of the TV as the input jacks, which means it is likely necessary to have two holes in the wall behind the TV. 

The WebOS is very sluggish and, once I disabled the ads, there is about 75% of the home page that is unused. It would be great to be able to use the entire 65" display rather that scrolling a single horizontal line of apps. Fortunately, the home page is used infrequently.

Overall, I am quite happy with how the TV looks on the wall; the matte display and the mini-LED panel are genuinely stunning and make the artwork look incredibly realistic. However, the clunky software, lack of a true "always-on" art mode, and frustrating mounting process hold a premium television back from being perfect. If you are willing to deal with a few software quirks and a tedious installation, the end result looks beautiful in the room.

title: Hisense 75-Inch 4K TV Review
body: I have been using the Hisense 75-inch 4K TV for a few weeks now, and it has been an outstanding upgrade for my living room. The picture quality is sharp and vibrant, especially in 4K HDR content — colors pop without looking oversaturated, and dark scenes hold up surprisingly well thanks to its strong contrast and local dimming.  The size alone makes a huge difference for movies and sports. It delivers a true theater-like experience, and the wide viewing angles make it great for gatherings. The sound quality is decent for built-in speakers — clear dialogue and a bit of bass — though I paired it with a soundbar for more immersion.  Hisense’s smart TV interface is easy to navigate. Apps like Netflix, Prime Video, and YouTube load quickly, and it supports both Alexa and Google Assistant. Connectivity has been rock solid through Wi-Fi and HDMI (it includes multiple HDMI 2.1 ports, perfect for gaming).  If you want a massive, high-quality TV without paying premium-brand prices, the Hisense 75-inch is hard to beat. It delivers excellent performance, simple setup, and a feature set that rivals more expensive models.

title: Perfect Choice for a Sunny Room
body: I was excited to find this TV on sale at a local store, and I have not been disappointed. The QLED display is perfect for our extra sunny living room. Where OLED displays might refract and reflect light, this one just stops it in its tracks! I'll show one of our windows in the photo I'm including. This is a vast improvement over our old TV! I'm still getting used to some of the settings, and I'll need to upgrade my HDMI cables to get the most out of my game consoles, but I am super pleased so far. I was able to hook up the TV to my soundbar with no problem using HDMI eARC, though the sound from the TV itself is really nice. I might not even need the soundbar anymore. My one wishlist item would be an easier way to switch the display to a night-specific setting. I found it way too bright in the evening, when the room's lights were low. After fiddling with all kinds of picture settings and turning off the auto light sensor, I found a comfortable enough spot. I figured out that if I make my changes in one picture mode (like Standard), the TV will remember my settings. That means I can switch back to Game or FilmMaker mode during the day, then switch to Standard at night. That should do the trick! On a related note, the settings change really slowly, which is weird. It doesn't matter if I press the remote buttons repeatedly or just hold them down. Maybe there's a way to do this with an app? Overall, though, I'm still really happy with this choice.

title: Best tv in price range
body: The Hisense 55U78QG is one of the best value 55-inch TVs in its class. Gaming performance is a standout thanks to a 165Hz panel, VRR, ALLM, and very low input lag. I tried the included snow white magnetic frame, but I actually preferred the look without it. For my space, I think one of the wood-look frame options would complement the room better. 
The picture quality is a huge upgrade from my old TV. Everything I've watched so far has looked incredibly sharp and clear. Colors appear vibrant, details are easy to see, and the matte display does a great job reducing glare from nearby windows and lighting. 
The sound has also impressed me. I wasn't expecting much from built-in TV speakers, but audio has been clear and full enough that I haven't felt the need to connect external speakers right away. 
Another feature I've really enjoyed is the AI Magic Remote. Being able to point at the screen and click where you want to go feels much more intuitive than repeatedly pressing navigation buttons. It makes browsing apps and menus quick and easy.

title: Beautiful Art Frame TV Held Back by Software
body:
I had been waiting for months for this TV to finally become available and was excited to see it finally available for purchase. The mini-LED display is superior to any other artwork TV I've seen. The matte display really is impressive and there is practically no glare. The artwork looks great and it works wonderfully as a TV as well.

I was hoping there would be more than one frame option, but I guess maybe these will come with time. It's easy enough to install the magnetic frame, so changing it later won't be a problem. The included white frame looks okay, just very basic.

There are a few things that are a little frustrating though. Firstly, I bought this mainly to display artwork, but the TV automatically shuts off after an hour. To find the timer, you have to press the center wheel button while the artwork is actively running, navigate to a hidden three-dots "Options" menu, and change the power-off timer. Unfortunately, the firmware limits you to a maximum of 1 hour with no option to disable the timer entirely. For a dedicated art TV, not having a true "always-on" mode is highly frustrating. What I would like to see is the ability to create a schedule for artwork to be displayed. 

Additionally, it's really annoying that the gallery-mode screensaver is only available with a membership. Such a basic feature should not require additional fees when it's already a premium model TV.  It's not possible to disable the screensaver. I would much rather the TV just automatically enter always-ready mode instead of activating the screensaver. 

The included flush-mount bracket is not particularly easy to use. It takes a lot of attempts to find the bracket while it's hidden behind the TV. We found it worked best to have three people to hang it; one on each end of the TV and the third to help guide us to where they bracket should be. Once up, it does look nice, but now we need to repaint where we scratched up the wall during the hanging process.

There isn't much room behind the TV for cable management. Just two tiny pockets in the back of the TV. This makes it frustratingly difficult to try to hide the cables and get the TV sitting flat against the wall. It would be nice if you could tilt the TV away from the wall to access the cables to tidy it up. The power cord is on the opposite side of the TV as the input jacks, which means it is likely necessary to have two holes in the wall behind the TV. 

The WebOS is very sluggish and, once I disabled the ads, there is about 75% of the home page that is unused. It would be great to be able to use the entire 65" display rather that scrolling a single horizontal line of apps. Fortunately, the home page is used infrequently.

Overall, I am quite happy with how the TV looks on the wall; the matte display and the mini-LED panel are genuinely stunning and make the artwork look incredibly realistic. However, the clunky software, lack of a true "always-on" art mode, and frustrating mounting process hold a premium television back from being perfect. If you are willing to deal with a few software quirks and a tedious installation, the end result looks beautiful in the room.

title: Hisense 75-Inch 4K TV Review
body: I have been using the Hisense 75-inch 4K TV for a few weeks now, and it has been an outstanding upgrade for my living room. The picture quality is sharp and vibrant, especially in 4K HDR content — colors pop without looking oversaturated, and dark scenes hold up surprisingly well thanks to its strong contrast and local dimming.  The size alone makes a huge difference for movies and sports. It delivers a true theater-like experience, and the wide viewing angles make it great for gatherings. The sound quality is decent for built-in speakers — clear dialogue and a bit of bass — though I paired it with a soundbar for more immersion.  Hisense’s smart TV interface is easy to navigate. Apps like Netflix, Prime Video, and YouTube load quickly, and it supports both Alexa and Google Assistant. Connectivity has been rock solid through Wi-Fi and HDMI (it includes multiple HDMI 2.1 ports, perfect for gaming).  If you want a massive, high-quality TV without paying premium-brand prices, the Hisense 75-inch is hard to beat. It delivers excellent performance, simple setup, and a feature set that rivals more expensive models.

title: Perfect Choice for a Sunny Room
body: I was excited to find this TV on sale at a local store, and I have not been disappointed. The QLED display is perfect for our extra sunny living room. Where OLED displays might refract and reflect light, this one just stops it in its tracks! I'll show one of our windows in the photo I'm including. This is a vast improvement over our old TV! I'm still getting used to some of the settings, and I'll need to upgrade my HDMI cables to get the most out of my game consoles, but I am super pleased so far. I was able to hook up the TV to my soundbar with no problem using HDMI eARC, though the sound from the TV itself is really nice. I might not even need the soundbar anymore. My one wishlist item would be an easier way to switch the display to a night-specific setting. I found it way too bright in the evening, when the room's lights were low. After fiddling with all kinds of picture settings and turning off the auto light sensor, I found a comfortable enough spot. I figured out that if I make my changes in one picture mode (like Standard), the TV will remember my settings. That means I can switch back to Game or FilmMaker mode during the day, then switch to Standard at night. That should do the trick! On a related note, the settings change really slowly, which is weird. It doesn't matter if I press the remote buttons repeatedly or just hold them down. Maybe there's a way to do this with an app? Overall, though, I'm still really happy with this choice.

Gaming performance is a standout thanks to a 165Hz panel, VRR, ALLM, and very low input lag. body: Overall I'm happy with the Hisense 85QD7QFM. The picture quality is excellent for the price, the sound is solid, and at this size it offers great value for money. That said, there are two issues worth knowing about. The power button on the remote does not work at all, meaning you can't turn the TV on or off with it. The bigger issue is app compatibility. I use an app that works fine on my Firestick but throws an error when running natively on the TV, so I've had to plug my Firestick into the TV's HDMI just to work around it. Neither issue is a dealbreaker, but they're the kind of things that shouldn't be a problem on a new TV. Hopefully a firmware update addresses them down the road.

title: Hisense 75-Inch 4K TV Review
body: I have been using the Hisense 75-inch 4K TV for a few weeks now, and it has been an outstanding upgrade for my living room. The picture quality is sharp and vibrant, especially in 4K HDR content — colors pop without looking oversaturated, and dark scenes hold up surprisingly well thanks to its strong contrast and local dimming.  The size alone makes a huge difference for movies and sports. It delivers a true theater-like experience, and the wide viewing angles make it great for gatherings. The sound quality is decent for built-in speakers — clear dialogue and a bit of bass — though I paired it with a soundbar for more immersion.  Hisense’s smart TV interface is easy to navigate. Apps like Netflix, Prime Video, and YouTube load quickly, and it supports both Alexa and Google Assistant. Connectivity has been rock solid through Wi-Fi and HDMI (it includes multiple HDMI 2.1 ports, perfect for gaming).  If you want a massive, high-quality TV without paying premium-brand prices, the Hisense 75-inch is hard to beat. It delivers excellent performance, simple setup, and a feature set that rivals more expensive models.

title: Perfect Choice for a Sunny Room
body: I was excited to find this TV on sale at a local store, and I have not been disappointed. The QLED display is perfect for our extra sunny living room. Where OLED displays might refract and reflect light, this one just stops it in its tracks! I'll show one of our windows in the photo I'm including. This is a vast improvement over our old TV! I'm still getting used to some of the settings, and I'll need to upgrade my HDMI cables to get the most out of my game consoles, but I am super pleased so far. I was able to hook up the TV to my soundbar with no problem using HDMI eARC, though the sound from the TV itself is really nice. I might not even need the soundbar anymore. My one wishlist item would be an easier way to switch the display to a night-specific setting. I found it way too bright in the evening, when the room's lights were low. After fiddling with all kinds of picture settings and turning off the auto light sensor, I found a comfortable enough spot. I figured out that if I make my changes in one picture mode (like Standard), the TV will remember my settings. That means I can switch back to Game or FilmMaker mode during the day, then switch to Standard at night. That should do the trick! On a related note, the settings change really slowly, which is weird. It doesn't matter if I press the remote buttons repeatedly or just hold them down. Maybe there's a way to do this with an app? Overall, though, I'm still really happy with this choice.

title: My DREAM TV Upgrade for 2026!!! 📺
body:
I’ve been looking for a new premium TV to upgrade my living room for the new year, and I didn’t want to spend an arm and a leg for one so I got the 65” Hisense U88QG, which is one of the top premium MiniLED options on the market!

Now the first thing I noticed using this new TV was the crazy 5000 nits of peak brightness which means it gets plenty bright for daytime watching, not to mention having an anti-reflective coating so it still looks good from the side for when you have friends over! It’s also a MiniLED panel that uses quantum dots which if you don’t know what that is, basically means you get some really rich vibrant colours, that are actually accurate too so your favourite movies don’t look washed out! But as much as you might wanna binge watch, gaming is an epic experience too thanks to the 165hz refresh rate that actually supports AMD Freesync so everything feels smooth! There are even built-in top firing speakers with subwoofers in the back for Dolby Atmos surround sound which actually sounds shockingly good and cool, but not as cool as the built-in USB-C DisplayPort so I can easily plug my laptop in to use with the TV, or even a full on gaming PC if you wanna game on the TV!

Genuinely so happy with this TV upgrade and if you want something real nice for your living room this year, this is the one guys! Special shoutout and thanks to Hisense Canada for sending this TV over! 😊

title: 85Inch TV 85U88QG
body: I upgraded to the 85” Hisense U88QG after owning an OLED for a long time, and I was honestly nervous about losing those perfect blacks.  I can confidently say: I was surprised in the best possible way.  The black levels on this TV are outstanding for an LED. Local dimming is very aggressive, blooming is minimal, and in real content the contrast looks fantastic. In many scenes I simply stop thinking about the technology and just enjoy the image.  Where this TV really shocked me is brightness. HDR highlights, reflections, explosions, daylight scenes — they have an intensity my OLED simply could not reach. It makes movies and games feel incredibly dynamic.  Gaming is excellent. The Game Bar gives you real information, VRR works perfectly, motion is super smooth, and input lag feels very low. Playing on an 85” screen completely changes immersion.  Google TV runs fast, apps load quickly, and the overall experience feels premium.  Sound is also much better than I expected from built-in speakers.  Is OLED still king in a fully dark room for absolute black? Yes. But this TV fights back with size, brightness, and impact — and it does it very, very well.  For anyone afraid of moving from OLED to high-end Mini-LED: don’t be. This set delivers.  Highly recommended.

title: Hisense 75-Inch 4K TV Review
body: I have been using the Hisense 75-inch 4K TV for a few weeks now, and it has been an outstanding upgrade for my living room. The picture quality is sharp and vibrant, especially in 4K HDR content — colors pop without looking oversaturated, and dark scenes hold up surprisingly well thanks to its strong contrast and local dimming.  The size alone makes a huge difference for movies and sports. It delivers a true theater-like experience, and the wide viewing angles make it great for gatherings. The sound quality is decent for built-in speakers — clear dialogue and a bit of bass — though I paired it with a soundbar for more immersion.  Hisense’s smart TV interface is easy to navigate. Apps like Netflix, Prime Video, and YouTube load quickly, and it supports both Alexa and Google Assistant. Connectivity has been rock solid through Wi-Fi and HDMI (it includes multiple HDMI 2.1 ports, perfect for gaming).  If you want a massive, high-quality TV without paying premium-brand prices, the Hisense 75-inch is hard to beat. It delivers excellent performance, simple setup, and a feature set that rivals more expensive models.

title: Perfect Choice for a Sunny Room
body: I was excited to find this TV on sale at a local store, and I have not been disappointed. The QLED display is perfect for our extra sunny living room. Where OLED displays might refract and reflect light, this one just stops it in its tracks! I'll show one of our windows in the photo I'm including. This is a vast improvement over our old TV! I'm still getting used to some of the settings, and I'll need to upgrade my HDMI cables to get the most out of my game consoles, but I am super pleased so far. I was able to hook up the TV to my soundbar with no problem using HDMI eARC, though the sound from the TV itself is really nice. I might not even need the soundbar anymore. My one wishlist item would be an easier way to switch the display to a night-specific setting. I found it way too bright in the evening, when the room's lights were low. After fiddling with all kinds of picture settings and turning off the auto light sensor, I found a comfortable enough spot. I figured out that if I make my changes in one picture mode (like Standard), the TV will remember my settings. That means I can switch back to Game or FilmMaker mode during the day, then switch to Standard at night. That should do the trick! On a related note, the settings change really slowly, which is weird. It doesn't matter if I press the remote buttons repeatedly or just hold them down. Maybe there's a way to do this with an app? Overall, though, I'm still really happy with this choice.

title: OS is slow
body:
I’ve had this TV for three days, and my main issue is its slow performance. Almost every button press has a noticeable delay, with the settings menu being the worst—it takes quite a while to open and navigate.

Other than that, there are several positives. WOW Orchestra works very well, and the sound integration is impressive. The picture quality is decent; the colours are good, although they aren’t quite as vibrant as I was hoping for. Brightness is strong and handles a sunlit room without any problems.

One thing that really stood out is the casting feature. It works smoothly and reliably, making it easy to stream content from other devices.

Overall, it’s a solid TV with good brightness, sound, and casting capabilities, but the sluggish interface prevents it from feeling as premium as it could.

Navigating through the built-in Google TV interface is snappy and makes finding our streaming apps a breeze If you have the wall space and are considering making the jump to a massive screen, this Hisense model offers incredible value and premium performance without breaking the bank compared to other brands. title: Review of the TV
body: The Hisense TV offers great value for its price, making it a strong option for anyone looking for a budget-friendly smart TV. The picture quality is impressive, especially on the 4K models, with bright colours and sharp details. Many Hisense TVs also support Dolby Vision and HDR10, which helps improve contrast and overall viewing experience.  The built-in smart features—like Google TV or Roku TV depending on the model—are easy to use and give access to popular apps such as Netflix, YouTube, Disney+, and more. The remote is straightforward, and the interface runs smoothly for everyday use.  Sound quality is decent for regular watching, though some users might prefer adding a soundbar for a better audio experience. Build quality is good for the price, though not as premium as higher-end brands like Samsung or LG.  Overall, Hisense provides excellent performance for the cost and is a reliable choice for movies, sports, and daily streaming.

One thing that has me a bit concerned is the TV started to possibly clitch. What I mean is the screen will cut off to a black screen, then come back on but with the sound gone. Desn't matter if it's set to Optical which uses my soundbar, or set to use the TV speakers. Oddly just turning it off/on seems to get the sound back. I did a restart and it still did the same thing. Now this doesn't happen constantly, but did happen enough yesterday to make it quite annoying. Today though, so far no issues so I really can't say if it's an issue with the TV or not. Only thing I can do is see if it continues in the future, and hope if it is a defect that it happens within the 1yr warrenty. Besides any of that I am overall very pleased with my choice to purchase this item

title: Fantastic value for high quality picture
body: The Hisense QD6 55-Inch TV is an impressive mid-range option that delivers excellent picture quality at an affordable price. Featuring Quantum Dot technology, it offers vibrant colors and sharp contrasts that make movies and shows come to life. The 4K resolution ensures crisp visuals, while its HDR capabilities (HDR10, HLG, and Dolby Vision) add depth to both bright and dark scenes.  The TV runs on the Google TV platform, which provides a smooth and intuitive interface for navigating apps like Netflix, YouTube, and Disney+. Voice control with Google Assistant is a handy feature, and the inclusion of built-in Chromecast makes it easy to stream content from your phone or tablet.  The design is sleek, with thin bezels that allow the screen to take center stage. The 60Hz refresh rate might not satisfy hardcore gamers looking for ultra-smooth motion, but for casual viewing and console gaming, it performs well. The built-in speakers are decent for the size, but you might want to pair it with a soundbar for a richer audio experience.  Overall, the Hisense QD6 55-Inch TV is a fantastic value for those seeking a high-quality picture, modern smart features, and a stylish design without breaking the bank.

title: Imperfect motion smoothness
body: Having the 65in version for 10days and keep trying to find an optimal setting for smooth picture motion. I'm 90% of time it produced super smooth beautiful video but the then at some sections of a video it stops working and jumps from the 240fps down to the basic 25 fps as either the AI can't make generate frames there, hardware can't keep up or better optimization is needed. I have tried factory resets, enabling turbo modes, plugging a fire TV stick, installing updates and no improvements. Sometimes when I rewind a video back to where it juddered it is suddenly smooth. It is very annoying and once you start focusing on this flaw you can't unsee it anymore. I can't concentrate on a movie I watch. For that reason I am thinking of returning the TV when it is still time. Other than that it has a very beautiful color and sharpness representation and  upscaling works fine. TV speakers are weak and need some upgrade. Loading apps or browsing Google TV isn't very fast so if I eventually decided to keep it, I would run fire TV stick on it. Lastly, switching of the motion smoothness isn't a good idea as 25fps on such a large TV does not look good.

title: Great TV.  Too much bloatware.
body:
Love the TV.  Great sound and display, but it's not a simple plug and play.  Lots of fine-tuning to get the picture and sound just right for all types of viewing.  Purchased this model, because of not needing a sound bar.  Not interested in gaming, but wanted a tv for watching tv: live sports, tv shows and streaming, movies on DVDs and sports.  After a week or 2 of picture and sound adjustments, I think I got the settings just right, but can't quite get the viewing of hockey adjusted,  The whites from the ice and jerseys are off and the sound is tinning for some reason.  

One piece of advice if you buy one: don't just click "accept all" when you're setting it up. Take time to look through the privacy settings and terms. There’s a lot of bloatware and ad banners that can make the home screen very cluttered, so it's definitely worth the effort to turn that off.

title: Vivid pictures, need 4k content to fully gain benefits!
body:

Movies look amazing on it, especially with the deep blacks from the OLED screen. Dark scenes actually have detail instead of looking gray or washed out, and the colors pop in a way that makes the whole picture feel more realistic. You can also really notice the pixel quality up close. The image stays sharp and smooth, whether I’m watching something cinematic or just regular TV.

It’s also been great for sports, especially watching games like the NBA Finals. The motion looks smooth, the court colors look vibrant, and the picture is clear enough that it makes the game feel more immersive. The 65 inch size gives it that theater feel without being too much for a living room, and the viewing angles are really nice too. Even from the side, the picture still looks great. Overall, it’s a beautiful TV with great color, sharp pixels, deep contrast, and a viewing experience that makes everything from movies to basketball feel way more enjoyable.

(they only had me ungplug the TV which only temporarily fixes these issues).  Why would I need to do this out of the box?  Also, the mute button being on the volume down is really dumb-to lower my volume 20% I now have to individually hit volume down 20 times because I can't hold it for 2 seconds?  Also, please attach the light sensor function to individual picture modes, I want full eye searing HDR when I want it and a nice dark picture when I want it, but the light sensor limits HDR brightness by default-really dumb-it's not just for power savings.  Also setting all picture modes to +20 cold and color saturation to 60 is made everything look neon and the AI settings mode used tiny blurry images.  The sound AI audio clips where so compressed and muddy that through the terrible built in speakers I just got a headache.  Guys, please offer a better range of picture presets so we can have a good out of the box experience.  Please fix the software updates.  Please fix the mute button fiasco.  I was 1 day away from a return.

body: Out of the box, my TV was buggy. (they only had me ungplug the TV which only temporarily fixes these issues).  Why would I need to do this out of the box?  Also, the mute button being on the volume down is really dumb-to lower my volume 20% I now have to individually hit volume down 20 times because I can't hold it for 2 seconds?  Also, please attach the light sensor function to individual picture modes, I want full eye searing HDR when I want it and a nice dark picture when I want it, but the light sensor limits HDR brightness by default-really dumb-it's not just for power savings.  Also setting all picture modes to +20 cold and color saturation to 60 is made everything look neon and the AI settings mode used tiny blurry images.  The sound AI audio clips where so compressed and muddy that through the terrible built in speakers I just got a headache.  Guys, please offer a better range of picture presets so we can have a good out of the box experience.  Please fix the software updates.  Please fix the mute button fiasco.  I was 1 day away from a return.

body:

After a week or 2 of picture and sound adjustments, I think I got the settings just right, but can't quite get the viewing of hockey adjusted,  The whites from the ice and jerseys are off and the sound is tinning for some reason.

body:
Overall this is a great TV. The visuals are a 10/10, but there are problems I wish they would fix.

1st problem, no steam link or moonlight support. My gaming PC is in another room, but I can't stream games to the TV. Competition has this feature and it's pretty disappointing WebOS doesn't support it.

2nd problem, eARC audio disconnections. I use a pair of Klipsch the Fives speakers over eARC, but they occasionally disconnect and switch to using the TVs built in speakers. Some days it doesn't disconnect, others I have to switch it back to eARC multiple times. Not a deal breaker, but definitely annoying to deal with while watching a movie.

Neither of these are deal breakers, but with this being an expensive flagship TV it's enough to drop the TV down a star.

title: Recommended for anyone with light sensitivity
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I highly recommend this TV to anyone else who suffers with light sensitivity. Most modern TVs cause me to experience symptoms of eye pain, headache, nausea and dizziness. I wanted an OLED to replace my 2011 plasma, but the first I ordered (the Sony) was unwatchable because of my photosensitivity. I ordered this LG G6 in the hope that the eye care mode (blue light filter) would help. It really does. And interestingly, even with eye care mode turned off, I don't experience the level of symptoms I had watching the Sony OLED. So maybe this type of OLED is better for light sensitive people than QD OLED?  I'm still experimenting with the settings, but the picture out of the box with some minor tweaks is truly amazing. The sound is better than I expected. Having switched off advertising and home screen recommendations, I like the operating system. I think the remote control is rubbish for a premium TV.  Also, I don't want to set up voice command, but if I accidentally press the voice commands button on the remote, the only way to remove the voice command instructions from the screen is to switch the TV off completely. Is there a way to stop this? But otherwise I love my TV.

title: Beware this years 77 inch
body: I purchased my first one early July to replace a 77 C1. I’m literally throwing my hands up at this point.  Every panel out of all of them were simply horrid. Major vertical banding on each panel.  I put over 100 hours on each panel.  Major dirty screen affect, and major cyan color push on the far left and right sides of some of the panels.  Black blobs in low dark scenes. Completely unacceptable for the price point.  LG should be embarrassed.  AV forum users confirming major issues with 2026 77 inch panels in comparison to the 65 and 83 inch models.  I currently have one of the seven panels left, and may pull the trigger on an 83 to compare. body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I’m very happy with the 77 inch LG OLED G6 television. The picture quality is absolutely amazing when watching 4K content. The image is incredibly clear, sharp, and detailed, making movies, sports, and streaming shows look fantastic. The colors are vibrant, and the OLED display really stands out. The 77 inch size is perfect for my wall and makes a huge impact in the room without feeling overwhelming. One of the reasons I chose this model was the gallery style design. Initially, we had it wall mounted with the wires visible, and it sat completely flush against the wall. While it looks sleek, the exposed wires took away from the overall appearance. We later had the wires run through the wall, which looks much cleaner and more professional. The trade-off is that the TV no longer sits quite as flush against the wall as it did originally, but the cleaner installation was well worth it. I also love that it’s a smart TV. Setting up and downloading all of my favorite streaming apps was easy, and everything is conveniently accessible in one place. One feature that pleasantly surprised me was the number of free channels included with LG channels. I wasn’t expecting to have access to so much free content right out of the box. There are channels for news, movies, sports, and more, which adds a lot of value without needing additional subscriptions. The included remote is simple, and intuitive, and easy to use. There is a stand available for purchase separately, but we preferred the clean look of a wall mounted installation. Overall, this is an excellent TV outstanding 4K picture quality, a beautiful design, and easy to use smart features. If you’re looking for a premium large screen TV, the LG OLED G6 is a great choice. ￼

title: Premium OLED Performance That Lives Up to the Hype
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] After spending several weeks with the LG OLED77G6WUA as our primary TV for movies, sports, gaming, and everyday streaming, it's clear this is a premium television that delivers an outstanding overall experience. 
The build quality immediately stands out. The panel feels exceptionally well-made with a slim, premium design that looks fantastic mounted on the wall. Despite its large 77-inch size, it feels sturdy and well-engineered, with excellent fit and finish. Nothing creaks or flexes during installation, giving confidence that it's built to last. 
The included remote is comfortable to hold and intuitive to use, The pointer function makes navigating menus and streaming apps much faster than traditional directional buttons, and voice controls respond accurately for searching content or adjusting settings. Dedicated streaming shortcuts are also a welcome convenience. 
From an ergonomics standpoint, everyday use is effortless. The webOS interface is responsive, inputs switch quickly, and settings are logically organized. Whether adjusting picture modes for movies, enabling Game Optimizer for console gaming, or customizing audio, everything is easy to access. The anti-reflective screen performs well in brighter rooms while still delivering exceptional contrast in darker environments.
After extensive daily use, the TV has remained consistent and reliable. It powers on quickly, maintains a stable Wi-Fi connection, and shows no signs of performance degradation. The premium construction and high-quality materials inspire confidence in its long-term durability. 
Overall, the LG OLED77G6WUA is an exceptional television. Between its premium build, user-friendly remote, thoughtful ergonomics, and dependable performance after extensive testing, it has exceeded expectations and has become the centerpiece of our home entertainment setup. It's a worthwhile investment for anyone looking for a flagship OLED experience.

title: Great with a few issues
body:
Overall this is a great TV. The visuals are a 10/10, but there are problems I wish they would fix.

1st problem, no steam link or moonlight support. My gaming PC is in another room, but I can't stream games to the TV. Competition has this feature and it's pretty disappointing WebOS doesn't support it.

2nd problem, eARC audio disconnections. I use a pair of Klipsch the Fives speakers over eARC, but they occasionally disconnect and switch to using the TVs built in speakers. Some days it doesn't disconnect, others I have to switch it back to eARC multiple times. Not a deal breaker, but definitely annoying to deal with while watching a movie.

Neither of these are deal breakers, but with this being an expensive flagship TV it's enough to drop the TV down a star.

Bottom line, if you have a bright room like me this TV is a game changer, as long as these gripes aren't too annoying to you.

title: Recommended for anyone with light sensitivity
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I highly recommend this TV to anyone else who suffers with light sensitivity. Most modern TVs cause me to experience symptoms of eye pain, headache, nausea and dizziness. I wanted an OLED to replace my 2011 plasma, but the first I ordered (the Sony) was unwatchable because of my photosensitivity. I ordered this LG G6 in the hope that the eye care mode (blue light filter) would help. It really does. And interestingly, even with eye care mode turned off, I don't experience the level of symptoms I had watching the Sony OLED. So maybe this type of OLED is better for light sensitive people than QD OLED?  I'm still experimenting with the settings, but the picture out of the box with some minor tweaks is truly amazing. The sound is better than I expected. Having switched off advertising and home screen recommendations, I like the operating system. I think the remote control is rubbish for a premium TV.  Also, I don't want to set up voice command, but if I accidentally press the voice commands button on the remote, the only way to remove the voice command instructions from the screen is to switch the TV off completely. Is there a way to stop this? But otherwise I love my TV.

title: Simply the best
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I had been waiting to pick up a large TV for my living room, and I'm glad this is where I ended up. My previous TV had a VA panel with local dimming and this OLED is a massive improvement in every way. The blacks are pitch black, with no halo effect you can get with local dimming. Nearly instantaneous response times with no smearing. Much better color reproduction that leads to a very vivid viewing experience. Gamers will appreciate the 165Hz refresh rate as well. The remote uses motion controls that are fun and very intuitive to use. For screen calibration the TV will show you a series of images with different options applied (gamma, brightness, sharpness, etc.) and you will pick your favorite from each series and at the end get a personalized picture profile. I think this is a fun way to help the average person get the most out of their TV and make it their own. If you opt for the stand the TV does sit back at an angle which can be noticeable. Not a big deal, but thought I would mention it. Personally, I would recommend using the wall mount if you have that option. Overall it's a fantastic TV, and with LG's post-launch support it will continue to be for years to come.

title: Beware this years 77 inch
body: I purchased my first one early July to replace a 77 C1.  I have been through 7 panels, whether it be through exchanges or purchasing additional units to compare and then exchanging those as well:  at one point I had 3 TVs in the house trying to compare and pick the more acceptable one.  I’m literally throwing my hands up at this point.  Every panel out of all of them were simply horrid. Major vertical banding on each panel.  I put over 100 hours on each panel.  Major dirty screen affect, and major cyan color push on the far left and right sides of some of the panels.  Black blobs in low dark scenes. Completely unacceptable for the price point.  LG should be embarrassed.  AV forum users confirming major issues with 2026 77 inch panels in comparison to the 65 and 83 inch models.  I currently have one of the seven panels left, and may pull the trigger on an 83 to compare.  Iv literally waisted the last 3 weeks going back and fourth, returning, testing and am spinning my wheels on how a company like this is allowing these panels; at this price, to hit store shelves in this state.  Buyer beware.

title: The Centre Peice My Living Room
body:
(This review was collected as part of a promotion.) The G6 is the premier TV from LG and right out of the box it showed very clearly why. Never in my life have I had so many compliments about something in my home, it’s actually received more compliments then anything i’ve ever owned! It truly has become the centre piece of my living room and ascends beyond just a TV, it is art. This is my first flagship TV, and out of all my friends and family the only top of the line TV I know of anyone to have. The TV was significantly more affordable than Sony’s offering, and also slightly under the Samsung, however I preferred the glossy look of the LG over the samsungs matte and found the performance the same. We went with the LG and couldn’t be happier. Upon first view the TVs slim frame pops immediately. it looks as if a picture frame itself. The picture quality is so good, that with default settings, certain live sports had become unwatchable, I never realized how poor quality some of these sports broadcast in, and my TV was TOO HD. Luckily the LG has many settings to smooth out the broadcast. I can confidently say the best view of the 2026 FIFA world cup was at my house! The TV has also made watching tv anywhere else a crime, my parents or friends TVs cannot compare to the HD quality and pure blacks the G6 offers, and that would have to be my only complaint. Watching TV on anything other than this TV (or its equals) is sometimes unbearable,  but it’s a downside worth every penny. 

So far as for the reliability, we don’t have any issues as of yet and i’m hoping in the future it can also hold up well.

title: FINALLY the television that fits our niche needs!
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Our last TV was 15 years old, stuck out from the wall, and had run its course. We have been moving back toward physical media, DVDs, Blu ray, even VHS, and refused to let that mean downgrading our experience. Think of it like a high end turntable for vinyl. It makes everything you love look better than ever. The picture quality on the LG OLED evo AI G6 is stunning. Watching favorite films on physical media on this screen is something we were not prepared for. The motion smoothing feature called TruMotion can be turned off, giving us back that warm cinematic film look we love. As someone with motion sensitivity and migraines, this was a BIG relief. The Magic Remote with voice search has spoiled us completely. No more typing letter by letter while a toddler screams for their show. The flush wall mount is a dream. Our TV sits near our front door and this one practically disappears against the wall. Review submitted as part of a program that provides a purchase discount.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

title: Disappointed at this time
body: I just purchased the G6 after having the G5. I noticed immediately that the G6 is not as bright and many scenes as the G5. Now that I’m reading reviews from the top reviewers, they are also noticing this and actually. Rtings.com testing shows that the G6 actually is dimmer in HDR content. This TV is advertised as their brightest OLED ever yet its brightness is not showing. What I will say is it has incredible fine detail and a huge step up in that area over the G5. They’re obviously needs to be some updates because there’s also motion handling issues that are bothering me. The G5 motion handling was perfect after a full year of updates. The G6 has such bad flickering and small, moving objects that they almost disappear, especially movies like Star Wars. My main complaint though is the brightness. I bought this TV because I thought it was going to be a brighter. More vivid TV like it was advertised. It is not at this point. I sincerely hope LG is making effort to fixing this particular issues so that it lives up to the advertising.

title: Rough start great result
body: Out of the box, my TV was buggy. I downloaded the firmware from the website (which did nothing at first) then did the factory reset and viola, everything fixed.  Why didn't LG support ever suggest this? (they only had me ungplug the TV which only temporarily fixes these issues).  Why would I need to do this out of the box?  Also, the mute button being on the volume down is really dumb-to lower my volume 20% I now have to individually hit volume down 20 times because I can't hold it for 2 seconds? body:
Overall this is a great TV. The visuals are a 10/10, but there are problems I wish they would fix.

1st problem, no steam link or moonlight support. My gaming PC is in another room, but I can't stream games to the TV. Competition has this feature and it's pretty disappointing WebOS doesn't support it.

2nd problem, eARC audio disconnections. I use a pair of Klipsch the Fives speakers over eARC, but they occasionally disconnect and switch to using the TVs built in speakers. Some days it doesn't disconnect, others I have to switch it back to eARC multiple times. Not a deal breaker, but definitely annoying to deal with while watching a movie.

Bottom line, if you have a bright room like me this TV is a game changer, as long as these gripes aren't too annoying to you.

title: Recommended for anyone with light sensitivity
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I highly recommend this TV to anyone else who suffers with light sensitivity. Most modern TVs cause me to experience symptoms of eye pain, headache, nausea and dizziness. I wanted an OLED to replace my 2011 plasma, but the first I ordered (the Sony) was unwatchable because of my photosensitivity. I ordered this LG G6 in the hope that the eye care mode (blue light filter) would help. It really does. And interestingly, even with eye care mode turned off, I don't experience the level of symptoms I had watching the Sony OLED. So maybe this type of OLED is better for light sensitive people than QD OLED?  I'm still experimenting with the settings, but the picture out of the box with some minor tweaks is truly amazing. The sound is better than I expected. Having switched off advertising and home screen recommendations, I like the operating system. I think the remote control is rubbish for a premium TV.  Also, I don't want to set up voice command, but if I accidentally press the voice commands button on the remote, the only way to remove the voice command instructions from the screen is to switch the TV off completely. Is there a way to stop this? But otherwise I love my TV.

title: Simply the best
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I had been waiting to pick up a large TV for my living room, and I'm glad this is where I ended up. My previous TV had a VA panel with local dimming and this OLED is a massive improvement in every way. The blacks are pitch black, with no halo effect you can get with local dimming. Nearly instantaneous response times with no smearing. Much better color reproduction that leads to a very vivid viewing experience. Gamers will appreciate the 165Hz refresh rate as well. The remote uses motion controls that are fun and very intuitive to use. For screen calibration the TV will show you a series of images with different options applied (gamma, brightness, sharpness, etc.) and you will pick your favorite from each series and at the end get a personalized picture profile. I think this is a fun way to help the average person get the most out of their TV and make it their own. If you opt for the stand the TV does sit back at an angle which can be noticeable. Not a big deal, but thought I would mention it. Personally, I would recommend using the wall mount if you have that option. Overall it's a fantastic TV, and with LG's post-launch support it will continue to be for years to come.

title: Beware this years 77 inch
body: I purchased my first one early July to replace a 77 C1.  I have been through 7 panels, whether it be through exchanges or purchasing additional units to compare and then exchanging those as well:  at one point I had 3 TVs in the house trying to compare and pick the more acceptable one.  I’m literally throwing my hands up at this point.  Every panel out of all of them were simply horrid. Major vertical banding on each panel.  I put over 100 hours on each panel.  Major dirty screen affect, and major cyan color push on the far left and right sides of some of the panels.  Black blobs in low dark scenes. Completely unacceptable for the price point.  LG should be embarrassed.  AV forum users confirming major issues with 2026 77 inch panels in comparison to the 65 and 83 inch models.  I currently have one of the seven panels left, and may pull the trigger on an 83 to compare.  Iv literally waisted the last 3 weeks going back and fourth, returning, testing and am spinning my wheels on how a company like this is allowing these panels; at this price, to hit store shelves in this state.  Buyer beware.

title: The LG OLED G6 combines incredible 4K picture quality with smart features and an impressive selection of free channels.
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I’m very happy with the 77 inch LG OLED G6 television. The picture quality is absolutely amazing when watching 4K content. The image is incredibly clear, sharp, and detailed, making movies, sports, and streaming shows look fantastic. The colors are vibrant, and the OLED display really stands out. For non-4K channels, the picture quality is still good, but it is not nearly as crisp as true 4K content. If you watch a lot of 4K programming, this TV really shines. The 77 inch size is perfect for my wall and makes a huge impact in the room without feeling overwhelming. One of the reasons I chose this model was the gallery style design. Initially, we had it wall mounted with the wires visible, and it sat completely flush against the wall. While it looks sleek, the exposed wires took away from the overall appearance. We later had the wires run through the wall, which looks much cleaner and more professional. The trade-off is that the TV no longer sits quite as flush against the wall as it did originally, but the cleaner installation was well worth it. I also love that it’s a smart TV. Setting up and downloading all of my favorite streaming apps was easy, and everything is conveniently accessible in one place. One feature that pleasantly surprised me was the number of free channels included with LG channels. I wasn’t expecting to have access to so much free content right out of the box. There are channels for news, movies, sports, and more, which adds a lot of value without needing additional subscriptions. The included remote is simple, and intuitive, and easy to use. There is a stand available for purchase separately, but we preferred the clean look of a wall mounted installation. Overall, this is an excellent TV outstanding 4K picture quality, a beautiful design, and easy to use smart features. If you’re looking for a premium large screen TV, the LG OLED G6 is a great choice. ￼

title: Premium OLED Performance That Lives Up to the Hype
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] After spending several weeks with the LG OLED77G6WUA as our primary TV for movies, sports, gaming, and everyday streaming, it's clear this is a premium television that delivers an outstanding overall experience. 
The build quality immediately stands out. The panel feels exceptionally well-made with a slim, premium design that looks fantastic mounted on the wall. Despite its large 77-inch size, it feels sturdy and well-engineered, with excellent fit and finish. Nothing creaks or flexes during installation, giving confidence that it's built to last. 
The included remote is comfortable to hold and intuitive to use, The pointer function makes navigating menus and streaming apps much faster than traditional directional buttons, and voice controls respond accurately for searching content or adjusting settings. Dedicated streaming shortcuts are also a welcome convenience. 
From an ergonomics standpoint, everyday use is effortless. The webOS interface is responsive, inputs switch quickly, and settings are logically organized. Whether adjusting picture modes for movies, enabling Game Optimizer for console gaming, or customizing audio, everything is easy to access. The anti-reflective screen performs well in brighter rooms while still delivering exceptional contrast in darker environments.
After extensive daily use, the TV has remained consistent and reliable. It powers on quickly, maintains a stable Wi-Fi connection, and shows no signs of performance degradation. The premium construction and high-quality materials inspire confidence in its long-term durability. 
Overall, the LG OLED77G6WUA is an exceptional television. Between its premium build, user-friendly remote, thoughtful ergonomics, and dependable performance after extensive testing, it has exceeded expectations and has become the centerpiece of our home entertainment setup. It's a worthwhile investment for anyone looking for a flagship OLED experience.

body:

​Moving to the OLED65G64LW has been an absolute revelation. The jump from 55 to 65 inches is impressive on its own, but the sheer leap in technology over the last ten years is mind-blowing.
​The brightness levels on this G-series panel are a massive step up from my old B6—it handles room reflections effortlessly while keeping those famous, perfect OLED blacks. Knowing how much LG has advanced their built-in panel-care features, logo luminance adjustment, and anti-burn-in tech over the years gives me massive peace of mind this time around, especially for broadcast TV and subtitles.
​The design is a work of art it mounts incredibly flush to the wall, looking completely seamless and premium. The smart webOS interface is also lightning-fast compared to older generations.
​If you are hesitating to upgrade an older OLED, don't look back. This is a masterful piece of engineering and proves why LG still leads the way.

title: Great with a few issues
body:
Overall this is a great TV. The visuals are a 10/10, but there are problems I wish they would fix.

1st problem, no steam link or moonlight support. My gaming PC is in another room, but I can't stream games to the TV. Competition has this feature and it's pretty disappointing WebOS doesn't support it.

2nd problem, eARC audio disconnections. I use a pair of Klipsch the Fives speakers over eARC, but they occasionally disconnect and switch to using the TVs built in speakers. Some days it doesn't disconnect, others I have to switch it back to eARC multiple times. Not a deal breaker, but definitely annoying to deal with while watching a movie.

Neither of these are deal breakers, but with this being an expensive flagship TV it's enough to drop the TV down a star.

Bottom line, if you have a bright room like me this TV is a game changer, as long as these gripes aren't too annoying to you.

The g6 completely fixes all of these issues. Its the best tv I have owend. Motion for movies is great. The motion interpolation setting are fantastic and some of the best I have seen. Colour banding is not an issue at all on this tv. 60hz gaming motion is massivly improved, image is alot clearer. I still prefer it with bfi enabled as it sharpens it up. But because the tv is so bright even with bfi enabled, the drop in brightness isnt an issue. The brightness of the tv is perfect for bright room viewing.
If anyone had an older oled tv and was on the fence if a newer oled was worth it and had any improvements. I can safely say the g6 is well worth the upgrade.

title: Recommended for anyone with light sensitivity
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I highly recommend this TV to anyone else who suffers with light sensitivity. Most modern TVs cause me to experience symptoms of eye pain, headache, nausea and dizziness. I wanted an OLED to replace my 2011 plasma, but the first I ordered (the Sony) was unwatchable because of my photosensitivity. I ordered this LG G6 in the hope that the eye care mode (blue light filter) would help. It really does. And interestingly, even with eye care mode turned off, I don't experience the level of symptoms I had watching the Sony OLED. So maybe this type of OLED is better for light sensitive people than QD OLED?  I'm still experimenting with the settings, but the picture out of the box with some minor tweaks is truly amazing. The sound is better than I expected. Having switched off advertising and home screen recommendations, I like the operating system. I think the remote control is rubbish for a premium TV.  Also, I don't want to set up voice command, but if I accidentally press the voice commands button on the remote, the only way to remove the voice command instructions from the screen is to switch the TV off completely. Is there a way to stop this? But otherwise I love my TV.

title: Simply the best
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I had been waiting to pick up a large TV for my living room, and I'm glad this is where I ended up. Nearly instantaneous response times with no smearing. Much better color reproduction that leads to a very vivid viewing experience. Gamers will appreciate the 165Hz refresh rate as well. The remote uses motion controls that are fun and very intuitive to use. For screen calibration the TV will show you a series of images with different options applied (gamma, brightness, sharpness, etc.) and you will pick your favorite from each series and at the end get a personalized picture profile. I think this is a fun way to help the average person get the most out of their TV and make it their own. If you opt for the stand the TV does sit back at an angle which can be noticeable. Not a big deal, but thought I would mention it. Personally, I would recommend using the wall mount if you have that option. Overall it's a fantastic TV, and with LG's post-launch support it will continue to be for years to come.

title: Beware this years 77 inch
body: I purchased my first one early July to replace a 77 C1. I’m literally throwing my hands up at this point.  Every panel out of all of them were simply horrid. Major vertical banding on each panel.  I put over 100 hours on each panel.  Major dirty screen affect, and major cyan color push on the far left and right sides of some of the panels.  Black blobs in low dark scenes. Completely unacceptable for the price point.  LG should be embarrassed.  AV forum users confirming major issues with 2026 77 inch panels in comparison to the 65 and 83 inch models.  I currently have one of the seven panels left, and may pull the trigger on an 83 to compare.  Iv literally waisted the last 3 weeks going back and fourth, returning, testing and am spinning my wheels on how a company like this is allowing these panels; at this price, to hit store shelves in this state.  Buyer beware.

Luckily the LG has many settings to smooth out the broadcast. I can confidently say the best view of the 2026 FIFA world cup was at my house! The TV has also made watching tv anywhere else a crime, my parents or friends TVs cannot compare to the HD quality and pure blacks the G6 offers, and that would have to be my only complaint. Watching TV on anything other than this TV (or its equals) is sometimes unbearable,  but it’s a downside worth every penny. 

So far as for the reliability, we don’t have any issues as of yet and i’m hoping in the future it can also hold up well.

title: The LG OLED G6 combines incredible 4K picture quality with smart features and an impressive selection of free channels.
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I’m very happy with the 77 inch LG OLED G6 television. The picture quality is absolutely amazing when watching 4K content. For non-4K channels, the picture quality is still good, but it is not nearly as crisp as true 4K content. If you watch a lot of 4K programming, this TV really shines. The 77 inch size is perfect for my wall and makes a huge impact in the room without feeling overwhelming. One of the reasons I chose this model was the gallery style design. Initially, we had it wall mounted with the wires visible, and it sat completely flush against the wall. While it looks sleek, the exposed wires took away from the overall appearance. We later had the wires run through the wall, which looks much cleaner and more professional. The trade-off is that the TV no longer sits quite as flush against the wall as it did originally, but the cleaner installation was well worth it. I also love that it’s a smart TV. Setting up and downloading all of my favorite streaming apps was easy, and everything is conveniently accessible in one place. One feature that pleasantly surprised me was the number of free channels included with LG channels. I wasn’t expecting to have access to so much free content right out of the box. There are channels for news, movies, sports, and more, which adds a lot of value without needing additional subscriptions. The included remote is simple, and intuitive, and easy to use. There is a stand available for purchase separately, but we preferred the clean look of a wall mounted installation. Overall, this is an excellent TV outstanding 4K picture quality, a beautiful design, and easy to use smart features. If you’re looking for a premium large screen TV, the LG OLED G6 is a great choice. ￼

title: FINALLY the television that fits our niche needs!

It makes everything you love look better than ever. The picture quality on the LG OLED evo AI G6 is stunning. Watching favorite films on physical media on this screen is something we were not prepared for. The Magic Remote with voice search has spoiled us completely. No more typing letter by letter while a toddler screams for their show. The flush wall mount is a dream. title: Disappointed at this time

This TV is advertised as their brightest OLED ever yet its brightness is not showing. What I will say is it has incredible fine detail and a huge step up in that area over the G5. They’re obviously needs to be some updates because there’s also motion handling issues that are bothering me. The G5 motion handling was perfect after a full year of updates. The G6 has such bad flickering and small, moving objects that they almost disappear, especially movies like Star Wars. My main complaint though is the brightness. title: A fantastic TV but......
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] After much research following the purchase of a Samsung TV earlier this year which had to be returned, I opted for the LG OLED C6 48". The TV is great & after a few false starts, pretty easy to navigate the menu to set it up to our taste.

(they only had me ungplug the TV which only temporarily fixes these issues).  Why would I need to do this out of the box?  Also, the mute button being on the volume down is really dumb-to lower my volume 20% I now have to individually hit volume down 20 times because I can't hold it for 2 seconds?  Also, please attach the light sensor function to individual picture modes, I want full eye searing HDR when I want it and a nice dark picture when I want it, but the light sensor limits HDR brightness by default-really dumb-it's not just for power savings.  Also setting all picture modes to +20 cold and color saturation to 60 is made everything look neon and the AI settings mode used tiny blurry images.  The sound AI audio clips where so compressed and muddy that through the terrible built in speakers I just got a headache.  Guys, please offer a better range of picture presets so we can have a good out of the box experience.  Please fix the software updates.  Please fix the mute button fiasco. body:
Overall this is a great TV. The visuals are a 10/10, but there are problems I wish they would fix.

1st problem, no steam link or moonlight support. My gaming PC is in another room, but I can't stream games to the TV. Competition has this feature and it's pretty disappointing WebOS doesn't support it.

2nd problem, eARC audio disconnections. I use a pair of Klipsch the Fives speakers over eARC, but they occasionally disconnect and switch to using the TVs built in speakers. Some days it doesn't disconnect, others I have to switch it back to eARC multiple times. Not a deal breaker, but definitely annoying to deal with while watching a movie.

Neither of these are deal breakers, but with this being an expensive flagship TV it's enough to drop the TV down a star.

Bottom line, if you have a bright room like me this TV is a game changer, as long as these gripes aren't too annoying to you.

title: Recommended for anyone with light sensitivity
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I highly recommend this TV to anyone else who suffers with light sensitivity. Most modern TVs cause me to experience symptoms of eye pain, headache, nausea and dizziness. I wanted an OLED to replace my 2011 plasma, but the first I ordered (the Sony) was unwatchable because of my photosensitivity. I ordered this LG G6 in the hope that the eye care mode (blue light filter) would help. It really does. And interestingly, even with eye care mode turned off, I don't experience the level of symptoms I had watching the Sony OLED. So maybe this type of OLED is better for light sensitive people than QD OLED?  I'm still experimenting with the settings, but the picture out of the box with some minor tweaks is truly amazing. The sound is better than I expected. Having switched off advertising and home screen recommendations, I like the operating system. I think the remote control is rubbish for a premium TV.  Also, I don't want to set up voice command, but if I accidentally press the voice commands button on the remote, the only way to remove the voice command instructions from the screen is to switch the TV off completely. Is there a way to stop this? But otherwise I love my TV.

body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I had been waiting to pick up a large TV for my living room, and I'm glad this is where I ended up. Nearly instantaneous response times with no smearing. Much better color reproduction that leads to a very vivid viewing experience. Gamers will appreciate the 165Hz refresh rate as well. The remote uses motion controls that are fun and very intuitive to use. For screen calibration the TV will show you a series of images with different options applied (gamma, brightness, sharpness, etc.) and you will pick your favorite from each series and at the end get a personalized picture profile. I think this is a fun way to help the average person get the most out of their TV and make it their own. If you opt for the stand the TV does sit back at an angle which can be noticeable. Not a big deal, but thought I would mention it. Personally, I would recommend using the wall mount if you have that option. Overall it's a fantastic TV, and with LG's post-launch support it will continue to be for years to come.

Major dirty screen affect, and major cyan color push on the far left and right sides of some of the panels.  Black blobs in low dark scenes. Completely unacceptable for the price point.  LG should be embarrassed.  AV forum users confirming major issues with 2026 77 inch panels in comparison to the 65 and 83 inch models.  I currently have one of the seven panels left, and may pull the trigger on an 83 to compare. body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I’m very happy with the 77 inch LG OLED G6 television. The picture quality is absolutely amazing when watching 4K content. One feature that pleasantly surprised me was the number of free channels included with LG channels. I wasn’t expecting to have access to so much free content right out of the box. There are channels for news, movies, sports, and more, which adds a lot of value without needing additional subscriptions. The included remote is simple, and intuitive, and easy to use. There is a stand available for purchase separately, but we preferred the clean look of a wall mounted installation. Overall, this is an excellent TV outstanding 4K picture quality, a beautiful design, and easy to use smart features. If you’re looking for a premium large screen TV, the LG OLED G6 is a great choice. ￼

title: Premium OLED Performance That Lives Up to the Hype
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] After spending several weeks with the LG OLED77G6WUA as our primary TV for movies, sports, gaming, and everyday streaming, it's clear this is a premium television that delivers an outstanding overall experience. 
The build quality immediately stands out. The panel feels exceptionally well-made with a slim, premium design that looks fantastic mounted on the wall. Despite its large 77-inch size, it feels sturdy and well-engineered, with excellent fit and finish. Nothing creaks or flexes during installation, giving confidence that it's built to last. 
The included remote is comfortable to hold and intuitive to use, The pointer function makes navigating menus and streaming apps much faster than traditional directional buttons, and voice controls respond accurately for searching content or adjusting settings. Dedicated streaming shortcuts are also a welcome convenience. 
From an ergonomics standpoint, everyday use is effortless. The webOS interface is responsive, inputs switch quickly, and settings are logically organized. Whether adjusting picture modes for movies, enabling Game Optimizer for console gaming, or customizing audio, everything is easy to access. The anti-reflective screen performs well in brighter rooms while still delivering exceptional contrast in darker environments.
After extensive daily use, the TV has remained consistent and reliable. It powers on quickly, maintains a stable Wi-Fi connection, and shows no signs of performance degradation. The premium construction and high-quality materials inspire confidence in its long-term durability. 
Overall, the LG OLED77G6WUA is an exceptional television. Between its premium build, user-friendly remote, thoughtful ergonomics, and dependable performance after extensive testing, it has exceeded expectations and has become the centerpiece of our home entertainment setup. It's a worthwhile investment for anyone looking for a flagship OLED experience.

title: Stunning picture meets minimalist design
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The  LG OLED evo AI W6  is the most impressive TVs I have experienced. It's not just about the picture quality, it is about the entire experience, from the minimalist design to the wireless setup.

The first thing that caught my attention was the Wallpaper Design. Once mounted, it looks less like a television and more like a piece of modern art. Paired with Zero Connect Box, all of my streaming devices and game consoles connect to the box instead of the TV itself, leaving the display free of HDMI cables and creating an incredibly clean setup.

Picture quality is exactly what you would expect from a flagship OLED and then some! Blacks are truly black, colors are rich and vibrant without looking overprocessed, and the brightness is impressive for an OLED. Motion handling was excellent, and the TV's gaming features make it a fantastic choice for anyone with a PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, or gaming PC. The AI-powered picture and sound adjustments are surprisingly useful. Instead of constantly tweaking settings, the TV intelligently optimizes the experience based on what you are watching.

One thing I think buyers should know before mounting it: your wall setup matters. While the Wallpaper Design is meant to sit nearly flush against the wall, you will get the best results if you have a recessed power outlet behind the TV. If your wall has a standard outlet, the power plug can create a small gap, preventing it from sitting completely flat. It's not a flaw to be clear but something to plan for if aiming for that true gallery style look.

If you're looking for a TV that combines premium performance with one of the cleanest, most elegant wall flush look, thLG OLED evo AI W6 absolutely delivers. It's an investment, but one that transforms both your viewing experience and the look of your home.

body:
