Purchased this model, because of not needing a sound bar.  Not interested in gaming, but wanted a tv for watching tv: live sports, tv shows and streaming, movies on DVDs and sports.  After a week or 2 of picture and sound adjustments, I think I got the settings just right, but can't quite get the viewing of hockey adjusted,  The whites from the ice and jerseys are off and the sound is tinning for some reason.  

One piece of advice if you buy one: don't just click "accept all" when you're setting it up. Take time to look through the privacy settings and terms. There’s a lot of bloatware and ad banners that can make the home screen very cluttered, so it's definitely worth the effort to turn that off.

You can also really notice the pixel quality up close. The image stays sharp and smooth, whether I’m watching something cinematic or just regular TV.

It’s also been great for sports, especially watching games like the NBA Finals. The motion looks smooth, the court colors look vibrant, and the picture is clear enough that it makes the game feel more immersive. The 65 inch size gives it that theater feel without being too much for a living room, and the viewing angles are really nice too. Even from the side, the picture still looks great. title: Stunning picture meets minimalist design
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The  LG OLED evo AI W6  is the most impressive TVs I have experienced. It's not just about the picture quality, it is about the entire experience, from the minimalist design to the wireless setup.

The first thing that caught my attention was the Wallpaper Design. Once mounted, it looks less like a television and more like a piece of modern art. Paired with Zero Connect Box, all of my streaming devices and game consoles connect to the box instead of the TV itself, leaving the display free of HDMI cables and creating an incredibly clean setup.

Picture quality is exactly what you would expect from a flagship OLED and then some! Blacks are truly black, colors are rich and vibrant without looking overprocessed, and the brightness is impressive for an OLED. Motion handling was excellent, and the TV's gaming features make it a fantastic choice for anyone with a PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, or gaming PC. The AI-powered picture and sound adjustments are surprisingly useful. Instead of constantly tweaking settings, the TV intelligently optimizes the experience based on what you are watching.

One thing I think buyers should know before mounting it: your wall setup matters. While the Wallpaper Design is meant to sit nearly flush against the wall, you will get the best results if you have a recessed power outlet behind the TV. If your wall has a standard outlet, the power plug can create a small gap, preventing it from sitting completely flat. It's not a flaw to be clear but something to plan for if aiming for that true gallery style look.

If you're looking for a TV that combines premium performance with one of the cleanest, most elegant wall flush look, thLG OLED evo AI W6 absolutely delivers. It's an investment, but one that transforms both your viewing experience and the look of your home.

I had to do a hard restart (unplug TV, press on/off button for 30 seconds and then plug back in and turn on, same with soundbar).  That did at least sort out the soundbar issue and she was able to talk me through something so that I only have to use one remote control to use the TV, skybox and soundbar. title: Great with a few issues
body:
Overall this is a great TV. The visuals are a 10/10, but there are problems I wish they would fix.

1st problem, no steam link or moonlight support. My gaming PC is in another room, but I can't stream games to the TV. Competition has this feature and it's pretty disappointing WebOS doesn't support it.

2nd problem, eARC audio disconnections. I use a pair of Klipsch the Fives speakers over eARC, but they occasionally disconnect and switch to using the TVs built in speakers. Some days it doesn't disconnect, others I have to switch it back to eARC multiple times. Not a deal breaker, but definitely annoying to deal with while watching a movie.

Neither of these are deal breakers, but with this being an expensive flagship TV it's enough to drop the TV down a star.

Bottom line, if you have a bright room like me this TV is a game changer, as long as these gripes aren't too annoying to you.

Colour banding is not an issue at all on this tv. 60hz gaming motion is massivly improved, image is alot clearer. I still prefer it with bfi enabled as it sharpens it up. But because the tv is so bright even with bfi enabled, the drop in brightness isnt an issue. The brightness of the tv is perfect for bright room viewing.

title: Recommended for anyone with light sensitivity
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I highly recommend this TV to anyone else who suffers with light sensitivity. Most modern TVs cause me to experience symptoms of eye pain, headache, nausea and dizziness. I wanted an OLED to replace my 2011 plasma, but the first I ordered (the Sony) was unwatchable because of my photosensitivity. I ordered this LG G6 in the hope that the eye care mode (blue light filter) would help. It really does. And interestingly, even with eye care mode turned off, I don't experience the level of symptoms I had watching the Sony OLED. So maybe this type of OLED is better for light sensitive people than QD OLED?  I'm still experimenting with the settings, but the picture out of the box with some minor tweaks is truly amazing. The sound is better than I expected. Having switched off advertising and home screen recommendations, I like the operating system. I think the remote control is rubbish for a premium TV.  Also, I don't want to set up voice command, but if I accidentally press the voice commands button on the remote, the only way to remove the voice command instructions from the screen is to switch the TV off completely. Is there a way to stop this? But otherwise I love my TV.

title: Simply the best
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I had been waiting to pick up a large TV for my living room, and I'm glad this is where I ended up. Nearly instantaneous response times with no smearing. Much better color reproduction that leads to a very vivid viewing experience. Gamers will appreciate the 165Hz refresh rate as well. The remote uses motion controls that are fun and very intuitive to use. For screen calibration the TV will show you a series of images with different options applied (gamma, brightness, sharpness, etc.) and you will pick your favorite from each series and at the end get a personalized picture profile. I think this is a fun way to help the average person get the most out of their TV and make it their own. If you opt for the stand the TV does sit back at an angle which can be noticeable. Not a big deal, but thought I would mention it. Personally, I would recommend using the wall mount if you have that option. Overall it's a fantastic TV, and with LG's post-launch support it will continue to be for years to come.

title: Beware this years 77 inch
body: I purchased my first one early July to replace a 77 C1. I’m literally throwing my hands up at this point.  Every panel out of all of them were simply horrid. Major vertical banding on each panel.  I put over 100 hours on each panel.  Major dirty screen affect, and major cyan color push on the far left and right sides of some of the panels.  Black blobs in low dark scenes. Completely unacceptable for the price point.  LG should be embarrassed.  AV forum users confirming major issues with 2026 77 inch panels in comparison to the 65 and 83 inch models.  I currently have one of the seven panels left, and may pull the trigger on an 83 to compare.  Iv literally waisted the last 3 weeks going back and fourth, returning, testing and am spinning my wheels on how a company like this is allowing these panels; at this price, to hit store shelves in this state.  Buyer beware.

title: The LG OLED G6 combines incredible 4K picture quality with smart features and an impressive selection of free channels.
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I’m very happy with the 77 inch LG OLED G6 television. The picture quality is absolutely amazing when watching 4K content. The image is incredibly clear, sharp, and detailed, making movies, sports, and streaming shows look fantastic. The colors are vibrant, and the OLED display really stands out. For non-4K channels, the picture quality is still good, but it is not nearly as crisp as true 4K content. If you watch a lot of 4K programming, this TV really shines. The 77 inch size is perfect for my wall and makes a huge impact in the room without feeling overwhelming. One of the reasons I chose this model was the gallery style design. Initially, we had it wall mounted with the wires visible, and it sat completely flush against the wall. While it looks sleek, the exposed wires took away from the overall appearance. We later had the wires run through the wall, which looks much cleaner and more professional. The trade-off is that the TV no longer sits quite as flush against the wall as it did originally, but the cleaner installation was well worth it. I also love that it’s a smart TV. Setting up and downloading all of my favorite streaming apps was easy, and everything is conveniently accessible in one place. One feature that pleasantly surprised me was the number of free channels included with LG channels. I wasn’t expecting to have access to so much free content right out of the box. title: 🌟The Greatest Upgrade in History🌟
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] 🌟 RIP to My Optometrist and Audiologist: The Greatest Upgrade in History

We just replaced our ancient, 32-inch dinosaur of a TV with the 65-inch Neo QLED and matching soundbar, and our lives have officially changed.

For the last decade, watching a movie in our living room required the tactical precision of a bomb squad. My glasses had to be perfectly wiped, my chair had to be exactly four feet from the screen, and my hearing aids were turned up so high I could hear my neighbour's cat changing its mind in the next house over.

Not anymore.

With this new 65-inch beast, the glasses are officially OFF. The picture is so crisp, bright, and staggeringly massive that I can see the individual pores on a football player's face from the kitchen. I'm pretty sure the local airport is using my living room as a backup runway flare.

And the soundbar - S-Series All-in-one Soundbar HW-S60D with 5.0ch? Hearing aids: DEACTIVATED. Turned them straight off. The bass from this thing doesn’t just enter your ears; it rattles your fillings and rearranges your internal organs. I watched an action movie last night and felt the explosions in my shins. For the first time in years, I can actually understand the whispered dialogue in gritty dramas without needing subtitles or blasting the volume to maximum.

Even the remote control is a hyperactive masterpiece. Our old TV remote required a literal prayer ritual, a hard point-and-shoot aim, and a thumb wrestling match just to change the channel. This new remote is so lightning-fast and responsive that if I even blink near the directional pad, it has already skipped three episodes of my show. It responds faster than my own reflexes.

Hubby says it’s "too big for the room", but I can't hear them over the glorious, cinematic rumble of my new setup.  The only downside is that my adult children—who already refuse to move out of home—have now permanently barricaded themselves in the lounge room like squatters, meaning I have to physically fight off my own offspring just to watch my KDramas.10/10.

The resolution on this screen is absolutely awesome. Every scene is crystal clear, and the sheer size of the display makes total immersion a cinch. It genuinely feels like bringing the commercial theater experience right into your living room.
Incredible Built-In Sound
The biggest surprise is the audio. The way the sound travels and bounces around the room is incredible. It completely fills the space, making it almost unnecessary to buy an additional surround sound system or expensive soundbar.
Flawless Smart Features
Smart features can sometimes be clunky, but this TV has zero issues with my Alexa. It integrated into my smart home instantly and works flawlessly every single time.
The Ultimate Verdict
More than anything, this TV has brought my family closer together. My kids absolutely enjoy our cinema nights when they come over to spend time with their dad. Seeing their faces light up during movie nights makes this worth every single penny. Highly recommended!

title: Viewing Experience
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Upgrading from a 55-inch to the Samsung Neo QLED 75-inch has been an absolute game changer for our home. The difference in size alone makes everything feel so much more immersive for movies, sport, even everyday TV just feel bigger and more cinematic.

The picture quality is incredible. The brightness, contrast, and colour are on another level, and the detail is so sharp it almost feels 3D at times. Dark scenes look deep and rich, while bright scenes really pop without being overwhelming.. The sound is also much better than expected for a flat-screen TV, giving a more surround-like feel without needing a sound bar.

Overall, this upgrade has completely transformed our viewing experience. If you're thinking about going bigger, I’d absolutely recommend it — the jump from 55” to 75” is 100% worth it.

title: Aussie oldies review OLED smart TV
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] We bought this Samsung OLED TV thinking we’d just be upgrading from “pretty good” to “a bit better.” Turns out we’ve accidentally brought a cinema into the lounge room.

We’re definitely not tech experts. If the remote has more than six buttons, we start looking for the grandkids. But this TV was surprisingly easy to set up, and even we had it working without threatening to throw the instructions out the window.

The picture is incredible. The blacks are actually black instead of that washed-out grey our old TV specialised in. Colours are so sharp we’ve caught ourselves saying, “I don’t remember that actor having so many wrinkles!” Sport looks fantastic too—you can almost see the grass stains.

The sound is much better than we expected, although it still can’t drown out the neighbour mowing the lawn halfway through the footy.

The smart features are great once you remember which button gets you back to normal TV. 

Is it cheap? No. But neither are decent tyres or a good mattress, and you use this every day. We’ve got absolutely no regrets.

From two everyday Aussies who still occasionally call the remote “the clicker,” we’d happily recommend a Samsung OLED. Just be warned—you’ll spend the first week watching nature documentaries because they look so good, even if you’ve never cared about penguins before.

Five stars from us. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

title: Incredible Picture and Amazing Value
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I bought this 65” OLED S85H 4K Samsung Vision AI TV a few weeks ago and have been really impressed overall. The brightness is excellent for an OLED panel, and HDR content looks vibrant without washing out darker scenes. Contrast is where this TV really stands out — blacks are deep and true, making movies and shows look incredibly cinematic, especially in a dark room.

The 4K resolution is super sharp, and streaming content from Netflix, YouTube, and gaming consoles looks detailed and clean. Even older content upscales surprisingly well. Viewing angles are also great since the picture quality stays consistent even when watching from the side, which is perfect for family movie nights or sports gatherings.

The refresh rate and motion handling are smooth for gaming and fast-action sports. Gameplay feels responsive with minimal blur, and movies run smoothly without noticeable stuttering. Samsung’s smart features and AI enhancements also make navigating apps and adjusting picture settings simple and quick.

What really surprised me most is the value for money. In my opinion, this TV is top of the range for the price. You get premium OLED picture quality, excellent gaming performance, smart features, and a sleek design without paying the extreme prices of some competing models.

Overall, this TV delivers premium picture quality, smooth performance, and outstanding value. I’d definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a high-end OLED TV with impressive brightness, contrast, resolution, viewing angles, refresh performance, and great bang for the buck.

title: 83" of Absolute Display Perfection on the Wall
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The Star of the Show: Samsung S90H 83"

​Getting an 83-inch panel up on the wall is a serious project, but once mounted, it completely anchors the room. More importantly, the display performance matches the massive physical presence.

​Contrast: The black levels are absolute zero. Dark scenes are deep and precise, creating an incredible contrast ratio where bright highlights pop without any haloing or light bleed into the shadows.

​Brightness: It easily handles ambient daylight. The panel pushes serious luminance, keeping colors vibrant and specular HDR highlights crisp even in a bright room.

​Uniformity: Screen uniformity on a panel this huge can be a gamble, but this screen is flawless. Zero "dirty screen effect" (DSE), no banding, and perfectly even color distribution edge-to-edge during wide panning shots.

​Upscaling: The onboard picture engine does heavy lifting. Compressed 1080p streaming content is sharpened intelligently without looking over-processed, bringing older feeds impressively close to native 4K quality.

​Responsiveness: Motion processing is rock-solid and the pixel response time is instantaneous. Menu navigation is snappy, and high-frame-rate content feels fluid with zero noticeable input lag or motion blur.

​The Setup Context
​I ran a single-cable eARC connection down to a Samsung Q990H soundbar to complete the audio side of the build. It syncs automatically, handles the high-bitrate audio formats, and keeps the entire wall-mounted setup visually minimal with zero wire clutter.

​Verdict:
Flagship picture quality, flawless panel uniformity, and elite processing. If you're wall-mounting an 83-inch TV, this is the gold standard.

title: Surprisingly Gentle for my first OLED.
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] My 77" model is from Australia so I get the QD-OLED version and this is my first OLED.
The colors and picture are so stunning they could sell tickets at the door. I didn’t realize OLEDs could beam that bright until my eyeballs threatened to unionize on the very first night, forcing me to dial back my HDR bravado. The AI upscaling is pure wizardry, transforming dusty old SD footage into something so crisp that, with my glasses on, it’s basically nostalgia strutting around in 4K cosplay. Some folks talk about contrast and raised blacks or lighter tones from the matte finish in daylight, but I haven’t noticed a thing, if anything, the matte finish moonlights as my personal anti-glare bodyguard.

My only hiccups so far have been:  
1. eARC decided to play hard to get with my Denon AVR, stubbornly sending PCM 2.0 no matter what I streamed or played. Then, as if by magic, it suddenly decided to behave, and now it’s all sunshine and surround sound.  
2. The Xbox GamePass app insists on AI Upscaling mode, because if I dare use Low Latency mode, it treats me to a thrilling black screen audio drama instead of an actual game.

title: Excellent OLED TV with impressive picture quality
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I've been extremely happy with the Samsung QA65S90H. The OLED panel delivers outstanding picture quality, with deep blacks, vibrant colours and excellent contrast that make movies, sports and streaming content look fantastic. The 4K upscaling does a great job with lower-resolution content, and the overall image is sharp and detailed.

One feature I particularly appreciate is how well the screen handles reflections, making it much easier to watch during the day in a bright room. The smart TV interface is responsive and easy to navigate, with all the major streaming apps available. Gaming performance has also been excellent thanks to the smooth motion and low input lag.

The design is sleek and modern, and the TV looks great mounted on the wall or on its stand. Setup was straightforward, and the sound quality is surprisingly good for a slim TV, although a soundbar would still enhance the experience.

Overall, the QA65S90H offers a premium viewing experience with excellent picture quality, strong smart features and great gaming performance. I would happily recommend it to anyone looking for a high-quality OLED TV.

title: Shrinkflation
body:
To be honest, this TV isn't exactly the thing it was always marketed to be. I bought a 2024 version and it was cheaper and better in every way. Unfortunately, the bloated software misbehaved and would just turn itself off - even after a factory reset. 

I was upsold this 2026 version instead and while it will display the art in art mode just fine, the one cable to power it and provide all the inputs no longer exists. Meaning, you have wires coming out the back like a regular TV. You also have a terrible viewing angle, like a normal TV (actually, perhaps worse). The OS is horrible and I wish companies would stop adding their own horrible versions of what they think a TV OS should be because sorry Samsung, you're not good at it. The TV also has what only I can describe as JPG artifacts appearing on the screen (and no, it's not my connection) making it seem like the TV is working double duty trying to process something that doesn't need processing. More AI junk? Who knows. The tradeoff of it being pretty darn thin - which is a plus, the sound is horrible but, who buys a TV like this and doesn't consider getting better sound via at least a sound bar anyways?

This TV is a clear indication that shrinkflation exists. I feel like I am getting less but paying far more compared to the previous years. Yes the TV turns on and yes, it has an anti-glair coating but thats all I can say for this thing. 

Wish they would have kept what was good about the "The Frame" line and continued it on through to make it even better than that previous years.

title: Great display, lacking full features/connectivity
body:
We bought this TV because of it being a 4K 144Hz matte screen with the Art mode. We love how bright or how dim we can make the image, and displaying our own photos. We also wanted the aesthetic of having a TV that was very unobtrusive, and the near-flush mounting plus available decorative frames do that. 

However, as someone looking for a "professional" TV install, this TV's lack of hardwire connection between display and connection box is very disappointing. Previous The Frame TV's had at least a connection kit available separately, this one does not. Which also means "hiding the box" is very limited, and EMI will be an issue, especially with higher resolution and framerate video. 

We also are not pleased that our 4K (and above) photos cannot be displayed edge-to-edge - you must have a mat - yet the subscription Art does not require the mat.

The sound quality from this is also very mediocre and "tinny," anyone looking for better sound will absolutely need a soundbar or AV reciever.

title: 🌟The Greatest Upgrade in History🌟
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] 🌟 RIP to My Optometrist and Audiologist: The Greatest Upgrade in History

We just replaced our ancient, 32-inch dinosaur of a TV with the 65-inch Neo QLED and matching soundbar, and our lives have officially changed.

For the last decade, watching a movie in our living room required the tactical precision of a bomb squad. My glasses had to be perfectly wiped, my chair had to be exactly four feet from the screen, and my hearing aids were turned up so high I could hear my neighbour's cat changing its mind in the next house over.

Not anymore.

With this new 65-inch beast, the glasses are officially OFF. The picture is so crisp, bright, and staggeringly massive that I can see the individual pores on a football player's face from the kitchen. I'm pretty sure the local airport is using my living room as a backup runway flare.

And the soundbar - S-Series All-in-one Soundbar HW-S60D with 5.0ch? Hearing aids: DEACTIVATED. Turned them straight off. The bass from this thing doesn’t just enter your ears; it rattles your fillings and rearranges your internal organs. I watched an action movie last night and felt the explosions in my shins. For the first time in years, I can actually understand the whispered dialogue in gritty dramas without needing subtitles or blasting the volume to maximum.

Even the remote control is a hyperactive masterpiece. Our old TV remote required a literal prayer ritual, a hard point-and-shoot aim, and a thumb wrestling match just to change the channel. This new remote is so lightning-fast and responsive that if I even blink near the directional pad, it has already skipped three episodes of my show. It responds faster than my own reflexes.

Hubby says it’s "too big for the room", but I can't hear them over the glorious, cinematic rumble of my new setup.  The only downside is that my adult children—who already refuse to move out of home—have now permanently barricaded themselves in the lounge room like squatters, meaning I have to physically fight off my own offspring just to watch my KDramas.10/10.

body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I bought this TV to upgrade our family entertainment, and it has exceeded every expectation. If you are on the fence, just buy it.

The resolution on this screen is absolutely awesome. Every scene is crystal clear, and the sheer size of the display makes total immersion a cinch. It genuinely feels like bringing the commercial theater experience right into your living room.
Incredible Built-In Sound
The biggest surprise is the audio. The way the sound travels and bounces around the room is incredible. It completely fills the space, making it almost unnecessary to buy an additional surround sound system or expensive soundbar.
Flawless Smart Features
Smart features can sometimes be clunky, but this TV has zero issues with my Alexa. It integrated into my smart home instantly and works flawlessly every single time.
The Ultimate Verdict
More than anything, this TV has brought my family closer together. My kids absolutely enjoy our cinema nights when they come over to spend time with their dad. Seeing their faces light up during movie nights makes this worth every single penny. Highly recommended!

title: Viewing Experience
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Upgrading from a 55-inch to the Samsung Neo QLED 75-inch has been an absolute game changer for our home. The difference in size alone makes everything feel so much more immersive for movies, sport, even everyday TV just feel bigger and more cinematic.

The picture quality is incredible. The brightness, contrast, and colour are on another level, and the detail is so sharp it almost feels 3D at times. Dark scenes look deep and rich, while bright scenes really pop without being overwhelming.. The sound is also much better than expected for a flat-screen TV, giving a more surround-like feel without needing a sound bar.

Overall, this upgrade has completely transformed our viewing experience. If you're thinking about going bigger, I’d absolutely recommend it — the jump from 55” to 75” is 100% worth it.

title: Aussie oldies review OLED smart TV
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] We bought this Samsung OLED TV thinking we’d just be upgrading from “pretty good” to “a bit better.” Turns out we’ve accidentally brought a cinema into the lounge room.

We’re definitely not tech experts. If the remote has more than six buttons, we start looking for the grandkids. But this TV was surprisingly easy to set up, and even we had it working without threatening to throw the instructions out the window.

The picture is incredible. The blacks are actually black instead of that washed-out grey our old TV specialised in. Colours are so sharp we’ve caught ourselves saying, “I don’t remember that actor having so many wrinkles!” Sport looks fantastic too—you can almost see the grass stains.

The sound is much better than we expected, although it still can’t drown out the neighbour mowing the lawn halfway through the footy.

The smart features are great once you remember which button gets you back to normal TV. 

Is it cheap? No. But neither are decent tyres or a good mattress, and you use this every day. We’ve got absolutely no regrets.

From two everyday Aussies who still occasionally call the remote “the clicker,” we’d happily recommend a Samsung OLED. Just be warned—you’ll spend the first week watching nature documentaries because they look so good, even if you’ve never cared about penguins before.

Five stars from us. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

title: 83" of Absolute Display Perfection on the Wall
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The Star of the Show: Samsung S90H 83"

​Getting an 83-inch panel up on the wall is a serious project, but once mounted, it completely anchors the room. More importantly, the display performance matches the massive physical presence.

​Contrast: The black levels are absolute zero. Dark scenes are deep and precise, creating an incredible contrast ratio where bright highlights pop without any haloing or light bleed into the shadows.

​Brightness: It easily handles ambient daylight. The panel pushes serious luminance, keeping colors vibrant and specular HDR highlights crisp even in a bright room.

​Uniformity: Screen uniformity on a panel this huge can be a gamble, but this screen is flawless. Zero "dirty screen effect" (DSE), no banding, and perfectly even color distribution edge-to-edge during wide panning shots.

​Upscaling: The onboard picture engine does heavy lifting. Compressed 1080p streaming content is sharpened intelligently without looking over-processed, bringing older feeds impressively close to native 4K quality.

​Responsiveness: Motion processing is rock-solid and the pixel response time is instantaneous. Menu navigation is snappy, and high-frame-rate content feels fluid with zero noticeable input lag or motion blur.

​The Setup Context
​I ran a single-cable eARC connection down to a Samsung Q990H soundbar to complete the audio side of the build. It syncs automatically, handles the high-bitrate audio formats, and keeps the entire wall-mounted setup visually minimal with zero wire clutter.

​Verdict:
Flagship picture quality, flawless panel uniformity, and elite processing. If you're wall-mounting an 83-inch TV, this is the gold standard.

title: Surprisingly Gentle for my first OLED.
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] My 77" model is from Australia so I get the QD-OLED version and this is my first OLED.
The colors and picture are so stunning they could sell tickets at the door. I didn’t realize OLEDs could beam that bright until my eyeballs threatened to unionize on the very first night, forcing me to dial back my HDR bravado. The AI upscaling is pure wizardry, transforming dusty old SD footage into something so crisp that, with my glasses on, it’s basically nostalgia strutting around in 4K cosplay. Some folks talk about contrast and raised blacks or lighter tones from the matte finish in daylight, but I haven’t noticed a thing, if anything, the matte finish moonlights as my personal anti-glare bodyguard.

My only hiccups so far have been:  
1. eARC decided to play hard to get with my Denon AVR, stubbornly sending PCM 2.0 no matter what I streamed or played. Then, as if by magic, it suddenly decided to behave, and now it’s all sunshine and surround sound.  
2. The Xbox GamePass app insists on AI Upscaling mode, because if I dare use Low Latency mode, it treats me to a thrilling black screen audio drama instead of an actual game.

title: Excellent OLED TV with impressive picture quality
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I've been extremely happy with the Samsung QA65S90H. The OLED panel delivers outstanding picture quality, with deep blacks, vibrant colours and excellent contrast that make movies, sports and streaming content look fantastic. The 4K upscaling does a great job with lower-resolution content, and the overall image is sharp and detailed.

One feature I particularly appreciate is how well the screen handles reflections, making it much easier to watch during the day in a bright room. The smart TV interface is responsive and easy to navigate, with all the major streaming apps available. Gaming performance has also been excellent thanks to the smooth motion and low input lag.

The design is sleek and modern, and the TV looks great mounted on the wall or on its stand. Setup was straightforward, and the sound quality is surprisingly good for a slim TV, although a soundbar would still enhance the experience.

Overall, the QA65S90H offers a premium viewing experience with excellent picture quality, strong smart features and great gaming performance. I would happily recommend it to anyone looking for a high-quality OLED TV.

title: Art for Art’s Sake
body: For my husband’s 70th birthday, I decided to surprise him with The Frame Art Tv. He is quite the homebody and I figured it would be the perfect gift where he may enjoy watching his favorite martial arts movies and geopolitical news on a 50 inch tv. I t had the Art Tv - Frame in mind because having access to art works from around the world museums would certainly provide some pleasure to me as well. My husband was overwhelmed with awe and delight when he unwrapped the said Samsung Tv. I believe it will be difficult to tear him away from the screen even for a short holiday. Truth be told, I take immense pleasure every morning as I sit in front of my new-found love ( The Frame) and select my art work I will contemplate and meditate in front of with my early morning espresso . Sheer enchantment and moments of bliss as I happily view the works available in museums worldwide and artwork from all corners of the planet. In the past , I would frequently pay a visit to the Artotheque , an art library whereby as a member, I would support local artists and rent paintings monthly to display on my wall in my apartment. Today, beautiful art is available to me at the touch of a button , thanks to the genius that is the Art Tv , the Frame from Samsung. I can’t fathom the luck and luxury I have access to right in my sacred little haven I call home. I can’t wait until my husband’s next landmark birthday! Thank you Samsung !

title: The Perfect "Incognito" TV for a Man Cave
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] ​I recently added the Samsung Frame to my setup, and it has completely changed the vibe of the room. If you are looking for something that balances high-end tech with a clean, sophisticated look, this is it.
​The Highlights:
​The Matte Finish: This is the absolute "killer feature." The anti-glare properties are superb; there’s zero reflection from overhead lights or windows. It doesn't look like a screen—it looks like a high-quality physical print.
​Man Cave Aesthetic: I wanted a space that didn't just look like a wall of black glass when the TV was off. Being able to rotate through high-res art and photography turns the room into a gallery. It adds a level of class that a standard TV just can't match.
​Form Meets Function: While the art mode is the star, it’s still a fantastic display for actual watching. Whether it’s sports or a movie, the 4K clarity is sharp, and the colors are vibrant.
​Bottom Line:
It’s the best of both worlds. You get a stunning piece of decor that blends into your man cave perfectly, but with the push of a button, you’ve got a high-performance TV. If you value aesthetics as much as performance, the Frame is in a league of its own.

title: Unbelievable clarity in both modes
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Samsung is an addiction this is the 4th Samsung TV we have in our house all quality even as they are getting older. The New Frame unexpectedly out preforms them all clarity there is no competition it definitely out preforms here and so many other areas, the interface between the user and TV enables smooth navigation, with the intuitive menus for viewing from a distance.
As a tradesmen use to hanging TVs and also pictures this was sure to be a breeze. Template so easy to piece together find the correct height and find the wall studs and drill after checking levels. 
Oh no! How did I get it so wrong after checking with 3 spirit-levels. Remeasure, all level however to the eye it seemed to be at an angle. The angle proved to be my cornices they are not level, so have faith in Samsungs Template it is correct, you won’t go wrong proof Samsung gets every detail correct ensuring your viewing pleasure.
Once the TV was on the slime wall mount, so easy to place on with one other person, it actually is level. 
The TV itself was bought for the picture addition which again is unbelievably faultless, the setup was hassle free and was up and running within 15 to 20 mins. The matt finish of the screen does what it says no interference from surrounding shadows, and brightness from objects that would normally be reflected on screen, brilliant. The viewing of the TV draws you in peacefully with never before seen crispness with no feathering during movements during sports or movie watching. What else can you say Samsung the frame is so enjoyable to use not to mention a money saver for your electric bill. The solar remote really, why hasn’t anyone thought of that before no more fumbling to change batteries, thank you.

title: Sharper and more coloful!
body: Our 15 year old 55" TV gave up the ghost last month. Well actually it suddenly got multiple ghosts - green ones!. So we opted for the Samsung Frame 65". What an amazing difference! We sit about 8 feet from our screen, so we didn't know if we'd see much difference in sharpness. But everything is so much crisper and with richer colors. Art Mode is great. We paid extra so that we would have a bigger selection. And almost right away I downloaded the SmartThings app so that I could transfer photos to the Frame. What an impact to see them at that size! There are a few things you need to do to get the best out of the Frame. First, you have to ask your internet provider to provide you a higher speed of data transfer. We were getting 50 GB but have had that increased to  150. You can expect a price increase with the new service. 4K video (UHD) requires around 4 x as much data per second as 2K (HD).

title: Beautiful TV, One Connect Box pairing failure
body:
Samsung The Frame Pro 2025 65". Gorgeous matte display, slim profile and Art Mode are standout features.

Unfortunately my unit developed an early Wireless One Connect Box issue — stuck in a pairing loop due to a confirmed hardware fault. For a premium TV, connection reliability is essential, as this single box is a single point of failure.

Other drawbacks: the UI feels sluggish when navigating menus, and there are ads in the interface — unexpected in a high-end model. It’s a bit like buying a luxury car and finding billboard ads on the dashboard screen - tacky!

If Samsung improves One Connect Box reliability, menu responsiveness, and decides whether it wants to be a technology leader focused on premium product experience or an ad platform monetising its customers, this could be an exceptional product.

Pros: Art Mode, matte screen, slim design, colour/contrast
Cons: One Connect Box pairing loop, UI lag, ads in interface

I was also incredibly impressed by the separated One Connect Box, which keeps all the cables neatly organized away from the TV, resulting in a wonderfully clean setup.

It feels sluggish, constantly loading elements, and frustratingly insists on re-optimizing image quality every time a new HDMI device is plugged in, instead of processing these adjustments in the background and applying them seamlessly. title: Shrinkflation
body:
To be honest, this TV isn't exactly the thing it was always marketed to be. I bought a 2024 version and it was cheaper and better in every way. Unfortunately, the bloated software misbehaved and would just turn itself off - even after a factory reset. 

I was upsold this 2026 version instead and while it will display the art in art mode just fine, the one cable to power it and provide all the inputs no longer exists. Meaning, you have wires coming out the back like a regular TV. You also have a terrible viewing angle, like a normal TV (actually, perhaps worse). The OS is horrible and I wish companies would stop adding their own horrible versions of what they think a TV OS should be because sorry Samsung, you're not good at it. The TV also has what only I can describe as JPG artifacts appearing on the screen (and no, it's not my connection) making it seem like the TV is working double duty trying to process something that doesn't need processing. More AI junk? Who knows. The tradeoff of it being pretty darn thin - which is a plus, the sound is horrible but, who buys a TV like this and doesn't consider getting better sound via at least a sound bar anyways?

This TV is a clear indication that shrinkflation exists. I feel like I am getting less but paying far more compared to the previous years. Yes the TV turns on and yes, it has an anti-glair coating but thats all I can say for this thing. 

Wish they would have kept what was good about the "The Frame" line and continued it on through to make it even better than that previous years.

body:

Gaming: Annoying sometimes. I had to disable game mode due to the screen blacking out and loading and it rendered, causing many interruptions to online performance and quick reaction moments.

Interface: I disabled as much as I could. Regardless of configuring the settings properly, the television refused to comply and would auto-run apps, shows, etc. I am extremely tech literate, worked with customer support, reset the tv and settings, and it would still auto-run apps that I have never opened and used myself, thus my statement of not wanting smart features on future tvs. 

Overall - mid tier tv. Variety of features available, great quality image, but frustrating to use for what I'd like out of it.

title: Great display, lacking full features/connectivity
body:
We bought this TV because of it being a 4K 144Hz matte screen with the Art mode. We love how bright or how dim we can make the image, and displaying our own photos. We also wanted the aesthetic of having a TV that was very unobtrusive, and the near-flush mounting plus available decorative frames do that. 

However, as someone looking for a "professional" TV install, this TV's lack of hardwire connection between display and connection box is very disappointing. Previous The Frame TV's had at least a connection kit available separately, this one does not. Which also means "hiding the box" is very limited, and EMI will be an issue, especially with higher resolution and framerate video. 

We also are not pleased that our 4K (and above) photos cannot be displayed edge-to-edge - you must have a mat - yet the subscription Art does not require the mat.

The sound quality from this is also very mediocre and "tinny," anyone looking for better sound will absolutely need a soundbar or AV reciever.

title: 🌟The Greatest Upgrade in History🌟
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] 🌟 RIP to My Optometrist and Audiologist: The Greatest Upgrade in History

We just replaced our ancient, 32-inch dinosaur of a TV with the 65-inch Neo QLED and matching soundbar, and our lives have officially changed.

For the last decade, watching a movie in our living room required the tactical precision of a bomb squad. My glasses had to be perfectly wiped, my chair had to be exactly four feet from the screen, and my hearing aids were turned up so high I could hear my neighbour's cat changing its mind in the next house over.

Not anymore.

With this new 65-inch beast, the glasses are officially OFF. The picture is so crisp, bright, and staggeringly massive that I can see the individual pores on a football player's face from the kitchen. I'm pretty sure the local airport is using my living room as a backup runway flare.

And the soundbar - S-Series All-in-one Soundbar HW-S60D with 5.0ch? Hearing aids: DEACTIVATED. Turned them straight off. The bass from this thing doesn’t just enter your ears; it rattles your fillings and rearranges your internal organs. I watched an action movie last night and felt the explosions in my shins. For the first time in years, I can actually understand the whispered dialogue in gritty dramas without needing subtitles or blasting the volume to maximum.

Even the remote control is a hyperactive masterpiece. Our old TV remote required a literal prayer ritual, a hard point-and-shoot aim, and a thumb wrestling match just to change the channel. This new remote is so lightning-fast and responsive that if I even blink near the directional pad, it has already skipped three episodes of my show. It responds faster than my own reflexes.

Hubby says it’s "too big for the room", but I can't hear them over the glorious, cinematic rumble of my new setup.  The only downside is that my adult children—who already refuse to move out of home—have now permanently barricaded themselves in the lounge room like squatters, meaning I have to physically fight off my own offspring just to watch my KDramas.10/10.

Incredible Built-In Sound
The biggest surprise is the audio. The way the sound travels and bounces around the room is incredible. It completely fills the space, making it almost unnecessary to buy an additional surround sound system or expensive soundbar.
Flawless Smart Features
Smart features can sometimes be clunky, but this TV has zero issues with my Alexa. It integrated into my smart home instantly and works flawlessly every single time.
The Ultimate Verdict
More than anything, this TV has brought my family closer together. My kids absolutely enjoy our cinema nights when they come over to spend time with their dad. Seeing their faces light up during movie nights makes this worth every single penny. Highly recommended!

body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Upgrading from a 55-inch to the Samsung Neo QLED 75-inch has been an absolute game changer for our home. The difference in size alone makes everything feel so much more immersive for movies, sport, even everyday TV just feel bigger and more cinematic.

The picture quality is incredible. The brightness, contrast, and colour are on another level, and the detail is so sharp it almost feels 3D at times. Dark scenes look deep and rich, while bright scenes really pop without being overwhelming.. The sound is also much better than expected for a flat-screen TV, giving a more surround-like feel without needing a sound bar.

Overall, this upgrade has completely transformed our viewing experience. If you're thinking about going bigger, I’d absolutely recommend it — the jump from 55” to 75” is 100% worth it.

body:

The picture quality is incredible—the OLED display produces rich, vibrant colours, deep blacks, and amazing detail that make everything from movies to travel documentaries look stunning.

title: Aussie oldies review OLED smart TV
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] We bought this Samsung OLED TV thinking we’d just be upgrading from “pretty good” to “a bit better.” Turns out we’ve accidentally brought a cinema into the lounge room.

We’re definitely not tech experts. If the remote has more than six buttons, we start looking for the grandkids. But this TV was surprisingly easy to set up, and even we had it working without threatening to throw the instructions out the window.

The picture is incredible. The blacks are actually black instead of that washed-out grey our old TV specialised in. Colours are so sharp we’ve caught ourselves saying, “I don’t remember that actor having so many wrinkles!” Sport looks fantastic too—you can almost see the grass stains.

The sound is much better than we expected, although it still can’t drown out the neighbour mowing the lawn halfway through the footy.

The smart features are great once you remember which button gets you back to normal TV. 

Is it cheap? No. But neither are decent tyres or a good mattress, and you use this every day. We’ve got absolutely no regrets.

From two everyday Aussies who still occasionally call the remote “the clicker,” we’d happily recommend a Samsung OLED. Just be warned—you’ll spend the first week watching nature documentaries because they look so good, even if you’ve never cared about penguins before.

Five stars from us. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

title: 83" of Absolute Display Perfection on the Wall
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The Star of the Show: Samsung S90H 83"

​Getting an 83-inch panel up on the wall is a serious project, but once mounted, it completely anchors the room. More importantly, the display performance matches the massive physical presence.

​Contrast: The black levels are absolute zero. Dark scenes are deep and precise, creating an incredible contrast ratio where bright highlights pop without any haloing or light bleed into the shadows.

​Brightness: It easily handles ambient daylight. The panel pushes serious luminance, keeping colors vibrant and specular HDR highlights crisp even in a bright room.

​Uniformity: Screen uniformity on a panel this huge can be a gamble, but this screen is flawless. Zero "dirty screen effect" (DSE), no banding, and perfectly even color distribution edge-to-edge during wide panning shots.

​Upscaling: The onboard picture engine does heavy lifting. Compressed 1080p streaming content is sharpened intelligently without looking over-processed, bringing older feeds impressively close to native 4K quality.

​Responsiveness: Motion processing is rock-solid and the pixel response time is instantaneous. Menu navigation is snappy, and high-frame-rate content feels fluid with zero noticeable input lag or motion blur.

​The Setup Context
​I ran a single-cable eARC connection down to a Samsung Q990H soundbar to complete the audio side of the build. It syncs automatically, handles the high-bitrate audio formats, and keeps the entire wall-mounted setup visually minimal with zero wire clutter.

​Verdict:
Flagship picture quality, flawless panel uniformity, and elite processing. If you're wall-mounting an 83-inch TV, this is the gold standard.

title: Surprisingly Gentle for my first OLED.
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] My 77" model is from Australia so I get the QD-OLED version and this is my first OLED.
The colors and picture are so stunning they could sell tickets at the door. I didn’t realize OLEDs could beam that bright until my eyeballs threatened to unionize on the very first night, forcing me to dial back my HDR bravado. The AI upscaling is pure wizardry, transforming dusty old SD footage into something so crisp that, with my glasses on, it’s basically nostalgia strutting around in 4K cosplay. Some folks talk about contrast and raised blacks or lighter tones from the matte finish in daylight, but I haven’t noticed a thing, if anything, the matte finish moonlights as my personal anti-glare bodyguard.

My only hiccups so far have been:  
1. eARC decided to play hard to get with my Denon AVR, stubbornly sending PCM 2.0 no matter what I streamed or played. Then, as if by magic, it suddenly decided to behave, and now it’s all sunshine and surround sound.  
2. The Xbox GamePass app insists on AI Upscaling mode, because if I dare use Low Latency mode, it treats me to a thrilling black screen audio drama instead of an actual game.

title: Shrinkflation
body:
To be honest, this TV isn't exactly the thing it was always marketed to be. I bought a 2024 version and it was cheaper and better in every way. Unfortunately, the bloated software misbehaved and would just turn itself off - even after a factory reset. 

I was upsold this 2026 version instead and while it will display the art in art mode just fine, the one cable to power it and provide all the inputs no longer exists. Meaning, you have wires coming out the back like a regular TV. You also have a terrible viewing angle, like a normal TV (actually, perhaps worse). The OS is horrible and I wish companies would stop adding their own horrible versions of what they think a TV OS should be because sorry Samsung, you're not good at it. The TV also has what only I can describe as JPG artifacts appearing on the screen (and no, it's not my connection) making it seem like the TV is working double duty trying to process something that doesn't need processing. More AI junk? Who knows. The tradeoff of it being pretty darn thin - which is a plus, the sound is horrible but, who buys a TV like this and doesn't consider getting better sound via at least a sound bar anyways?

This TV is a clear indication that shrinkflation exists. I feel like I am getting less but paying far more compared to the previous years. Yes the TV turns on and yes, it has an anti-glair coating but thats all I can say for this thing. 

Wish they would have kept what was good about the "The Frame" line and continued it on through to make it even better than that previous years.

title: 🌟The Greatest Upgrade in History🌟
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] 🌟 RIP to My Optometrist and Audiologist: The Greatest Upgrade in History

We just replaced our ancient, 32-inch dinosaur of a TV with the 65-inch Neo QLED and matching soundbar, and our lives have officially changed.

For the last decade, watching a movie in our living room required the tactical precision of a bomb squad. My glasses had to be perfectly wiped, my chair had to be exactly four feet from the screen, and my hearing aids were turned up so high I could hear my neighbour's cat changing its mind in the next house over.

Not anymore.

With this new 65-inch beast, the glasses are officially OFF. The picture is so crisp, bright, and staggeringly massive that I can see the individual pores on a football player's face from the kitchen. I'm pretty sure the local airport is using my living room as a backup runway flare.

And the soundbar - S-Series All-in-one Soundbar HW-S60D with 5.0ch? Hearing aids: DEACTIVATED. Turned them straight off. The bass from this thing doesn’t just enter your ears; it rattles your fillings and rearranges your internal organs. I watched an action movie last night and felt the explosions in my shins. For the first time in years, I can actually understand the whispered dialogue in gritty dramas without needing subtitles or blasting the volume to maximum.

Even the remote control is a hyperactive masterpiece. Our old TV remote required a literal prayer ritual, a hard point-and-shoot aim, and a thumb wrestling match just to change the channel. This new remote is so lightning-fast and responsive that if I even blink near the directional pad, it has already skipped three episodes of my show. It responds faster than my own reflexes.

Hubby says it’s "too big for the room", but I can't hear them over the glorious, cinematic rumble of my new setup.  The only downside is that my adult children—who already refuse to move out of home—have now permanently barricaded themselves in the lounge room like squatters, meaning I have to physically fight off my own offspring just to watch my KDramas.10/10.

title: Aussie oldies review OLED smart TV
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] We bought this Samsung OLED TV thinking we’d just be upgrading from “pretty good” to “a bit better.” Turns out we’ve accidentally brought a cinema into the lounge room.

We’re definitely not tech experts. If the remote has more than six buttons, we start looking for the grandkids. But this TV was surprisingly easy to set up, and even we had it working without threatening to throw the instructions out the window.

The picture is incredible. The blacks are actually black instead of that washed-out grey our old TV specialised in. Colours are so sharp we’ve caught ourselves saying, “I don’t remember that actor having so many wrinkles!” Sport looks fantastic too—you can almost see the grass stains.

The sound is much better than we expected, although it still can’t drown out the neighbour mowing the lawn halfway through the footy.

The smart features are great once you remember which button gets you back to normal TV. 

Is it cheap? No. But neither are decent tyres or a good mattress, and you use this every day. We’ve got absolutely no regrets.

From two everyday Aussies who still occasionally call the remote “the clicker,” we’d happily recommend a Samsung OLED. Just be warned—you’ll spend the first week watching nature documentaries because they look so good, even if you’ve never cared about penguins before.

Five stars from us. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

title: Incredible Picture and Amazing Value
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I bought this 65” OLED S85H 4K Samsung Vision AI TV a few weeks ago and have been really impressed overall. The brightness is excellent for an OLED panel, and HDR content looks vibrant without washing out darker scenes. Contrast is where this TV really stands out — blacks are deep and true, making movies and shows look incredibly cinematic, especially in a dark room.

The 4K resolution is super sharp, and streaming content from Netflix, YouTube, and gaming consoles looks detailed and clean. Even older content upscales surprisingly well. Viewing angles are also great since the picture quality stays consistent even when watching from the side, which is perfect for family movie nights or sports gatherings.

The refresh rate and motion handling are smooth for gaming and fast-action sports. Gameplay feels responsive with minimal blur, and movies run smoothly without noticeable stuttering. Samsung’s smart features and AI enhancements also make navigating apps and adjusting picture settings simple and quick.

What really surprised me most is the value for money. In my opinion, this TV is top of the range for the price. You get premium OLED picture quality, excellent gaming performance, smart features, and a sleek design without paying the extreme prices of some competing models.

Overall, this TV delivers premium picture quality, smooth performance, and outstanding value. I’d definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a high-end OLED TV with impressive brightness, contrast, resolution, viewing angles, refresh performance, and great bang for the buck.

title: 83" of Absolute Display Perfection on the Wall
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The Star of the Show: Samsung S90H 83"

​Getting an 83-inch panel up on the wall is a serious project, but once mounted, it completely anchors the room. More importantly, the display performance matches the massive physical presence.

​Contrast: The black levels are absolute zero. Dark scenes are deep and precise, creating an incredible contrast ratio where bright highlights pop without any haloing or light bleed into the shadows.

​Brightness: It easily handles ambient daylight. The panel pushes serious luminance, keeping colors vibrant and specular HDR highlights crisp even in a bright room.

​Uniformity: Screen uniformity on a panel this huge can be a gamble, but this screen is flawless. Zero "dirty screen effect" (DSE), no banding, and perfectly even color distribution edge-to-edge during wide panning shots.

​Upscaling: The onboard picture engine does heavy lifting. Compressed 1080p streaming content is sharpened intelligently without looking over-processed, bringing older feeds impressively close to native 4K quality.

​Responsiveness: Motion processing is rock-solid and the pixel response time is instantaneous. Menu navigation is snappy, and high-frame-rate content feels fluid with zero noticeable input lag or motion blur.

​The Setup Context
​I ran a single-cable eARC connection down to a Samsung Q990H soundbar to complete the audio side of the build. It syncs automatically, handles the high-bitrate audio formats, and keeps the entire wall-mounted setup visually minimal with zero wire clutter.

​Verdict:
Flagship picture quality, flawless panel uniformity, and elite processing. If you're wall-mounting an 83-inch TV, this is the gold standard.

title: Surprisingly Gentle for my first OLED.
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] My 77" model is from Australia so I get the QD-OLED version and this is my first OLED.
The colors and picture are so stunning they could sell tickets at the door. I didn’t realize OLEDs could beam that bright until my eyeballs threatened to unionize on the very first night, forcing me to dial back my HDR bravado. The AI upscaling is pure wizardry, transforming dusty old SD footage into something so crisp that, with my glasses on, it’s basically nostalgia strutting around in 4K cosplay. Some folks talk about contrast and raised blacks or lighter tones from the matte finish in daylight, but I haven’t noticed a thing, if anything, the matte finish moonlights as my personal anti-glare bodyguard.

My only hiccups so far have been:  
1. eARC decided to play hard to get with my Denon AVR, stubbornly sending PCM 2.0 no matter what I streamed or played. Then, as if by magic, it suddenly decided to behave, and now it’s all sunshine and surround sound.  
2. The Xbox GamePass app insists on AI Upscaling mode, because if I dare use Low Latency mode, it treats me to a thrilling black screen audio drama instead of an actual game.

title: Excellent OLED TV with impressive picture quality
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I've been extremely happy with the Samsung QA65S90H. The OLED panel delivers outstanding picture quality, with deep blacks, vibrant colours and excellent contrast that make movies, sports and streaming content look fantastic. The 4K upscaling does a great job with lower-resolution content, and the overall image is sharp and detailed.

One feature I particularly appreciate is how well the screen handles reflections, making it much easier to watch during the day in a bright room. The smart TV interface is responsive and easy to navigate, with all the major streaming apps available. Gaming performance has also been excellent thanks to the smooth motion and low input lag.

The design is sleek and modern, and the TV looks great mounted on the wall or on its stand. Setup was straightforward, and the sound quality is surprisingly good for a slim TV, although a soundbar would still enhance the experience.

Overall, the QA65S90H offers a premium viewing experience with excellent picture quality, strong smart features and great gaming performance. I would happily recommend it to anyone looking for a high-quality OLED TV.

title: Aussie oldies review OLED smart TV
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] We bought this Samsung OLED TV thinking we’d just be upgrading from “pretty good” to “a bit better.” Turns out we’ve accidentally brought a cinema into the lounge room.

We’re definitely not tech experts. If the remote has more than six buttons, we start looking for the grandkids. But this TV was surprisingly easy to set up, and even we had it working without threatening to throw the instructions out the window.

The picture is incredible. The blacks are actually black instead of that washed-out grey our old TV specialised in. Colours are so sharp we’ve caught ourselves saying, “I don’t remember that actor having so many wrinkles!” Sport looks fantastic too—you can almost see the grass stains.

The sound is much better than we expected, although it still can’t drown out the neighbour mowing the lawn halfway through the footy.

The smart features are great once you remember which button gets you back to normal TV. 

Is it cheap? No. But neither are decent tyres or a good mattress, and you use this every day. We’ve got absolutely no regrets.

From two everyday Aussies who still occasionally call the remote “the clicker,” we’d happily recommend a Samsung OLED. Just be warned—you’ll spend the first week watching nature documentaries because they look so good, even if you’ve never cared about penguins before.

Five stars from us. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

title: Incredible Picture and Amazing Value
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I bought this 65” OLED S85H 4K Samsung Vision AI TV a few weeks ago and have been really impressed overall. The brightness is excellent for an OLED panel, and HDR content looks vibrant without washing out darker scenes. Contrast is where this TV really stands out — blacks are deep and true, making movies and shows look incredibly cinematic, especially in a dark room.

The 4K resolution is super sharp, and streaming content from Netflix, YouTube, and gaming consoles looks detailed and clean. Even older content upscales surprisingly well. Viewing angles are also great since the picture quality stays consistent even when watching from the side, which is perfect for family movie nights or sports gatherings.

The refresh rate and motion handling are smooth for gaming and fast-action sports. Gameplay feels responsive with minimal blur, and movies run smoothly without noticeable stuttering. Samsung’s smart features and AI enhancements also make navigating apps and adjusting picture settings simple and quick.

What really surprised me most is the value for money. In my opinion, this TV is top of the range for the price. You get premium OLED picture quality, excellent gaming performance, smart features, and a sleek design without paying the extreme prices of some competing models.

Overall, this TV delivers premium picture quality, smooth performance, and outstanding value. I’d definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a high-end OLED TV with impressive brightness, contrast, resolution, viewing angles, refresh performance, and great bang for the buck.

title: 83" of Absolute Display Perfection on the Wall
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The Star of the Show: Samsung S90H 83"

​Getting an 83-inch panel up on the wall is a serious project, but once mounted, it completely anchors the room. More importantly, the display performance matches the massive physical presence.

​Contrast: The black levels are absolute zero. Dark scenes are deep and precise, creating an incredible contrast ratio where bright highlights pop without any haloing or light bleed into the shadows.

​Brightness: It easily handles ambient daylight. The panel pushes serious luminance, keeping colors vibrant and specular HDR highlights crisp even in a bright room.

​Uniformity: Screen uniformity on a panel this huge can be a gamble, but this screen is flawless. Zero "dirty screen effect" (DSE), no banding, and perfectly even color distribution edge-to-edge during wide panning shots.

​Upscaling: The onboard picture engine does heavy lifting. Compressed 1080p streaming content is sharpened intelligently without looking over-processed, bringing older feeds impressively close to native 4K quality.

​Responsiveness: Motion processing is rock-solid and the pixel response time is instantaneous. Menu navigation is snappy, and high-frame-rate content feels fluid with zero noticeable input lag or motion blur.

​The Setup Context
​I ran a single-cable eARC connection down to a Samsung Q990H soundbar to complete the audio side of the build. It syncs automatically, handles the high-bitrate audio formats, and keeps the entire wall-mounted setup visually minimal with zero wire clutter.

​Verdict:
Flagship picture quality, flawless panel uniformity, and elite processing. If you're wall-mounting an 83-inch TV, this is the gold standard.

title: Surprisingly Gentle for my first OLED.
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] My 77" model is from Australia so I get the QD-OLED version and this is my first OLED.
The colors and picture are so stunning they could sell tickets at the door. I didn’t realize OLEDs could beam that bright until my eyeballs threatened to unionize on the very first night, forcing me to dial back my HDR bravado. The AI upscaling is pure wizardry, transforming dusty old SD footage into something so crisp that, with my glasses on, it’s basically nostalgia strutting around in 4K cosplay. Some folks talk about contrast and raised blacks or lighter tones from the matte finish in daylight, but I haven’t noticed a thing, if anything, the matte finish moonlights as my personal anti-glare bodyguard.

My only hiccups so far have been:  
1. eARC decided to play hard to get with my Denon AVR, stubbornly sending PCM 2.0 no matter what I streamed or played. Then, as if by magic, it suddenly decided to behave, and now it’s all sunshine and surround sound.  
2. The Xbox GamePass app insists on AI Upscaling mode, because if I dare use Low Latency mode, it treats me to a thrilling black screen audio drama instead of an actual game.

title: Shrinkflation
body:
To be honest, this TV isn't exactly the thing it was always marketed to be. I bought a 2024 version and it was cheaper and better in every way. Unfortunately, the bloated software misbehaved and would just turn itself off - even after a factory reset. 

I was upsold this 2026 version instead and while it will display the art in art mode just fine, the one cable to power it and provide all the inputs no longer exists. Meaning, you have wires coming out the back like a regular TV. You also have a terrible viewing angle, like a normal TV (actually, perhaps worse). The OS is horrible and I wish companies would stop adding their own horrible versions of what they think a TV OS should be because sorry Samsung, you're not good at it. The TV also has what only I can describe as JPG artifacts appearing on the screen (and no, it's not my connection) making it seem like the TV is working double duty trying to process something that doesn't need processing. More AI junk? Who knows. The tradeoff of it being pretty darn thin - which is a plus, the sound is horrible but, who buys a TV like this and doesn't consider getting better sound via at least a sound bar anyways?

This TV is a clear indication that shrinkflation exists. I feel like I am getting less but paying far more compared to the previous years. Yes the TV turns on and yes, it has an anti-glair coating but thats all I can say for this thing. 

Wish they would have kept what was good about the "The Frame" line and continued it on through to make it even better than that previous years.

title: 🌟The Greatest Upgrade in History🌟
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] 🌟 RIP to My Optometrist and Audiologist: The Greatest Upgrade in History

We just replaced our ancient, 32-inch dinosaur of a TV with the 65-inch Neo QLED and matching soundbar, and our lives have officially changed.

For the last decade, watching a movie in our living room required the tactical precision of a bomb squad. My glasses had to be perfectly wiped, my chair had to be exactly four feet from the screen, and my hearing aids were turned up so high I could hear my neighbour's cat changing its mind in the next house over.

Not anymore.

With this new 65-inch beast, the glasses are officially OFF. The picture is so crisp, bright, and staggeringly massive that I can see the individual pores on a football player's face from the kitchen. I'm pretty sure the local airport is using my living room as a backup runway flare.

And the soundbar - S-Series All-in-one Soundbar HW-S60D with 5.0ch? Hearing aids: DEACTIVATED. Turned them straight off. The bass from this thing doesn’t just enter your ears; it rattles your fillings and rearranges your internal organs. I watched an action movie last night and felt the explosions in my shins. For the first time in years, I can actually understand the whispered dialogue in gritty dramas without needing subtitles or blasting the volume to maximum.

Even the remote control is a hyperactive masterpiece. Our old TV remote required a literal prayer ritual, a hard point-and-shoot aim, and a thumb wrestling match just to change the channel. This new remote is so lightning-fast and responsive that if I even blink near the directional pad, it has already skipped three episodes of my show. It responds faster than my own reflexes.

Hubby says it’s "too big for the room", but I can't hear them over the glorious, cinematic rumble of my new setup.  The only downside is that my adult children—who already refuse to move out of home—have now permanently barricaded themselves in the lounge room like squatters, meaning I have to physically fight off my own offspring just to watch my KDramas.10/10.

title: Absolute Game Changer for Family Movie Nights!
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I bought this TV to upgrade our family entertainment, and it has exceeded every expectation. If you are on the fence, just buy it.
Stunning Visuals & Massive Scale
The resolution on this screen is absolutely awesome. Every scene is crystal clear, and the sheer size of the display makes total immersion a cinch. It genuinely feels like bringing the commercial theater experience right into your living room.
Incredible Built-In Sound
The biggest surprise is the audio. The way the sound travels and bounces around the room is incredible. It completely fills the space, making it almost unnecessary to buy an additional surround sound system or expensive soundbar.
Flawless Smart Features
Smart features can sometimes be clunky, but this TV has zero issues with my Alexa. It integrated into my smart home instantly and works flawlessly every single time.
The Ultimate Verdict
More than anything, this TV has brought my family closer together. My kids absolutely enjoy our cinema nights when they come over to spend time with their dad. Seeing their faces light up during movie nights makes this worth every single penny. Highly recommended!

title: Viewing Experience
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Upgrading from a 55-inch to the Samsung Neo QLED 75-inch has been an absolute game changer for our home. The difference in size alone makes everything feel so much more immersive for movies, sport, even everyday TV just feel bigger and more cinematic.

The picture quality is incredible. The brightness, contrast, and colour are on another level, and the detail is so sharp it almost feels 3D at times. Dark scenes look deep and rich, while bright scenes really pop without being overwhelming.. The sound is also much better than expected for a flat-screen TV, giving a more surround-like feel without needing a sound bar.

Overall, this upgrade has completely transformed our viewing experience. If you're thinking about going bigger, I’d absolutely recommend it — the jump from 55” to 75” is 100% worth it.

title: Shrinkflation
body:
To be honest, this TV isn't exactly the thing it was always marketed to be. I bought a 2024 version and it was cheaper and better in every way. Unfortunately, the bloated software misbehaved and would just turn itself off - even after a factory reset. 

I was upsold this 2026 version instead and while it will display the art in art mode just fine, the one cable to power it and provide all the inputs no longer exists. Meaning, you have wires coming out the back like a regular TV. You also have a terrible viewing angle, like a normal TV (actually, perhaps worse). The OS is horrible and I wish companies would stop adding their own horrible versions of what they think a TV OS should be because sorry Samsung, you're not good at it. The TV also has what only I can describe as JPG artifacts appearing on the screen (and no, it's not my connection) making it seem like the TV is working double duty trying to process something that doesn't need processing. More AI junk? Who knows. The tradeoff of it being pretty darn thin - which is a plus, the sound is horrible but, who buys a TV like this and doesn't consider getting better sound via at least a sound bar anyways?

This TV is a clear indication that shrinkflation exists. I feel like I am getting less but paying far more compared to the previous years. Yes the TV turns on and yes, it has an anti-glair coating but thats all I can say for this thing. 

Wish they would have kept what was good about the "The Frame" line and continued it on through to make it even better than that previous years.

title: Great quality, interface and settings lacking
body:
I've had the tv for about 2.5 years now and it has me wanting to no longer have smart tv features in future televisions. 

Image quality:
Absolutely fantastic! The matte screen is great for watching in sunny environments, and the frame mode is a lot of fun. Many frame features are hidden behind a paywall however. As a gamer, the image quality has been great for the image resolution.

Gaming: Annoying sometimes. I had to disable game mode due to the screen blacking out and loading and it rendered, causing many interruptions to online performance and quick reaction moments.

Interface: I disabled as much as I could. Regardless of configuring the settings properly, the television refused to comply and would auto-run apps, shows, etc. I am extremely tech literate, worked with customer support, reset the tv and settings, and it would still auto-run apps that I have never opened and used myself, thus my statement of not wanting smart features on future tvs. 

Overall - mid tier tv. Variety of features available, great quality image, but frustrating to use for what I'd like out of it.
