title: MAKABAGONG MINI LEAD THIS 2026!
body:
gusto ko lang i-share kasi nung una nagdadalawang isip din ako bumili kasi medyo mahal sya para sa monitor. Pero ngayon masasabi ko sulit na sulit.

binili ko yung Samsung M80H Mini LED 2026 model mismo sa Robinson Appliances Bagong Silang Caloocan. Pag bukas ko pa lang ang ganda na ng screen, 4K tapos Mini LED kaya pala iba yung black nya, as in itim talaga hindi yung parang gray lang sa ibang monitor. Kahit gabi kami nanonood ng movie kita pa rin lahat.

Ako kasi WFH 8hrs ako nakaharap dito pero di sumasakit ulo ko unlike dati kong monitor. Malaking bagay sakin yun.

Akala ko monitor lang pero Smart TV na pala talaga tong M80H na to. Kahit patay laptop ko nanonood kami ng Netflix Youtube dito lang mismo. May speaker na malakas at may SlimFit camera pa na kasama pang zoom, kaya di na ako bumili ng iba. Yung remote nya ang liit lang pero solar pala likod nya, tapat mo lang sa bintana nagchacharge na kaya di na need battery.

pero yung pinaka nagustuhan namin mag asawa dito sa M80H 2026 eto talaga

yung AI Companion nya hindi na yung luma na utos lang. Dito sa M80H pwede mo na talaga kausapin. Sasabihin mo lang "Hey Samsung ano magandang ulam ngayon" o "hanapan mo ko ng comedy movie" sasagutin ka nya mismo at magsasalita yung monitor. Minsan habang nagluluto ako tinatanong ko recipe sinasagot nya at nalabas sa screen. Parang may kasama ka sa bahay.

tapos yung AI Football Mode nya. Dito ako napabili talaga. Nung nanonood kami ng PBA nung linggo nung in-on ko yung Football Mode sa M80H, biglang mas naging buhay yung kulay ng court, kita mo pawis ng player, at yung bola kahit mabilis hindi nagbblur. Tapos yung sound lumakas yung sigawan ng crowd parang nasa Araneta ka talaga. Sabi ng byenan ko "bakit parang ang linaw ng TV nyo parang nasa harap ka"

kaya kung naghahanap ka ng monitor na pang work at pang TV na rin, eto na yung Samsung M80H Mini LED 2026 kunin mo na. Isang bilihan lang tapos na, monitor na TV pa may kausap ka pa pag nanonood ng bola. 5 stars ako dito hindi ako nagsisisi. order nyo na habang may stock pa.

title: Samsung Tv Plus
body:
Samsung TV Plus is a great free streaming service that comes built into Samsung Mini LED TVs. It offers a wide variety of live TV channels and on-demand content without requiring a subscription. The service is easy to access, and the interface is clean and responsive.

On a Samsung Mini LED TV, the viewing experience is excellent. The Mini LED display delivers bright highlights, deep blacks, and vibrant colors, making movies, sports, and live channels look sharp and immersive. The smooth performance and fast navigation make switching between channels quick and convenient.

While Samsung TV Plus includes ads and its content library isn't as extensive as paid streaming platforms, it's an excellent value because it's completely free. It's especially useful for casual viewing, news, sports highlights, documentaries, and entertainment channels.

Overall Rating: 4.5/5

Samsung TV Plus is a fantastic bonus feature on Samsung Mini LED TVs. It provides plenty of free entertainment, and the outstanding picture quality of the Mini LED display makes the viewing experience even more enjoyable.

body:
(This review was collected as part of a promotion.) The 98 Inch Crystal UHD DU9000 4K Tizen OS Smart TV (2024) is nothing short of spectacular. Its massive screen offers a stunningly immersive viewing experience, perfect for family movie nights and bringing everyone together. The 4K resolution ensures that every detail is crystal clear, making you feel like you're right in the middle of the action. title: รีวิว TV SONY BRAVIA KD-32W830K
body:
รู้สึกภูมิใจที่อย่างน้อยได้ใช้ผลิตภัณ TV จาก SONY ที่ยังคงผลิตจากญี่ปุ่นอยู่ ก่อนที่จะถูกควบรวมกับบริษั​ท TCL แม้ TV SONY BRAVIA จะมีราคาที่สูงกว่า TV ตามท้องตลาดทั่วไป แต่ราคานี้ก็คุ้มค่ากับคุณภาพและอายุการใช้งานที่ยาวนาน ทำไมถึงพูดเช่นนี้ได้ เพราะผมยืนยันจากประสบการณ์ตรงจาก TV เครื่องเก่าที่เป็นของ SONY BRAVIA รุ่น KLV-32BX300 ซึ่งยังคงใช้ได้เต็มประสิทธิภาพอยู่ในปัจจุบั​น แน่นอนว่าครั้งนี้ผมยังคงเลือก TV SONY ในรุ่น KD-32W830K เพราะความเชื่อมั่นในแบรนด์ของ SONY

หลังจากได้ลองใช้มา 20 วัน คุณภาพด้านภาพให้ภาพที่คมชัด สีที่จัดกำลังพอดี แสงและเงามืดไม่โอเวอร์หรืออันเดอร์จนเกินไป คุณภาพด้านเสียง ผมค่อนข้างชอบกับเสียงที่มีมิติ เช่น เวลาฟังเพลงจะให้อารมณ์ความรู้สึกถึงระดับชั้นของเสียงเสมือนฟังจากห้องอัดเสียง ในตอนดูหนังก็ให้อรรถรสในการรับชมที่เต็มเปี่ยม เช่น ตอนที่ต่อสู้กัน เสียงกระหึ่มและเร้าใจอย่างมาก ส่วนตอนที่ตัวละครสนทนา ก็สามารถแยกเสียงได้ชัด แน่นอนว่าสิ่งที่ต้องไม่พูดไม่ได้เลยคือการนำ TV ตัวนี้มาเล่นกับเครื่องเล่น PS4 &​ PS5 ซึ่งยังคงทำได้ดีทั้งเรื่องภาพและเสียงอย่างเสมอต้นเสมอปลาย

แม้จะเป็น TV 32 นิ้ว แต่คุณภาพคับจออย่างล้นเหลือครับ

title: Slow & Glitchy
body:
We bought a 43" and 50" after having had a Sony for the past 10 years, how I regret that decision. They are slow and terribly glitchy, like using a 15 year old computer. Problems we have had include;
1. Terrible WIFI reception, only works on 5 GHz channel, if it drops to 2.4 GHz you might as well have dial up. Had to install a WIFI extender behind each TV and plug them in with a cable. No WIFI reception issues with any other device in our house.
2. Incredibly slow to start up, select and move through apps. Often you'll be 5 minutes in, finally watching something, and then it will wake up and reset to home screen.
3. Glitchy apps, especially SBS Australia. Often will play the audio of the last thing watched on SBS over the top of whatever you happen to be watching now, even if on a completely different app. Need to turn it off at the wall to fix this.
4. Free TV guide generally shows "no information" until it's been on for 15-20 minutes.

Both TV's have exactly the same issues, so I assume it's not just a bad apple. Both updated as required. I'm not sure how much of this is the TV's fault and how much is the Google TV operating system, but since you don't have a choice of operating system it doesn't really matter.

Picture and sound are fine, as expected for any modern TV, but functionality is so poor that I will probably have to buy a 3rd party smart TV adapter and just relegate these to being dumb screens. Total junk, do not recommend at all.

With its self-emissive OLED panel, it produces true blacks, vibrant colors, and incredible contrast that brings your content to life. The A80L's sleek, minimalist design looks great in any living room, and the built-in Acoustic Surface Audio+ technology provides an immersive, theater-like sound without the need for external speakers. The Android TV smart platform offers a wide selection of streaming apps and services, and the intuitive user interface makes navigation a breeze.

For gamers, the A80L boasts low input lag, support for 4K 120Hz, and advanced HDMI 2.1 features like Variable Refresh Rate and Auto Low Latency Mode. Whether you're watching movies, TV shows, or playing the latest games, the Sony A80L is an exceptional OLED TV that I highly recommend.

title: Hisense 75-Inch 4K TV Review
body: I have been using the Hisense 75-inch 4K TV for a few weeks now, and it has been an outstanding upgrade for my living room. The picture quality is sharp and vibrant, especially in 4K HDR content — colors pop without looking oversaturated, and dark scenes hold up surprisingly well thanks to its strong contrast and local dimming.  The size alone makes a huge difference for movies and sports. It delivers a true theater-like experience, and the wide viewing angles make it great for gatherings. The sound quality is decent for built-in speakers — clear dialogue and a bit of bass — though I paired it with a soundbar for more immersion.  Hisense’s smart TV interface is easy to navigate. Apps like Netflix, Prime Video, and YouTube load quickly, and it supports both Alexa and Google Assistant. Connectivity has been rock solid through Wi-Fi and HDMI (it includes multiple HDMI 2.1 ports, perfect for gaming).  If you want a massive, high-quality TV without paying premium-brand prices, the Hisense 75-inch is hard to beat. It delivers excellent performance, simple setup, and a feature set that rivals more expensive models.

title: Excellent Value in a QLED TV
body: I recently upgraded to the 2025 Hisense 55QD6QF, and it has completely exceeded my expectations, delivering premium features at an unbelievable price point.  The QLED display truly makes colors pop. Everything I watch are incredibly vibrant and lifelike, far surpassing my previous TV. The blacks are deep, and the brightness is impressive, making viewing comfortable even in a well-lit room.  The integrated Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos support is the heart of the cinematic experience. Movies are breathtakingly detailed with dynamic HDR, and the sound quality is rich and enveloping. It genuinely feels like I have a budget home theater built right into the set.  Finally, the Fire TV operating system is fast and intuitive. Apps load quickly, and the built-in Alexa voice control makes searching for content effortless. The AI 4K Upscaler also deserves praise; it does a surprisingly good job of cleaning up older, lower-resolution content, making almost everything look crisp.

title: Premium OLED Performance That Lives Up to the Hype
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] After spending several weeks with the LG OLED77G6WUA as our primary TV for movies, sports, gaming, and everyday streaming, it's clear this is a premium television that delivers an outstanding overall experience. 
The build quality immediately stands out. The panel feels exceptionally well-made with a slim, premium design that looks fantastic mounted on the wall. Despite its large 77-inch size, it feels sturdy and well-engineered, with excellent fit and finish. Nothing creaks or flexes during installation, giving confidence that it's built to last. 
The included remote is comfortable to hold and intuitive to use, The pointer function makes navigating menus and streaming apps much faster than traditional directional buttons, and voice controls respond accurately for searching content or adjusting settings. Dedicated streaming shortcuts are also a welcome convenience. 
From an ergonomics standpoint, everyday use is effortless. The webOS interface is responsive, inputs switch quickly, and settings are logically organized. Whether adjusting picture modes for movies, enabling Game Optimizer for console gaming, or customizing audio, everything is easy to access. The anti-reflective screen performs well in brighter rooms while still delivering exceptional contrast in darker environments.
After extensive daily use, the TV has remained consistent and reliable. It powers on quickly, maintains a stable Wi-Fi connection, and shows no signs of performance degradation. The premium construction and high-quality materials inspire confidence in its long-term durability. 
Overall, the LG OLED77G6WUA is an exceptional television. Between its premium build, user-friendly remote, thoughtful ergonomics, and dependable performance after extensive testing, it has exceeded expectations and has become the centerpiece of our home entertainment setup. It's a worthwhile investment for anyone looking for a flagship OLED experience.

title: Absolute Masterclass in Picture Quality and Design
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] After 10 years of loyal service from my trusted LG OLED55B6V, I finally decided it was time to upgrade. My old TV was brilliant, but a decade of heavy use with static TV channel logos and subtitles had eventually caused some screen burn-in.
​Moving to the OLED65G64LW has been an absolute revelation. The jump from 55 to 65 inches is impressive on its own, but the sheer leap in technology over the last ten years is mind-blowing.
​The brightness levels on this G-series panel are a massive step up from my old B6—it handles room reflections effortlessly while keeping those famous, perfect OLED blacks. Knowing how much LG has advanced their built-in panel-care features, logo luminance adjustment, and anti-burn-in tech over the years gives me massive peace of mind this time around, especially for broadcast TV and subtitles.
​The design is a work of art it mounts incredibly flush to the wall, looking completely seamless and premium. The smart webOS interface is also lightning-fast compared to older generations.
​If you are hesitating to upgrade an older OLED, don't look back. This is a masterful piece of engineering and proves why LG still leads the way.

title: Great with a few issues
body:
Overall this is a great TV. The visuals are a 10/10, but there are problems I wish they would fix.

1st problem, no steam link or moonlight support. My gaming PC is in another room, but I can't stream games to the TV. Competition has this feature and it's pretty disappointing WebOS doesn't support it.

2nd problem, eARC audio disconnections. I use a pair of Klipsch the Fives speakers over eARC, but they occasionally disconnect and switch to using the TVs built in speakers. Some days it doesn't disconnect, others I have to switch it back to eARC multiple times. Not a deal breaker, but definitely annoying to deal with while watching a movie.

Neither of these are deal breakers, but with this being an expensive flagship TV it's enough to drop the TV down a star.

Bottom line, if you have a bright room like me this TV is a game changer, as long as these gripes aren't too annoying to you.

title: The LG OLED G6 combines incredible 4K picture quality with smart features and an impressive selection of free channels.
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I’m very happy with the 77 inch LG OLED G6 television. The picture quality is absolutely amazing when watching 4K content. The image is incredibly clear, sharp, and detailed, making movies, sports, and streaming shows look fantastic. The colors are vibrant, and the OLED display really stands out. For non-4K channels, the picture quality is still good, but it is not nearly as crisp as true 4K content. If you watch a lot of 4K programming, this TV really shines. The 77 inch size is perfect for my wall and makes a huge impact in the room without feeling overwhelming. One of the reasons I chose this model was the gallery style design. Initially, we had it wall mounted with the wires visible, and it sat completely flush against the wall. While it looks sleek, the exposed wires took away from the overall appearance. We later had the wires run through the wall, which looks much cleaner and more professional. The trade-off is that the TV no longer sits quite as flush against the wall as it did originally, but the cleaner installation was well worth it. I also love that it’s a smart TV. Setting up and downloading all of my favorite streaming apps was easy, and everything is conveniently accessible in one place. One feature that pleasantly surprised me was the number of free channels included with LG channels. I wasn’t expecting to have access to so much free content right out of the box. There are channels for news, movies, sports, and more, which adds a lot of value without needing additional subscriptions. The included remote is simple, and intuitive, and easy to use. There is a stand available for purchase separately, but we preferred the clean look of a wall mounted installation. Overall, this is an excellent TV outstanding 4K picture quality, a beautiful design, and easy to use smart features. If you’re looking for a premium large screen TV, the LG OLED G6 is a great choice. ￼

But then there is nothing about setting up the TV itself - I was told to download an app, which I did but that never 'found' the TV so was a pointless exercise (even though they are on the same WiFi).  But I had 4 options of my WiFi to choose from which I didn't understand, so just chose the top one. The picture is sharp but nothing spectacular.  I don't think it is any brighter than my old TV (not OLED), but the black is definitely blacker.  I specifically chose this TV because it says you don't get a reflection in a brightly lit room - sadly that's not true.  Whilst it is reduced a little, I do still get a reflection.  So still have to close the curtains.  The sound on the TV isn't great, it's okay but not great - so I am glad I took the free soundbar.  But again I had trouble setting that up, so eventually contacted the support.  I had to do a hard restart (unplug TV, press on/off button for 30 seconds and then plug back in and turn on, same with soundbar).  That did at least sort out the soundbar issue and she was able to talk me through something so that I only have to use one remote control to use the TV, skybox and soundbar.  But there is no way I would have been able to do that myself.  In short, it's a decent enough TV but nothing ground-breaking.
author: KelperKaz

title: Fantastic Gaming TV however some BIG AI drawbacks

For a 4k TV you should be respecting your customers more. 

The OS I feel is significantly slower than even my model bought in 2021, why does it take longer to open the settings panel or why is there noticable lag just navigating the menu? very annoying for a flagship TV. 

I wish I could rip out every nonsense AI video and I want to know how secure the TV really is after watching that  DO NOT BUY: LG’s Spyware TVs, Monitors, and Wiretapping Concerns by Gamers Nexus. 

My TV also came slightly damaged, there was no screen wrap which there always and removing a sticker on the screen has left a nasty residue on my screen which is visable both on and off. 

Reflection handling is decent, main reason I bought this was to game and I think it does that very well, the other issues I wish they would address soon.

title: Disappointed
body: Well, for about a month this TV was amazing. The updates .67.69 increase the brightness a great deal In vivid mode to where real content was bright and punchy and a step above the competition.  Then I updated to .73 and the brightness in vivid mode has been cut down and it is no longer hitting hard like it did. It’s actually looking just like my C4 and C5.  So if you’re looking to buy a really bright TV, save your money and get the midtier one because LG tends to push brightness to get people to buy it and then they dial it back down because they’re afraid of the TV having burn in. They did this with the G5 too. I want my money back because I feel like this is not the TV I purchased and it basically has been false advertising. You can’t sell a TV as the brightest OLED you ever made and then cut the brightness After everyone buys it

title: Beware this years 77 inch
body: I purchased my first one early July to replace a 77 C1.  I have been through 7 panels, whether it be through exchanges or purchasing additional units to compare and then exchanging those as well:  at one point I had 3 TVs in the house trying to compare and pick the more acceptable one.  I’m literally throwing my hands up at this point.  Every panel out of all of them were simply horrid. Major vertical banding on each panel.  I put over 100 hours on each panel.  Major dirty screen affect, and major cyan color push on the far left and right sides of some of the panels.  Black blobs in low dark scenes. Completely unacceptable for the price point.  LG should be embarrassed.  AV forum users confirming major issues with 2026 77 inch panels in comparison to the 65 and 83 inch models.  I currently have one of the seven panels left, and may pull the trigger on an 83 to compare.  Iv literally waisted the last 3 weeks going back and fourth, returning, testing and am spinning my wheels on how a company like this is allowing these panels; at this price, to hit store shelves in this state.  Buyer beware.

title: Hisense 75-Inch 4K TV Review
body: I have been using the Hisense 75-inch 4K TV for a few weeks now, and it has been an outstanding upgrade for my living room. The picture quality is sharp and vibrant, especially in 4K HDR content — colors pop without looking oversaturated, and dark scenes hold up surprisingly well thanks to its strong contrast and local dimming.  The size alone makes a huge difference for movies and sports. It delivers a true theater-like experience, and the wide viewing angles make it great for gatherings. The sound quality is decent for built-in speakers — clear dialogue and a bit of bass — though I paired it with a soundbar for more immersion.  Hisense’s smart TV interface is easy to navigate. Apps like Netflix, Prime Video, and YouTube load quickly, and it supports both Alexa and Google Assistant. Connectivity has been rock solid through Wi-Fi and HDMI (it includes multiple HDMI 2.1 ports, perfect for gaming).  If you want a massive, high-quality TV without paying premium-brand prices, the Hisense 75-inch is hard to beat. It delivers excellent performance, simple setup, and a feature set that rivals more expensive models.

title: Thousands cheaper than equivalent quality
body:
I did a lot of research before buying this for my partner. Hisense and TCL's Mini-LED TV's are feature packed and much more affordable. Some may mistake this for cheap, or corner cutting, that would lower the TV's quality. In fact, a TV's price is 60-70% the screen itself. What let's Hisense and TCL sell quality TV's at a lower price, is the manufacturing process. They make their own screens, in-house, and sell those same screens to larger name brands. Cutting out 60-70% of their cost, giving them another revenue stream with the screen sales and lowering the cost for the consumer. 

She loves her new TV. I bought my last TV from the Brick, a 65" LG C1 OLED in 2022, this new Hisense puts my aging (but high end) TV to shame. 

Thank you to The Brick for always being easy to deal with. I spoke with a nice lady named Charlie at the Halifax showroom to arrange the pickup and he was diligent and accommodating. We picked up the next morning and it was as easy as that. 

Don't hesitate to buy from the Brick, you have 48 hours from purchase to put the TV through it's paces and make sure all is working. If you find a dead pixel or anything out of the ordinary, The Brick makes it easy to call and exchange, not something we needed to do, but something that's assuring to know. 

Happy Easter, all. 

-J.P.    N.S.  Canada 🇨🇦

title: Absolute Masterclass in Performance and Value
body: AI Mode All Images Videos News Maps Shopping Books Flights Finance Here is a glowing review for your TV, written to highlight its premium features, picture quality, and smart capabilities. Review: Hisense 65" U7S QLED Mini-LED AI Google TV Verdict: An Absolute Masterclass in Performance and Value The Hisense 65U7S completely redefines what a mid-range television can achieve. By blending cutting-edge Mini-LED backlighting with advanced AI processing, this TV delivers a premium visual experience that easily competes with displays twice its price. It is an absolute triumph for movie lovers, gamers, and sports fans alike. Picture Quality: Stunning Contrast and Vibrant Color Mini-LED Precision: The local dimming execution is flawless, offering deep, inky blacks and eliminating distracting backlight bleed or blooming. Quantum Dot Brilliance: The QLED technology produces incredibly rich, lifelike colors that remain vibrant even in brightly lit rooms. Extreme Brightness: High-dynamic-range (HDR) content truly pops, making highlights like sunlight, explosions, and neon signs look remarkably realistic. AI and Smart Features: Smart, Fast, and Intuitive Next-Gen Upscaling: The onboard AI processor does a magnificent job cleaning up lower-resolution content, making standard HD broadcast and older streaming titles look crisp and clean. Google TV Hub: The user interface is fluid, perfectly organized, and provides highly accurate content recommendations right on the home screen. Hands-Free Control: Google Assistant integration is seamless, allowing for effortless voice commands to control playback, search for shows, or manage smart home devices. title: My DREAM TV Upgrade for 2026!!! 📺
body:
I’ve been looking for a new premium TV to upgrade my living room for the new year, and I didn’t want to spend an arm and a leg for one so I got the 65” Hisense U88QG, which is one of the top premium MiniLED options on the market!

Now the first thing I noticed using this new TV was the crazy 5000 nits of peak brightness which means it gets plenty bright for daytime watching, not to mention having an anti-reflective coating so it still looks good from the side for when you have friends over! It’s also a MiniLED panel that uses quantum dots which if you don’t know what that is, basically means you get some really rich vibrant colours, that are actually accurate too so your favourite movies don’t look washed out! But as much as you might wanna binge watch, gaming is an epic experience too thanks to the 165hz refresh rate that actually supports AMD Freesync so everything feels smooth! There are even built-in top firing speakers with subwoofers in the back for Dolby Atmos surround sound which actually sounds shockingly good and cool, but not as cool as the built-in USB-C DisplayPort so I can easily plug my laptop in to use with the TV, or even a full on gaming PC if you wanna game on the TV!

title: 85Inch TV 85U88QG
body: I upgraded to the 85” Hisense U88QG after owning an OLED for a long time, and I was honestly nervous about losing those perfect blacks.  I can confidently say: I was surprised in the best possible way.  The black levels on this TV are outstanding for an LED. Local dimming is very aggressive, blooming is minimal, and in real content the contrast looks fantastic. In many scenes I simply stop thinking about the technology and just enjoy the image.  Where this TV really shocked me is brightness. HDR highlights, reflections, explosions, daylight scenes — they have an intensity my OLED simply could not reach. It makes movies and games feel incredibly dynamic.  Gaming is excellent. The Game Bar gives you real information, VRR works perfectly, motion is super smooth, and input lag feels very low. Playing on an 85” screen completely changes immersion.  Google TV runs fast, apps load quickly, and the overall experience feels premium.  Sound is also much better than I expected from built-in speakers.  Is OLED still king in a fully dark room for absolute black? Yes. But this TV fights back with size, brightness, and impact — and it does it very, very well.  For anyone afraid of moving from OLED to high-end Mini-LED: don’t be. This set delivers.  Highly recommended.

The anti‑reflection screen also makes a noticeable difference, so daytime sports and shows are still clear without annoying glare. ​ For gaming, this set is a beast. Consoles and PC both look and feel great on this screen, and Auto Low Latency Mode means there is no need to constantly tweak settings.  The built‑in 4.1.2‑channel Dolby Atmos system is surprisingly powerful for a TV and does a good job with immersion for movies and games, thanks to the integrated subwoofer and upward‑firing speakers. Google TV runs smoothly, apps load quickly, and built‑in Google Assistant plus support for Alexa and Apple AirPlay make it easy to integrate into a smart home setup. title: Great with a few issues
body:
Overall this is a great TV. The visuals are a 10/10, but there are problems I wish they would fix.

1st problem, no steam link or moonlight support. My gaming PC is in another room, but I can't stream games to the TV. Competition has this feature and it's pretty disappointing WebOS doesn't support it.

2nd problem, eARC audio disconnections. I use a pair of Klipsch the Fives speakers over eARC, but they occasionally disconnect and switch to using the TVs built in speakers. Some days it doesn't disconnect, others I have to switch it back to eARC multiple times. Not a deal breaker, but definitely annoying to deal with while watching a movie.

Neither of these are deal breakers, but with this being an expensive flagship TV it's enough to drop the TV down a star.

Bottom line, if you have a bright room like me this TV is a game changer, as long as these gripes aren't too annoying to you.

title: The LG OLED G6 combines incredible 4K picture quality with smart features and an impressive selection of free channels.
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I’m very happy with the 77 inch LG OLED G6 television. The picture quality is absolutely amazing when watching 4K content. The image is incredibly clear, sharp, and detailed, making movies, sports, and streaming shows look fantastic. The colors are vibrant, and the OLED display really stands out. For non-4K channels, the picture quality is still good, but it is not nearly as crisp as true 4K content. If you watch a lot of 4K programming, this TV really shines. The 77 inch size is perfect for my wall and makes a huge impact in the room without feeling overwhelming. One of the reasons I chose this model was the gallery style design. Initially, we had it wall mounted with the wires visible, and it sat completely flush against the wall. While it looks sleek, the exposed wires took away from the overall appearance. We later had the wires run through the wall, which looks much cleaner and more professional. The trade-off is that the TV no longer sits quite as flush against the wall as it did originally, but the cleaner installation was well worth it. I also love that it’s a smart TV. Setting up and downloading all of my favorite streaming apps was easy, and everything is conveniently accessible in one place. One feature that pleasantly surprised me was the number of free channels included with LG channels. I wasn’t expecting to have access to so much free content right out of the box. There are channels for news, movies, sports, and more, which adds a lot of value without needing additional subscriptions. The included remote is simple, and intuitive, and easy to use. There is a stand available for purchase separately, but we preferred the clean look of a wall mounted installation. Overall, this is an excellent TV outstanding 4K picture quality, a beautiful design, and easy to use smart features. If you’re looking for a premium large screen TV, the LG OLED G6 is a great choice. ￼

I specifically chose this TV because it says you don't get a reflection in a brightly lit room - sadly that's not true.  Whilst it is reduced a little, I do still get a reflection. I had to do a hard restart (unplug TV, press on/off button for 30 seconds and then plug back in and turn on, same with soundbar).  That did at least sort out the soundbar issue and she was able to talk me through something so that I only have to use one remote control to use the TV, skybox and soundbar. title: Excellent Value in a QLED TV
body: I recently upgraded to the 2025 Hisense 55QD6QF, and it has completely exceeded my expectations, delivering premium features at an unbelievable price point.  The QLED display truly makes colors pop. Everything I watch are incredibly vibrant and lifelike, far surpassing my previous TV. The blacks are deep, and the brightness is impressive, making viewing comfortable even in a well-lit room.  The integrated Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos support is the heart of the cinematic experience. Movies are breathtakingly detailed with dynamic HDR, and the sound quality is rich and enveloping. It genuinely feels like I have a budget home theater built right into the set.  Finally, the Fire TV operating system is fast and intuitive. Apps load quickly, and the built-in Alexa voice control makes searching for content effortless. The AI 4K Upscaler also deserves praise; it does a surprisingly good job of cleaning up older, lower-resolution content, making almost everything look crisp.

title: Thousands cheaper than equivalent quality
body:
I did a lot of research before buying this for my partner. Hisense and TCL's Mini-LED TV's are feature packed and much more affordable. Some may mistake this for cheap, or corner cutting, that would lower the TV's quality. In fact, a TV's price is 60-70% the screen itself. What let's Hisense and TCL sell quality TV's at a lower price, is the manufacturing process. They make their own screens, in-house, and sell those same screens to larger name brands. Cutting out 60-70% of their cost, giving them another revenue stream with the screen sales and lowering the cost for the consumer. 

She loves her new TV. I bought my last TV from the Brick, a 65" LG C1 OLED in 2022, this new Hisense puts my aging (but high end) TV to shame. 

Thank you to The Brick for always being easy to deal with. I spoke with a nice lady named Charlie at the Halifax showroom to arrange the pickup and he was diligent and accommodating. We picked up the next morning and it was as easy as that. 

Don't hesitate to buy from the Brick, you have 48 hours from purchase to put the TV through it's paces and make sure all is working. If you find a dead pixel or anything out of the ordinary, The Brick makes it easy to call and exchange, not something we needed to do, but something that's assuring to know. 

Happy Easter, all. 

-J.P.    N.S.  Canada 🇨🇦

title: Best tv in price range
body: The Hisense 55U78QG is one of the best value 55-inch TVs in its class. Its Mini-LED backlighting and Quantum Dot panel deliver excellent brightness, rich colours, and strong contrast, making movies and sports look vibrant and sharp. Gaming performance is a standout thanks to a 165Hz panel, VRR, ALLM, and very low input lag.  Google TV runs smoothly and offers all major apps, and the built-in speakers are surprisingly decent for everyday use. The main drawbacks are narrow viewing angles and some blooming in dark scenes, which is typical for many VA-panel TVs.  Overall, the 55U78QG offers premium-level picture quality and gaming features at a mid-range price, making it a great choice for bright rooms, movie lovers, and gamers.

title: An amazing TV, very (very!) good image and system.
body:
(This review was collected as part of a promotion.) I have to say I’m super super impressed with this TV!

First of all, the quality of the image is AMAZING. In my house, the TV is in my living room, right by the window, and even in a very bright day like today (as you can see in the pictures, it’s 100% foggy outside, very white super super bright) I can still watch the TV with my blinds open. 
The colors, brightness and definition are amazing. I love how sharp and detailed the image looks. I have watched a movie in 4K and it was nice, the movie looked and sounded great. It was a life-changing experience!
I highly recommend this TV if you have a room which can get bright or darker depending on the time of the day. With the old TV I used to have, I had to close the blinds every time I wanted to watch TV during the day; and now I don’t have to!

The sound is also amazing. It is super loud and clear even though I don’t have any soundbars.￼

Something else I really like about it is the design. It’s super clean and minimalist. The leg is beautiful, and it made my living room look much nicer and very fancy!

Talking about when the TV arrived: smoothly delivery, it came very well packed and it was super easy to set up. You literally just need to fix the leg of the TV on it and voilà, it’s ready.
It was very easy and simple to set up. I could connect the TV to my phone so it automatically got access to my Wi-Fi at home. After that, I could download and open the apps I use for ￼streaming. It is a very VERY Smart TV, which I love. Oh, it is also super quick to turn on! As soon as you press the button it turns on in one second - much better than the TV I used to have. Changing the output, channels and all is also extremely fast - you click and it is changed. No delays! Amazing.

This Hisense TV has completely changed my experience watching movies, TV shows and news at home - the experience now is much better! I couldn’t be happier and I highly recommend it.

title: Worth the Hype!
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I have wanted the Samsung Frame TV for YEARS, and now that we finally have it, I can honestly say it completely lived up to the hype. It instantly changed the entire feel of our living room and somehow manages to be both functional and beautiful at the same time.

The biggest thing for me was wanting a TV that didn’t dominate the room or feel like a giant black box hanging on the wall. This truly looks like framed art. We had it professionally installed so it would sit perfectly flush against the wall, and I’m really glad we did because that clean built-in look makes such a difference. I also added a thin wooden magnetic frame around it, which made it feel even more custom and high-end.

We ended up getting the Pro version, and honestly… GO PRO. The wireless slim box is one of the coolest features. We hid ours inside a nearby cabinet, so there are zero visible cords and no need to fish wires through the walls. It keeps everything looking incredibly sleek and minimal.

The art mode is probably my favorite feature. We did the yearly art subscription, and there are so many beautiful options to choose from. I love changing the artwork depending on the season, mood, or room vibe, and my kids are obsessed with the fact that we can upload family photos too. People genuinely don’t realize it’s a TV at first, which still makes me laugh every time someone notices.

It’s also super smart and easy to use. All the apps are already built in like Netflix, YouTube, Hulu, and we use the multi-view feature constantly. Being able to have a baseball game on one side while someone else watches a show on the other has already become one of our favorite features.

The picture quality is beautiful and super crisp, clear, and bright without looking harsh or overly processed. Sports look amazing on it, movies feel cinematic, and even cartoons somehow look elevated. The matte screen also helps cut down glare during the day, which I love since our living room gets a lot of natural light.  I was also surprised by how good the sound quality is. The audio feels full and balanced for such a slim TV, and dialogue comes through really clearly without constantly adjusting the volume.

Also, the tiny remote is weirdly adorable. My kids think it’s the coolest little gadget ever. I just need to AirTag it before it disappears into the couch forever.

I had a few friends over recently, and the TV automatically turned on to show artwork as they walked in. Everyone was mesmerized by how much it actually looks like a piece of art.

One minor gripe is that I wish there were more free art options included right out of the box without a subscription, but I’m glad you can at least upload your own content to customize it.

title: Great TV
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I've been going back and forth on this TV for months, and honestly I'm glad I waited for the 2026 model. We mounted it in the living room and the first thing my wife said was "it looks like a painting" — that's exactly what sold us on it in the first place.
Setup was surprisingly smooth. The wireless One Connect box is a game changer if you hate cable clutter. I ran all my boxes and streaming devices through it and tucked it behind the entertainment center — the TV itself has zero cords hanging from it on the wall. That alone was worth it to me.
Picture quality on the Neo QLED panel is noticeably sharper and more vibrant than I expected from a "lifestyle" TV. HDR content looks great — the blacks are deep and highlights have real pop. It's not quite OLED territory, but it's impressive for what this thing is. Local dimming handles most scenes well, though I did notice a tiny bit of blooming around very bright objects on a dark background if you're being picky about it.
Art Mode is genuinely cool. I have it set to display a rotating gallery and guests always ask if it's a real print. The matte finish on the screen kills glare in our bright Texas living room — no more repositioning furniture around sun angles.
A few things to keep in mind: the Art Store subscription is required if you want the full catalog (30 free pieces per month otherwise), and the price point is definitely premium. But if you want a TV that looks like décor when you're not watching it and still performs well for movies and sports — this hits both marks.
Would buy again. No regrets.

title: I can't imagine going back to a normal TV now
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Setup was much more difficult than expected, but now that it's complete, I love the TV!

The setup manual is for multiple models, not just specifically this model. It would have helped to have one diagram that pointed to exactly where the TV controller and the plug for the power cord are.

The remote didn't work with the TV out of the box. I had to do an AI search to pair the remote. Eventually, I found the remote pairing instructions in the TV remote documentation. If it's something a customer will have to do during setup, it should be in the setup document.

Some online videos produced by the manufacturer for setup would have been helpful: a video for setup, one for TV operations, one for art functions, etc.

The Wireless Connect Box connected to the TV easily.

As far as the TV functions go, the picture and sound quality are very good. I assumed I would be buying a soundbar, but don't think I need it! I thought I had heard that the quality of these "Frame" TVs' picture wasn't spectacular, but I think it's very nice!

Onto the "Frame" functionality: The art collection is extensive, but I should probably slow down the rotation time, as I've seen it all within a few days. I decided to spend the money to get the Samsung library of art. It doesn't look like I can make playlists like one would do with music, but I might be able to control what is is shown by putting the pictures in the favorites folder. That should be good enough. I've slowed the rotation time and put a mat on the pictures. I'm having a lot of fun playing with the art.

All-in-all, this is a great TV for my needs; particularly because I wanted a TV that doubles as a piece of art when not being watched.

body:
We bought this TV because of it being a 4K 144Hz matte screen with the Art mode. We love how bright or how dim we can make the image, and displaying our own photos. We also wanted the aesthetic of having a TV that was very unobtrusive, and the near-flush mounting plus available decorative frames do that. 

However, as someone looking for a "professional" TV install, this TV's lack of hardwire connection between display and connection box is very disappointing. Previous The Frame TV's had at least a connection kit available separately, this one does not. Which also means "hiding the box" is very limited, and EMI will be an issue, especially with higher resolution and framerate video. 

We also are not pleased that our 4K (and above) photos cannot be displayed edge-to-edge - you must have a mat - yet the subscription Art does not require the mat.

The sound quality from this is also very mediocre and "tinny," anyone looking for better sound will absolutely need a soundbar or AV reciever.

Service response has been horrible as well. Good luck getting a service person to your house on any reasonable time for you. The positive is it displays art really well but as a tv….well.

title: Absolute Masterclass in Performance and Value
body: AI Mode All Images Videos News Maps Shopping Books Flights Finance Here is a glowing review for your TV, written to highlight its premium features, picture quality, and smart capabilities. Review: Hisense 65" U7S QLED Mini-LED AI Google TV Verdict: An Absolute Masterclass in Performance and Value The Hisense 65U7S completely redefines what a mid-range television can achieve. By blending cutting-edge Mini-LED backlighting with advanced AI processing, this TV delivers a premium visual experience that easily competes with displays twice its price. It is an absolute triumph for movie lovers, gamers, and sports fans alike. Picture Quality: Stunning Contrast and Vibrant Color Mini-LED Precision: The local dimming execution is flawless, offering deep, inky blacks and eliminating distracting backlight bleed or blooming. Quantum Dot Brilliance: The QLED technology produces incredibly rich, lifelike colors that remain vibrant even in brightly lit rooms. Extreme Brightness: High-dynamic-range (HDR) content truly pops, making highlights like sunlight, explosions, and neon signs look remarkably realistic. AI and Smart Features: Smart, Fast, and Intuitive Next-Gen Upscaling: The onboard AI processor does a magnificent job cleaning up lower-resolution content, making standard HD broadcast and older streaming titles look crisp and clean. Google TV Hub: The user interface is fluid, perfectly organized, and provides highly accurate content recommendations right on the home screen. Hands-Free Control: Google Assistant integration is seamless, allowing for effortless voice commands to control playback, search for shows, or manage smart home devices. title: Best Oled TV
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I bought an 83inch G6 last month and I am extremly happy with it. Its a truly fantastic tv. Truth be told my previous tv was an old LG C9 and I was never happy with it. It had poor motion for movies due to judder. The motion interpolation wasnt great. It had noticeable colour banding. Its 60hz motion for gaming was poor and blurry unless you used bfi, but it dimmed the picture significantly. Due to the lower brightness of the tv, the image would be washed out in brighter light conditions.
The g6 completely fixes all of these issues. Its the best tv I have owend. Motion for movies is great. The motion interpolation setting are fantastic and some of the best I have seen. Colour banding is not an issue at all on this tv. 60hz gaming motion is massivly improved, image is alot clearer. I still prefer it with bfi enabled as it sharpens it up. But because the tv is so bright even with bfi enabled, the drop in brightness isnt an issue. The brightness of the tv is perfect for bright room viewing.
If anyone had an older oled tv and was on the fence if a newer oled was worth it and had any improvements. I can safely say the g6 is well worth the upgrade.

body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I’ve been using this 65” LG TV in our main living space and it’s been a great upgrade overall. The picture quality stands out right away. Everything looks sharp, colors are vibrant without feeling overdone, and it performs well in both bright daytime and nighttime viewing.

One thing I really noticed is the lack of glare. Our living room gets a lot of natural light from different angles, and this screen still looks clear no matter where you’re sitting, which I couldn’t say about my previous TV.

The AI features are helpful and adjust settings automatically, which makes it very easy to use day to day. Setup was straightforward, and mounting was simple, though I wish it came with screws that fit my existing wall mount.

The speakers are fine but better with a sound bar, and the remote takes a little getting used to.

Overall, I’d give it 4 stars.

Review submitted as part of a program that provides a purchase discount.

We purchased our 65" LG G6 OLED TV from The Brick in Milton, and the entire experience was top-tier from start to finish. A huge shoutout to Zubash, who helped us with our purchase. Zubash was knowledgeable, patient, and made the whole process smooth and hassle-free.
As for the TV itself, the LG G6 is in a class of its own. The picture quality is remarkably lifelike it delivers deep, perfect blacks and vibrant highlights without the heavy artificial color saturation seen on other brands. The α11 AI Processor handles motion effortlessly, and the Reflection Free Premium panel keeps glare away even in a brightly lit room.
The included Zero-Gap Flush Wall Mount gives it a seamless, gallery-style look flat against the wall. Having 4K up to 165Hz VRR across all HDMI ports also makes it a powerhouse for gaming.
 If you are shopping at The Brick in Milton, definitely ask for Zubash for fantastic customer service. Highly recommended!

title: Hisense 75-Inch 4K TV Review
body: I have been using the Hisense 75-inch 4K TV for a few weeks now, and it has been an outstanding upgrade for my living room. The picture quality is sharp and vibrant, especially in 4K HDR content — colors pop without looking oversaturated, and dark scenes hold up surprisingly well thanks to its strong contrast and local dimming.  The size alone makes a huge difference for movies and sports. It delivers a true theater-like experience, and the wide viewing angles make it great for gatherings. The sound quality is decent for built-in speakers — clear dialogue and a bit of bass — though I paired it with a soundbar for more immersion.  Hisense’s smart TV interface is easy to navigate. Apps like Netflix, Prime Video, and YouTube load quickly, and it supports both Alexa and Google Assistant. Connectivity has been rock solid through Wi-Fi and HDMI (it includes multiple HDMI 2.1 ports, perfect for gaming).  If you want a massive, high-quality TV without paying premium-brand prices, the Hisense 75-inch is hard to beat. It delivers excellent performance, simple setup, and a feature set that rivals more expensive models.

title: Lg 75 inch qned
body:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

I’m very happy with my LG QNED TV. The picture quality is excellent, with beautiful colors, great brightness, and sharp details. The contrast is really good, and everything looks especially impressive when watching 4K movies and shows.

The TV has a sleek, modern design and looks great in our living room. The webOS interface is easy to use, and I really like having quick access to all the major streaming apps. The remote is also very convenient and responsive.

I’ve also noticed that the TV handles fast-moving scenes very well, which makes watching sports and action movies much more enjoyable. The upscaling is good too, so even content that isn’t 4K still looks clear.

Overall, I’m very impressed with the quality, features, and performance. It feels like a premium TV without being overly complicated to use. Definitely happy with the purchase and would recommend an LG QNED TV to anyone looking for a great picture and a modern smart TV experience.

title: Best tv in price range
body: The Hisense 55U78QG is one of the best value 55-inch TVs in its class. Its Mini-LED backlighting and Quantum Dot panel deliver excellent brightness, rich colours, and strong contrast, making movies and sports look vibrant and sharp. Gaming performance is a standout thanks to a 165Hz panel, VRR, ALLM, and very low input lag.  Google TV runs smoothly and offers all major apps, and the built-in speakers are surprisingly decent for everyday use. The main drawbacks are narrow viewing angles and some blooming in dark scenes, which is typical for many VA-panel TVs.  Overall, the 55U78QG offers premium-level picture quality and gaming features at a mid-range price, making it a great choice for bright rooms, movie lovers, and gamers.

title: My DREAM TV Upgrade for 2026!!! 📺
body:
I’ve been looking for a new premium TV to upgrade my living room for the new year, and I didn’t want to spend an arm and a leg for one so I got the 65” Hisense U88QG, which is one of the top premium MiniLED options on the market!

Now the first thing I noticed using this new TV was the crazy 5000 nits of peak brightness which means it gets plenty bright for daytime watching, not to mention having an anti-reflective coating so it still looks good from the side for when you have friends over! It’s also a MiniLED panel that uses quantum dots which if you don’t know what that is, basically means you get some really rich vibrant colours, that are actually accurate too so your favourite movies don’t look washed out! But as much as you might wanna binge watch, gaming is an epic experience too thanks to the 165hz refresh rate that actually supports AMD Freesync so everything feels smooth! There are even built-in top firing speakers with subwoofers in the back for Dolby Atmos surround sound which actually sounds shockingly good and cool, but not as cool as the built-in USB-C DisplayPort so I can easily plug my laptop in to use with the TV, or even a full on gaming PC if you wanna game on the TV!

Genuinely so happy with this TV upgrade and if you want something real nice for your living room this year, this is the one guys! Special shoutout and thanks to Hisense Canada for sending this TV over! 😊

title: 85Inch TV 85U88QG
body: I upgraded to the 85” Hisense U88QG after owning an OLED for a long time, and I was honestly nervous about losing those perfect blacks.  I can confidently say: I was surprised in the best possible way.  The black levels on this TV are outstanding for an LED. Local dimming is very aggressive, blooming is minimal, and in real content the contrast looks fantastic. In many scenes I simply stop thinking about the technology and just enjoy the image.  Where this TV really shocked me is brightness. HDR highlights, reflections, explosions, daylight scenes — they have an intensity my OLED simply could not reach. It makes movies and games feel incredibly dynamic.  Gaming is excellent. The Game Bar gives you real information, VRR works perfectly, motion is super smooth, and input lag feels very low. Playing on an 85” screen completely changes immersion.  Google TV runs fast, apps load quickly, and the overall experience feels premium.  Sound is also much better than I expected from built-in speakers.  Is OLED still king in a fully dark room for absolute black? Yes. But this TV fights back with size, brightness, and impact — and it does it very, very well.  For anyone afraid of moving from OLED to high-end Mini-LED: don’t be. This set delivers.  Highly recommended.

title: Blown away by brightness, gaming performance, and smart feat
body: This TV has exceeded expectations in almost every way. The Mini‑LED Pro backlight and Quantum Dot panel deliver an exceptionally bright, vibrant picture, and HDR movies look incredible with deep contrast and rich colour even in a bright room. The anti‑reflection screen also makes a noticeable difference, so daytime sports and shows are still clear without annoying glare. ​ For gaming, this set is a beast. The 165 Hz panel, Game Mode Ultra, VRR, and AMD FreeSync Premium Pro keep gameplay smooth and responsive with very low input lag, which is perfect for fast‑paced titles. Consoles and PC both look and feel great on this screen, and Auto Low Latency Mode means there is no need to constantly tweak settings.  The built‑in 4.1.2‑channel Dolby Atmos system is surprisingly powerful for a TV and does a good job with immersion for movies and games, thanks to the integrated subwoofer and upward‑firing speakers. Google TV runs smoothly, apps load quickly, and built‑in Google Assistant plus support for Alexa and Apple AirPlay make it easy to integrate into a smart home setup. Overall, this Hisense U88QG offers premium picture quality, excellent gaming features, and strong sound in a 55" package that feels like outstanding value. Highly recommended.

title: OS is slow
body:
I’ve had this TV for three days, and my main issue is its slow performance. Almost every button press has a noticeable delay, with the settings menu being the worst—it takes quite a while to open and navigate.

Other than that, there are several positives. WOW Orchestra works very well, and the sound integration is impressive. The picture quality is decent; the colours are good, although they aren’t quite as vibrant as I was hoping for. Brightness is strong and handles a sunlit room without any problems.

One thing that really stood out is the casting feature. It works smoothly and reliably, making it easy to stream content from other devices.

Overall, it’s a solid TV with good brightness, sound, and casting capabilities, but the sluggish interface prevents it from feeling as premium as it could.

body: ​Upgrading to this 98-inch Hisense TV has completely transformed our living room into a fully-fledged home cinema. The sheer scale of the 98-inch panel is breathtaking; it makes watching sports, movies, and gaming feel incredibly immersive, like you are sitting right in the middle of the action.   ​What surprised me most wasn't just the giant size, but the actual picture quality. The Quantum Dot technology ensures the colors are incredibly vibrant and punchy, and the brightness handles daytime viewing in a sunlit room effortlessly. For gaming, the smooth 144Hz refresh rate means there is zero lag or screen stuttering when playing fast-paced console games. Navigating through the built-in Google TV interface is snappy and makes finding our streaming apps a breeze If you have the wall space and are considering making the jump to a massive screen, this Hisense model offers incredible value and premium performance without breaking the bank compared to other brands. The sound quality is also surprisingly good for a TV in this price range, though adding a soundbar could enhance the audio for those who want a home theater experience. body: I bought this TV as an upgrade for the slighty larger screen (75" vs 65"). I'm very pleased at how it fits in my smallish Condo. Chose to have the TV wall mounted, which was a smart decision. One thing that has me a bit concerned is the TV started to possibly clitch. What I mean is the screen will cut off to a black screen, then come back on but with the sound gone. Desn't matter if it's set to Optical which uses my soundbar, or set to use the TV speakers. Oddly just turning it off/on seems to get the sound back. I did a restart and it still did the same thing. Now this doesn't happen constantly, but did happen enough yesterday to make it quite annoying. Today though, so far no issues so I really can't say if it's an issue with the TV or not. title: Fantastic value for high quality picture
body: The Hisense QD6 55-Inch TV is an impressive mid-range option that delivers excellent picture quality at an affordable price. Featuring Quantum Dot technology, it offers vibrant colors and sharp contrasts that make movies and shows come to life. The 4K resolution ensures crisp visuals, while its HDR capabilities (HDR10, HLG, and Dolby Vision) add depth to both bright and dark scenes.  The TV runs on the Google TV platform, which provides a smooth and intuitive interface for navigating apps like Netflix, YouTube, and Disney+. Voice control with Google Assistant is a handy feature, and the inclusion of built-in Chromecast makes it easy to stream content from your phone or tablet.  The design is sleek, with thin bezels that allow the screen to take center stage. The 60Hz refresh rate might not satisfy hardcore gamers looking for ultra-smooth motion, but for casual viewing and console gaming, it performs well. The built-in speakers are decent for the size, but you might want to pair it with a soundbar for a richer audio experience.  Overall, the Hisense QD6 55-Inch TV is a fantastic value for those seeking a high-quality picture, modern smart features, and a stylish design without breaking the bank.

title: Amazing clear TV compare to old Samsung
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The new Samsung Neo QLED 2026 model is to replace my aging half broken Samsung 55” (more than 10 years) LED TV. Installation to the wall is very simple. Samsung doesn’t include screws for wall mount. I had to remove the old TV and use the old screws. The new TV has very shallow mounting holes and I have to add spacer to the old longer screws to work. The placement of the mounts is also much narrower. If you don’t want to mount the TV on the wall, it does come with 2 stands to place the TV on a flat surface.
Setup is very straight forward. If you have a Samsung phone or a Gmail account, the TV will try to link up or back up what you have on your phone. But I skipped this step to make the setup faster. Later, I have the phone link up with the TV through the SmartThings app. Remote is a lot simpler to use compare to the old large one and you can use the phone app to control the TV
The picture quality is amazing and bright. Compared to my old TV, the new screen is much brighter and crystal clear. The upgrade almost feels like when people switched from old tube TVs to LED TVs. I actually have to tone down the brightness frok factory preset. This new TV has 4K resolution, and even regular YouTube content looks noticeably sharper and clearer when browsing.
There are a few hub connections in the back of the TV, includes 3 HDMI and one is eARC enabled, optical audio connection for sound bars, and couple USB connections which I used one for Amazon Firestick.
There are many features that I’m still trying to figure out with the new TV. However, the picture quality alone makes this a great TV option, especially if you’re looking for one at a good price.

title: QN70H: Great TV at an even greater price
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] What a Great TV! As a longtime Samsung owner, this latest model combines the best of Samsung’s Neo QLED 4K picture quality with its latest Tizen OS smart features, and all at a surprisingly reasonable price that won't break the bank. I've been an avid OLED fan for years, so was curious how Samsung’s NEO QLED compares. After testing this TV out for at least the past week, I can confirm it has such sharp, crisp picture quality and color that it can challenge even some mid-tier OLED TVs (only exception: it loses when it comes to perfect blacks). Based on my personal experience and the eyeball test, I believe the QN70H even bests OLEDs in terms of brightness and anti-glare screens. Our room has a lot of natural light so we definitely prioritize and need bright screens. It has all the smart features the higher end NEO QLEDs and OLEDs have, and I can hardly even tell what, if anything, I’m missing out on compared to those pricier versions. Setup was a breeze, the box wasn’t too heavy, and the TV can be either wall-mounted or placed on a TV stand that comes with it. All in all, a great TV I’d recommend to anyone.

title: Surprisingly Gentle for my first OLED.
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] My 77" model is from Australia so I get the QD-OLED version and this is my first OLED.
The colors and picture are so stunning they could sell tickets at the door. I didn’t realize OLEDs could beam that bright until my eyeballs threatened to unionize on the very first night, forcing me to dial back my HDR bravado. The AI upscaling is pure wizardry, transforming dusty old SD footage into something so crisp that, with my glasses on, it’s basically nostalgia strutting around in 4K cosplay. Some folks talk about contrast and raised blacks or lighter tones from the matte finish in daylight, but I haven’t noticed a thing, if anything, the matte finish moonlights as my personal anti-glare bodyguard.

My only hiccups so far have been:  
1. eARC decided to play hard to get with my Denon AVR, stubbornly sending PCM 2.0 no matter what I streamed or played. Then, as if by magic, it suddenly decided to behave, and now it’s all sunshine and surround sound.  
2. The Xbox GamePass app insists on AI Upscaling mode, because if I dare use Low Latency mode, it treats me to a thrilling black screen audio drama instead of an actual game.

title: Excellent OLED TV with impressive picture quality
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I've been extremely happy with the Samsung QA65S90H. The OLED panel delivers outstanding picture quality, with deep blacks, vibrant colours and excellent contrast that make movies, sports and streaming content look fantastic. The 4K upscaling does a great job with lower-resolution content, and the overall image is sharp and detailed.

One feature I particularly appreciate is how well the screen handles reflections, making it much easier to watch during the day in a bright room. The smart TV interface is responsive and easy to navigate, with all the major streaming apps available. Gaming performance has also been excellent thanks to the smooth motion and low input lag.

The design is sleek and modern, and the TV looks great mounted on the wall or on its stand. Setup was straightforward, and the sound quality is surprisingly good for a slim TV, although a soundbar would still enhance the experience.

Overall, the QA65S90H offers a premium viewing experience with excellent picture quality, strong smart features and great gaming performance. I would happily recommend it to anyone looking for a high-quality OLED TV.

body:

The resolution on this screen is absolutely awesome. Every scene is crystal clear, and the sheer size of the display makes total immersion a cinch. It genuinely feels like bringing the commercial theater experience right into your living room.
Incredible Built-In Sound
The biggest surprise is the audio. The way the sound travels and bounces around the room is incredible. It completely fills the space, making it almost unnecessary to buy an additional surround sound system or expensive soundbar.
Flawless Smart Features
Smart features can sometimes be clunky, but this TV has zero issues with my Alexa. It integrated into my smart home instantly and works flawlessly every single time.
The Ultimate Verdict
More than anything, this TV has brought my family closer together. My kids absolutely enjoy our cinema nights when they come over to spend time with their dad. Seeing their faces light up during movie nights makes this worth every single penny. Highly recommended!

title: Amazing TV
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I’ve been using the Samsung QN80H for a few weeks now, and it’s been a noticeable upgrade from older TV. The picture quality stands out right away, especially in darker scenes where blacks actually look dark instead of the grayish glow that you usually get. The contrast is impressive thanks to the Mini-LED backlighting, and bright scenes still pop without washing everything out. The AI picture features do a solid job in the background adjusting brightness, sharpening content, and even improving older, lower-resolution videos with upscaling, so you don’t really have to mess with settings much. It also includes Samsung’s automatic picture optimization, which helps fine-tune the image without needing a professional setup and eliminates the need for trying to figure out the best setting your self. 

The smart TV experience is smooth and convenient. All the major streaming apps like Netflix, YouTube, Hulu, Disney+, and Prime Video are built in and load quickly, so there’s really no need for an external streaming device. Navigation feels responsive, and the interface is easy enough to get used to after a little time. Gaming on a PS5 has also been great the high refresh rate make fps and racing games feel smooth and responsive, and overall motion handling is clean with no blur.

title: Thoroughly amazed..!
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] What a sweet surprise this was...  We unboxed the TV and we were happy to see that you can actually pick where you want the legs of the TV to go, either spread apart almost at the corners or more at the middle.  I don't recall ever seeing a TV that gives you that option, but boy is it a good one.. why?  Because it helps with cable management and also the atheistic of the TV change quite a bit depending on the stand placement. 

But let's get to the juicy details.. as soon as we turned it on to get the setup going, we were amazed.  The vibrant color, the SOUND,  the quality.. it was great.  We have quite a few TVs throughout the home and I can say without a doubt that this one is becoming my favorite, by a long shot.  The quality of the output it very sharp and makes everything look great.  We also enabled the dynamic sound and boy do we love that.  It adds more excitement to our TVs shows and movies, you truly do feel like it's immersing you in a deeper experience.  The remote is a standard size and it seems like they just did that on purpose as there is a lot of "dead" space on it.  So they made it big enough to fit comfortably in your hand.

One negative thing that I'll point out about it is that the glare is pretty bad on the TV, we tried different angles but nothing seemed to truly work when watching it during the day time with the shades open.  So for maximum enjoyment I would say that you need to place it where it gets the least amount of sun exposure.. or like us, enjoy it at night time :)

Aside from that, I highly recommend it.  Fits all of our needs and the picture quality is truly amazing.  5/5

title: Viewing Experience
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Upgrading from a 55-inch to the Samsung Neo QLED 75-inch has been an absolute game changer for our home. The difference in size alone makes everything feel so much more immersive for movies, sport, even everyday TV just feel bigger and more cinematic.

The picture quality is incredible. The brightness, contrast, and colour are on another level, and the detail is so sharp it almost feels 3D at times. Dark scenes look deep and rich, while bright scenes really pop without being overwhelming.. The sound is also much better than expected for a flat-screen TV, giving a more surround-like feel without needing a sound bar.

Overall, this upgrade has completely transformed our viewing experience. If you're thinking about going bigger, I’d absolutely recommend it — the jump from 55” to 75” is 100% worth it.

title: Beautiful TV
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Recently, I thought I would only buy OLED TVs from now on. After using this TV I have to say QLED is right up there in terms of picture quality. Setting up the TV was very easy. It was a very different experience from setting up any other TV I’ve had before. I’m in the Samsung ecosystem and the setup went through SmartThings. Nice and easy. Now, I do not prefer the standard setup of any TV. You always get that soap opera effect. So, I had to do some digging to turn it off. Normally, it’s as easy as looking for something called ‘smooth motion’. Problem is every manufacturer has a different name for it. For the life of me I was unable to find it but I did find the judder setting. I had lowered it all the way down to remove the effect. I’m still going to play around and tweak it further but that was my priority. Right now, I’m testing all the AI features built in. Sound seems to be really good. There is actually some bass or low tones that come through very well. I have this TV mounted in a spare bedroom so MAYBE it’s a little too big for the space but who cares! Watching sports has been great. The blacks are black and the motion is smooth. No weird artifacts. In my case, for my living room, I’m probably sticking with OLED but if I don’t have OLED money I’m going QLED. The TV handles bright windows great as well. My opinion, this purchase was a great decision!

title: Samsung QN90F 98‑inch Neo QLED Flagship
body:
The Samsung QN90F 98‑inch Neo QLED delivers stunning, glare-resistant visuals, immersive HDR performance, powerful gaming features, and a refined smart TV experience. If you're after a truly massive, ultra-bright screen with sleek body that performs exceptionally well in both daylight and dark environments, this is easily one of the most impressive TVs available in 2025.

I was initially considering the TCL CK8, but after noticing visible micro-LED structure and ghosting in 4K content, I had concerns about how it would handle SDR. Thankfully, I held off—and ended up getting a special offer on the QN90F instead. Also it looks better in anti glare mode.

This TV is huge—it literally fills the wall—and the 4K brightness is incredible. I absolutely love it. That said, a few picture tweaks are needed for different types of content to get the best experience.

Like all F1 cars are capable of winning the race—it still depends on who’s driving. 😉 Same with this TV: dial it in right, and it’s unbeatable.

The Neo Slim Design is sleek and modern, adding a stylish touch to any space without being bulky.Smart features are robust as expected—fast interface, voice control, and easy access to all major streaming apps. title: Blown Away by the Upgrade!
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I recently upgraded from a 10-year-old Samsung Series 8 (65") to this model, and it’s been a game changer. The TV sits next to large windows and directly across from sliding doors, so I was worried about glare—but the anti-reflective screen handles ambient light beautifully. The picture quality is outstanding, with rich colors and incredible brightness.

Setup was simple using the SmartThings app, and the included remote is fantastic—it now controls my Fetch TV and amplifier seamlessly. I also love having Alexa built-in, especially the option to use voice commands even when the TV is off.
Highlights:

    Stunning brightness and color
    Anti-glare screen works perfectly, even in bright rooms
    Super easy setup with SmartThings App
    Fantastic remote—controls all my devices effortlessly
    Alexa integration is a great touch

Opportunities for Improvement:
    Some TV settings are poorly explained, both on-screen and in the manual.
    Occasionally notice flickering between color tones—hoping future firmware updates improve this.
    The Art Mode feature is a nice addition, but I’d love the option to display art while in standby or when motion is detected, especially with such a large screen.

Final Verdict:
This TV delivers a cinematic experience at home. It’s easy to use, packed with features, and the display is phenomenal. Very glad I chose this over the QN90D. Highly recommend!

title: 75" Neo QLED QN92F 4K Vision AI Smart TV
body:
The Samsung 75″ Neo QLED QN92F 4K Vision AI Smart TV delivers an impressive overall viewing experience. The picture quality is excellent, with sharp details, vibrant colors, strong contrast, and excellent brightness. The large 75″ screen makes movies, sports, and 4K content feel immersive, and the smart features are smooth and easy to use.

However, the Sound Quality was Disappointing compared with what I expected from a TV in this premium price range. The audio lacks the richness, depth, and powerful bass I was hoping for, and I personally didn’t enjoy the sound experience. A sound bar or external audio system would definitely improve it.

Overall, the QN92F is an excellent TV for picture quality, brightness, design, and smart features, but Samsung could have done much better with the built-in speakers. If you care about sound quality as much as picture quality, you may want to budget for a sound bar.

The brightness is excellent for an OLED panel, and HDR content looks vibrant without washing out darker scenes. Contrast is where this TV really stands out — blacks are deep and true, making movies and shows look incredibly cinematic, especially in a dark room.

The 4K resolution is super sharp, and streaming content from Netflix, YouTube, and gaming consoles looks detailed and clean. Even older content upscales surprisingly well. Viewing angles are also great since the picture quality stays consistent even when watching from the side, which is perfect for family movie nights or sports gatherings.

The refresh rate and motion handling are smooth for gaming and fast-action sports. Gameplay feels responsive with minimal blur, and movies run smoothly without noticeable stuttering. Samsung’s smart features and AI enhancements also make navigating apps and adjusting picture settings simple and quick.

What really surprised me most is the value for money. In my opinion, this TV is top of the range for the price. You get premium OLED picture quality, excellent gaming performance, smart features, and a sleek design without paying the extreme prices of some competing models.

Overall, this TV delivers premium picture quality, smooth performance, and outstanding value. I’d definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a high-end OLED TV with impressive brightness, contrast, resolution, viewing angles, refresh performance, and great bang for the buck.

title: 83" of Absolute Display Perfection on the Wall
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The Star of the Show: Samsung S90H 83"

​Getting an 83-inch panel up on the wall is a serious project, but once mounted, it completely anchors the room. More importantly, the display performance matches the massive physical presence.

​Contrast: The black levels are absolute zero. Dark scenes are deep and precise, creating an incredible contrast ratio where bright highlights pop without any haloing or light bleed into the shadows.

​Brightness: It easily handles ambient daylight. The panel pushes serious luminance, keeping colors vibrant and specular HDR highlights crisp even in a bright room.

​Uniformity: Screen uniformity on a panel this huge can be a gamble, but this screen is flawless. Zero "dirty screen effect" (DSE), no banding, and perfectly even color distribution edge-to-edge during wide panning shots.

​Upscaling: The onboard picture engine does heavy lifting. Compressed 1080p streaming content is sharpened intelligently without looking over-processed, bringing older feeds impressively close to native 4K quality.

​Responsiveness: Motion processing is rock-solid and the pixel response time is instantaneous. Menu navigation is snappy, and high-frame-rate content feels fluid with zero noticeable input lag or motion blur.

​The Setup Context
​I ran a single-cable eARC connection down to a Samsung Q990H soundbar to complete the audio side of the build. It syncs automatically, handles the high-bitrate audio formats, and keeps the entire wall-mounted setup visually minimal with zero wire clutter.

​Verdict:
Flagship picture quality, flawless panel uniformity, and elite processing. If you're wall-mounting an 83-inch TV, this is the gold standard.
