title: Absolutely Great TV
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I absolutely love the S90H! 

First things first, the build quality is quite good. The TV itself is impressively thin and setting it up on a stand was rather straight forward. However, I didn't have it on the stand for very long, as this TV looks even better wall mounted. It can get very flush with the wall, so flush you could almost convince people it's a piece of art hanging on your wall.

Speaking of art, the pictures I took don’t do it any justice! The colors absolutely pops when watching movies and gaming. The anti-reflective coating makes it great for both day and nighttime viewing. My room has a trapezoidal window that's difficult to cover, so daytime light is unavoidable. This TV absolutely handles it like a champ! On most TVs, just a little light will turn the entire screen into a mirror. When the TV is off, you can see how the light diffuses across the screen but when actually watching content it completely disappears. In the image of Mario Kart World (on Rainbow Road in the stars) you can somewhat see it in the top right corner, but in most scenarios you are never going to notice it.

One thing that definitely surprised me with this TV is the sound quality. When I first turned it on, I put on Jeopardy and thought, “Wow the dialogue is pretty good!” Obviously Jeopardy isn’t a great test of audio quality, which is why I decided to watch Encanto! The opening song was a tad worrying, since the instruments were louder than the vocals. However, I think that might be a problem with the audio mix, because every other song sounded great! I wanted to test the AI audio features, however I couldn’t turn off the AI video features, which were not to my liking.

Finally, gaming on this TV was amazing! There are a few quirks with getting HDR set up on the Switch 2, but there are countless videos that help. Playing Pokopia was a blast! Seeing all the colors pop on the screen and hearing the game’s soundtrack on this TV was a real treat. 

I would highly recommend this TV to anyone as it looks fantastic! I can’t wait to watch more movies and games on it!

title: Superb
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] This was the first ever TV that I bought for myself, thinking it would be ideal for my bedroom. It has been exactly that. Both the sound and picture quality are excellent, and the ease of use is remarkable. Having multiple remotes provided is useful, as I can use one to quickly access streaming platforms and the other when I want to watch live TV quickly. The auto brightness adjustment feature has been most beneficial when I am watching TV in the dark, and again in the full shine of the sun. It is also great for gaming on, having tested it with Nvidia Geforce Now. Two things to be aware of with gaming, though:
1. The TV will not exceed 60 hertz if it is not in 'Game Mode', which in itself is only possible when the TV is connected via HDMI to a console or PC. So if you are using platforms like Nvidia Geforce Now, you will only be able to achieve a maximum of 60 fps.
2. If you are using a cloud platform and have to sign in to an account in a game, (for example signing into your Xbox account when playing Forza) you cannot do this with either of the remotes provided, or an Xbox controller. In my case, I had to plug in a wireless keyboard and mouse to enter my account information. This is something that can be easily fixed by having an on-screen keyboard, but alas it was missing.

Overall, however, I have been remarkably impressed with this TV and would definitely recommend it!

title: Surprisingly Gentle for my first OLED.
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] My 77" model is from Australia so I get the QD-OLED version and this is my first OLED.

I didn’t realize OLEDs could beam that bright until my eyeballs threatened to unionize on the very first night, forcing me to dial back my HDR bravado. The AI upscaling is pure wizardry, transforming dusty old SD footage into something so crisp that, with my glasses on, it’s basically nostalgia strutting around in 4K cosplay. Some folks talk about contrast and raised blacks or lighter tones from the matte finish in daylight, but I haven’t noticed a thing, if anything, the matte finish moonlights as my personal anti-glare bodyguard.

My only hiccups so far have been:  
1. eARC decided to play hard to get with my Denon AVR, stubbornly sending PCM 2.0 no matter what I streamed or played. Then, as if by magic, it suddenly decided to behave, and now it’s all sunshine and surround sound.  
2. The Xbox GamePass app insists on AI Upscaling mode, because if I dare use Low Latency mode, it treats me to a thrilling black screen audio drama instead of an actual game.

title: One of the best OLEDs in the Market
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] After evaluating the 55-inch Samsung S90H OLED TV, I’m particularly impressed by the panel’s ability to deliver precise luminance control at the pixel level. The OLED structure enables true black levels with effectively infinite contrast, and this is evident in how well the display maintains shadow detail without introducing visible blooming or halo artifacts. Near-black performance is especially noteworthy, with smooth gradation that avoids banding in darker scenes.

Peak brightness is strong for an OLED panel, which helps sustain specular highlights and improves HDR impact. Highlights retain detail rather than clipping, and the tone mapping appears well-calibrated, balancing brightness with color accuracy. The color volume is also robust, allowing the panel to maintain saturation even at higher luminance levels, which contributes to a more lifelike image.

From a motion standpoint, the panel’s fast response time minimizes blur, and motion interpolation can be adjusted to reduce judder without introducing an artificial “soap opera” effect. Native refresh handling ensures consistent playback across different frame rates, which is noticeable when switching between cinematic and broadcast content.

Upscaling performance is solid, with effective noise reduction and edge refinement that preserves detail without over-sharpening. Compression artifacts are handled reasonably well, especially in streamed content.

The smart interface runs smoothly with minimal latency, and general responsiveness supports a seamless user experience. Build quality is excellent, with a thin panel design that feels structurally sound.

Overall, the S90H demonstrates strong technical execution across contrast, brightness, color accuracy, and motion handling, making it a highly capable display for both everyday viewing and more demanding visual content.

title: Very nice picture
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] This TV is honestly one of those where you notice the difference right away. The OLED screen makes everything look better. Blacks are actually black, colors pop more, and it just looks way sharper than a normal TV.
One of the big things it has is Samsung’s Gen3 processor, which basically cleans up whatever you’re watching and upscales it closer to 4K. So even older shows still look pretty solid. 
It also has OLED HDR+, which helps with contrast and brightness, so you see more detail in dark and bright scenes. Movies especially look really good because of that.
If you watch sports or play games, it’s super smooth too. It can go up to 144Hz with so everything looks clean and not blurry when things move fast. 
Gaming wise, it’s built for it. It has HDMI 2.1, fast refresh rates and it has VRR support, so it keeps up with newer consoles without lag.
The smart side is easy. It runs on Samsung’s Tizen system, so all your apps like Netflix, YouTube and others are right there and load quick. You can also use voice control if you want. 
It’s also super thin and looks clean mounted or on a stand, so it doesn’t feel bulky at all.
This is just a really solid TV. Great picture, smooth performance, and packed with features that actually make a difference when you’re using it every day.

title: No more reflections!
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Upgrading to this 55” OLED was a huge change in more ways than one.

1. Display – an OLED display with a matte finish works perfectly for my bright room. Its screen is plenty bright enough to be viewable where the blacks still look very much deep black. The matte finish doesn’t take away from the picture quality at all. The best part of the of a matte screen is the lack of reflection in a bright room which makes the experiencing of watching TV less distracting during the day.

2. Sound – I was really impressed by the audio from this TV. It has depth, range, and a richness I would expect from a soundbar. The TV’s volume also gets very loud. The audio is still very clear at a higher volume as well. With all confidence, I won’t be going with my sound bar and just using the audio from the TV instead. It’s that good especially for a small room I have the TV in.

3. Ecosystem – I have Samsung appliances, tablets, earbuds, and the like and these devices integrates with the TV seamlessly. They automatically connect once the devices are turned on. I’m able to get notifications on my TV as to when my laundry is done or my oven has preheated. I find it really useful if your already in the ecosystem

4. Form – This thin but the bottom of the TV does provide confidence in mounting this TV on wall mount. The bezel less design makes the TV look really good where it becomes a centerpiece in my room. In terms of heat, the panel doesn’t really get too warm where it would warm the room.

Overall – this TV fits the bill for all my needs

title: The Best TV I've Ever Owned
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Where do I start! This Samsung TV is literally the best I've ever owned and seen with my own two eyes. As I unboxed, I immediate noticed how super thin the edges are, literally thinner than my monitor which was shocking. I was so worried that there would be a crack or a dent from the shipment because of how thin the upper edges are. The lower half of the TV is a bit thicker as it had the meat and potatoes of the screen inside, but still very thin compared to other TVs of the recent past. 
The colors! This TV has such deep blacks, and such a range of color, it is incredible. Whether watching the NCAA final four tournament, or watching an episode of Game of Thrones, the colors are stunning and visually satisfying. Ai is built in to help with colors and things if you allow it which is pretty cool. 
I have a PS5 and have played NBA 2K, Assassin's Creed Mirage, and Ghost of Tsushima, I almost dropped drooled at the graphics on these games. So crisp, so clean, and there's a whole set of game mode settings which allow you to make adjustments that you'd like for your preferred viewing. 
The sound! This is the first TV I've ever had or been around where the sound sounds like they have real speakers built in! There is base, treble, all of the things and if I didn't already have a sound bar and a music frame, I wouldn't feel the need to buy one! 
The one thing I don't like. There is an auto detection mode where if you walk by the screen, it automatically turns on to the brief page (which gives you a summary of current events, weather, music). I don't like this mode so I turned it to manual instead. 
This TV is a 12/10, I don't see myself changing for years to come.

title: High contrast, visual new experiences
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I hadn’t upgraded the TV in my bedroom for 10 years! So I knew I had a lot to gain when I bought this OLED TV, which has been a dream of mine. Assembling the stand and putting it on my furniture was pretty easy!! I needed just a hand to move it correctly.I did most of it by myself. The screen is very slim. Instantly it has a modern look. Although I can’t really see the anti-glare film on the screen , I have already noticed it has less glare than my previous TV.  The set up was easy and it prompted me to download the SmartThings app. There were a few instances where I felt like the operating system was asking for too many privacy permissions.  My phone is a remote control through the SmartThings app and the physical remote control is very responsive and slim. The voice command button on the remote does not work, I don’t know why, I did plenty of trouble shooting. The feature works on my phone remote though and I can search things with AI (bixby). A lot of the times it misunderstands me or takes me away from what I want on the TV so I don’rt use the AI search feature unless I am desperate. 
 Installing my apps was easy, but I had to figure out Samsung‘s App Store, which I had never used before. It was straightforward and logging into my apps was easy ‘cause  I can use a QR code.
Now to the TV itself, the picture. The screen is VERY bright so I am very happy with that! In the past when I’m watching my favorite shows that have clandestine sneaky, dark scenes such as basically anything in the Game of Thrones series.On my old TV I couldn’t really see what was happening in the dark and that’s the reason I wanted to upgrade. This TV is a game changer in terms of the clarity of dark scenes!! When this TV really really blows me away is in high contrast scenes such as tribal council in survivor where you have rich blacks, and then fire. This looks amazing on this Oled screen. Having this clear high contest picture brings me to a new level enjoying drama and my whole family has noticed the difference. Also the TV OS is very fast and it makes a cool old timey blip when I turn the TV off. Overall I am happy with the tv, the picture and sound are both great.

title: Great picture quality and sound.
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The Samsung 55" OLED has been a great addition to my game room. The side profile is surprisingly thin in person and it’s impressive how much picture quality they packed into something that slim. Setup was easy and the legs were simple to attach without any issues. It’s a little heavier than another Samsung model I own, but maybe that comes from the higher end tech inside. The picture quality is where it really stands out. Colors look rich and accurate, and the contrast is a big improvement over what I was using before. I’ve been playing my Nintendo Switch on it and games like Zelda look incredible. OLED brings out details that regular LED just can’t match. The sound quality has been excellent on its own, even without a soundbar, so I haven’t felt the need to add anything else. With all the streaming apps already built in, I haven’t needed to plug in anything extra. The smart interface is clean, quick, and easy to use, and everything loads smoothly. Overall, I would definitely choose this TV again. It’s a solid upgrade and the picture quality alone makes it worth it. The solar powered remote is also a nice touch and something I hadn’t seen before.

title: Fantastic Budget TV
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I've been using the 43-inch M70H for both everyday entertainment and gaming, and it's exceeded my expectations. After spending some time adjusting the picture settings, the image quality really comes to life. The brightness is excellent for daytime viewing, while the contrast provides deep blacks and vibrant colors that make movies and games look fantastic.
One thing that really stood out is the screen uniformity. Large bright scenes and darker scenes look clean and consistent without distracting patches or uneven lighting. The TV is also very responsive, making menu navigation feel smooth and gameplay enjoyable with very little noticeable delay.
I also appreciate how much control Samsung gives over picture calibration. Being able to fine-tune the image made it easy to find a look that feels natural and accurate for my room. Whether I'm watching shows, playing games, or streaming videos, the picture stays sharp and immersive.
Overall, this has been a reliable, high-quality TV that delivers an excellent viewing experience. It's easy to recommend to anyone looking for a well-rounded display with great picture quality and responsive performance.

title: Very good in it's class and range!
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] In it's class and price range the Samsung M70H Series Mini LED 4K tv is really exceptional. The color is rich and uniform across the screen and the contrast is deep and all facets of the picture have a good range of adjustment. The picture is very bright and the sound is more than acceptable so external speakers are not a necessity. The other feature which works well is the judder control. Using it motion is very smooth, even more so than tv's costing much more. The blacks are acceptable in day or brighter room lights but are not inky in lower light situations. If it had local dimming on the array (which it does not) this would be better. The only other thing that could use a bit of improvement is the off angle viewing which becomes washed out fairly quickly. So for straight on or nearly so viewing it is an easy budget conscious recommendation but if you have off angle seating... I would look elsewhere. Still all in all a good value and nice picture with good motion control.

title: Best 55in TV There Is
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I bought this Samsung 55” Class M70H Mini LED 4K for our family room a few weeks ago and have been really happy with it so far. The first thing that I noticed was how bright the picture is. We get a lot of daylight in the room, and the TV still looks great without having to close the blinds. viewing angle is also really good and you can stand anywhere in the room without odd colors. My kid streams shows on it constantly now that it's summer and I also have watched several games and movies without any complaints or gripes on picture quality.

Setup was straightforward and only took a few minutes. The Tizen menu is easy to navigate and we were able to jump right into streaming apps after an easy wi-fi connection setup. I was, as usual with wall-mounts, expecting to need a soundbar, but we don't with this set. Overall feels like a very premium TV. I also paired it with my SmartThings app and I can use that app to see my laundry, dishwasher, fridge and now TV! If you are looking for a 55in LED TV, please consider this model when shopping. Solid TV for our family usage.

title: Perfect Family TV
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] We've been using the Samsung 55-inch M70H Mini LED TV as our main family television, and it has been a fantastic addition to our home. It was surprisingly easy to set up, the remote is laid out well and the SmartThings app makes it easy to monitor my other Samsung appliances.

The Mini LED technology provides strong contrast and bright, detailed images, while Samsung's 4K upscaling helps older content look clearer and more enjoyable. The Motion Xcelerator feature keeps fast-moving scenes smooth, which has been especially great for watching sports and action movies together.

What we appreciate most is how easy the TV is for the whole family to use. The Tizen smart platform gives us quick access to streaming apps, Samsung TV Plus,, while built-in support for Apple AirPlay, Google Cast (what we use), and voice assistants makes sharing content simple. The sound quality is surprisingly immersive thanks to Object Tracking Sound Lite and Q-Symphony compatibility, and the overall experience feels premium for a family living room. Whether we're having movie nights, gaming, or just relaxing with our favorite shows, the Samsung M70H has delivered reliable performance and excellent value.

title: Great purchase!
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] We were looking to replace our bedroom television. The set was almost 20 years old and just not giving us the experience we wanted. Enter the Samsung 55” M70H Mini LED in 4K

Cons

* No direct voice control.

* Sound could be better, but it’s good overall. 

Overall, this is a great buy. The price point is extremely reasonable and we may  officially be a Samsung tv household.

title: Vibrant colors
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Honest Review – Great Sound, Strong Picture, But Needs Some Tweaking
After spending some time with this TV, I’d say it’s a solid overall experience with a few things worth noting.
First, the sound quality really stands out. I wasn’t expecting much from built-in speakers, but this one is surprisingly full and clear. Dialogue comes through crisp, and it has enough depth that I haven’t felt the need to immediately add a soundbar.
The picture quality is generally very good—bright, sharp, and easy to see even in a room with a lot of natural light. It handles daytime viewing well, which was important for my setup. That said, I’ve had a harder time getting the color settings just right. Depending on the content, tones can look a little off or overly saturated, and it takes some adjusting to find a balance that looks natural.
I also experienced an occasional screen glitch where part of the image briefly distorts or shifts horizontally. It doesn’t happen constantly, but when it does, it’s definitely noticeable and interrupts the viewing experience.
On the plus side, the TV itself looks sleek and modern, and setup was quick and easy.
Overall: great sound, strong brightness and clarity, but color calibration and occasional screen issues hold it back a bit. If those were ironed out, this would easily be a top-tier experience.    I did contact Samsung and they were able to help me resolve my problems! They were very helpful and nice!

title: Unreal
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] First, let me just say that upon receiving the box, it was extremely light.   I have had many t v s over the years fifty five inch up and I have never felt or handled the t v that was so lightweight at this size. It's so easy to set up and move if needed.

Next, Right out of the box, the setup was extremely easy and I even used the SmartThings app.\nAs this was the first t v I ever tried it with. Within 2 minutes, it was not only set up in all my accounts were there, but everything was signed in and it even set up the TV just like my projector and my other t v!

Next, I have seen great image quality on products from this brand but this one takes the cake. The blacks were much deeper.The colors were more vibrant , and I even had to tone down the brightness , because the t v itself would light up my entire living space in the evening and it was almost too bright. When?\nSmooth, TV's first came out versus tube TV's.I remember my eyes having to adjust to a great picture quality versus when I was used to.  And this is almost the same.  There is a difference vs even my led 4k tv.

Next, sound on t v's like this have always been hit or miss. On my older models, I would have to change the soundtrack to 2.1 channel versus 5.1 channel just because scenes with a lot of action would be too loud but scenes when people talk would be too soft.  Not only does this alleviate that , but the sound actually seems to come from certain sides of the t v , depending on where the dialogue is or the action is , which is very clear to understand but it also seems like the sound moves with the scene!

Lastly, I was very skeptical about using AI on a TV.But after trying this out , it's just like using a I on the phone only it's tailored to images, movies, music and videos.  I gave the AI several task of finding pictures.Short clips, movies and even things that I knew the title of but just described a part of a scene to see if it would find it and it never missed!

Very well made tv!

title: My 2nd Samsung  Tv
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I'm really happy with my Samsung TV overall. The picture quality is definitely the standout for me The brightness is excellent, especially in a bright room, and the contrast gives the image a really nice sense of depth. Colors look vibrant without being overdone, and everything just looks sharp clean, and detailed
I'm also very pleased with the screen uniformity. Bright and dark areas look consistent, and I haven't noticed anything distracting that takes away from the viewing experience,
The responsiveness of the TV did take a bit of getting used to. The menus, apps, and general interface feel a little different from what I was used to, so there was a bit of a learning curve. That said, once you spend some time with it, it becomes easier and more intuitive
My main disappointment is the sound. I would much rather have the TV audio go through my AV receiver and external speaker setup. The built-in speakers are fine, but if you already have a proper audio system, the integration could definitely be smoother and more straightforward
Overall though, I'm very pleased with it. The brightness, contrast, vibrancy, sharpness, and overall picture quality are all excellent. There's a bit of adjustment needed with the interface, and I'd prefer better integration with an external receiver for sound, but none of that really takes away from how good the picture is
Great picture and a very enjoyable TV overall

title: Love the picture, the remote and menus not so much
body: This is a re-write of my review, as requested by Samsung:  For the picture on this TV I would give it 5-stars.  The picture and the screen's abilities to provide an excellent picture are outstanding.  It is able to provide anything you might prefer from quite dim to absolutely brilliantly bright.  Contrast can be adjusted to the same level of extremes as the brightness.  The uniformity of the picture is also all that you could ask of a set, especially in this price range.  Being a 4K TV, its ability to upscale is something to really appreciate and is apparent when watching media that was made pre-1080I, as the upscaling feature does improve the lower resolution of those productions in most cases.  The sound is fairly decent considering the set is a simple two-speaker, down-firing system, with a relatively low-powered amplifier.  Sadly though, like so many manufacturers today have done, the only audio out is for optical devices only.  Long gone are any "legacy" hook-ups and I should point out here that not only includes the sound output, buy the video input as well.  You can no longer use RGB, component or even the traditional fall-back default of RCA composite connections.  There's HDMI in and Optical audio out.  There is a single USB A port that can be used to input from USB memory media devices for movies, videos, etc.  All of these things are pluses for this set and we like them.  Now, for what we don't like:  One, the included remote is sorely lacking in what it is able to control on the TV, mostly due to it being done in a "minimalist" style.  What I'm saying here is Samsung has attempted to move as much control from the included remote to the screen itself.  If you've been paying attention to what has been happening in new cars with the manufacturers removing buttons and knobs from the dashboards, and placing them on a screen on the dash instead, well they've done on this TV.  Samsung has tried to strike a similar aesthetic here on this TV and probably all of their sets.  To put it simply, we don't like what they've done.  The few buttons that remain on the remote are very poorly labeled, and some of them don't move in an intuitive manner.  For example, there are two very small rectangular buttons that stick up from the surface of the remote about 1/16th of an inch.  It took me quite some time to realize you needed to use these to change the channel, but you don't "push down" to get a response.  You must "catch" the top edge of these little buttons to "rock" or "nudge" them either forward or backward.  If you're anything like the average person you will frequently find your fingers simply sliding over the top of the button because they're very small, they do not stick up very far and the plastic is very smooth, almost slippery.  This is very much how the design of the entire included remote is done.  Not easy to use, almost indecipherable and actually small enough that you can easily have it fall out your hand if you aren't careful with it.  Now, our second dislike and it looms large for us.  This isn't our first 4K Samsung set.  Our first Samsung 4K set is now about 10 years old, but its menu system is far more intuitive, logical and understandable.  Our new MiniLED set's menus are very trying, not logical and many times the only way to actually pull something up that you want is to use the search function.  We are keeping the TV because we love the picture and sound, and we found an excellent work-around so that we can use our new set.  The remote from our 10 year old Samsung 4K set works perfectly with the new set, and the way it was laid out brings back the logic and control that was missing due to the included remote being almost useless for us.  With the old remote we now can access every feature on this new TV and do not have to hunt and depend on moving a little cursor around on the screen to back control.  Good TV, bad remote and software.

title: Brighter Than Most, But Falls Short Outdoors
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] We set this TV up on our beach property under a shaded structure, where cutting through heavy sunlight and reflections is our main goal. Compared to a standard 4K LCD TV, this model is noticeably brighter and performs significantly better in ambient light.

​However, it still falls a bit short of what we were hoping for in our specific setup. Even under shade, the outdoor glare and natural brightness are tough to overcome, and it doesn't quite cut through the reflections as much as we needed during peak daylight hours.

​It's a solid, vibrant TV that would probably excel in a bright indoor living room, but if you're using it in an outdoor covered patio or beach setup, it might still leave you wishing for a bit more glare resistance and peak brightness.

body:

There is no way to disable the autoplay (or everything I've tried so far isn't working) so shortly after starting the TV it automatically starts playing one of the previous programs. body:

title: Poor user interface
body:
This is thee worst user interface I've ever used on any TV in my lifetime. I had a 65" Samsung TV and it was nice, that's why I bumped up to a 75". Big mistake. All the user controls are hidden in a maze of confusion that takes you minutes to find for adjustment. For live TV you literally have to go and make sure the guide is on which ever TV channels you're using. If you're watching Samsung TV and you switch to OTA content, want to change the channel, you literally have to go back into the maze, find the menu for OTA channels and click on that or your channel will change back to Samsung TV channels. Super horrible interface!!
Next, there's no optical out. WHAT IN THE WORLD‽‽
99% of the home theater systems use optical for their audio. But not this one, right? If your system doesn't support eARC audio, you're screwed...
Next, when you watch a streaming service, it automatically switches from whatever TV screen mode you're using, over to film maker mode. Yup... You now have to go back into the maze and manually turn your mode back to whatever you were using...
In short, whoever developed the user interface for this TV should, needs to be fired!!!
This will be the last Samsung TV that I'll ever buy, FACT!!

title: Best TV of 2026
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I recently purchased the Crystal UHD 2026 TV, and overall, I have been very impressed with the experience. From the moment I set it up, the TV felt like a significant upgrade from my previous television. The design is modern, slim, and clean, so it looks great whether it is mounted on the wall or placed on a TV stand.
The picture quality is one of the biggest strengths of this TV. Colors look bright and vibrant without appearing overly artificial, while the 4K resolution provides plenty of detail. Watching movies and TV shows is particularly enjoyable because the picture feels sharp and clear. I also noticed that scenes with a lot of detail, such as nature documentaries and action movies, look especially impressive. The contrast and overall picture balance are good for everyday viewing, although the experience can vary depending on the lighting in the room.

Another thing I really like is how easy the TV is to use. The interface is straightforward, and navigating between streaming services and other features feels smooth. Apps load quickly, and having access to popular streaming platforms makes it convenient to watch everything in one place. The remote is also simple to understand, which is helpful if you don't want to spend a lot of time figuring out complicated controls.

The sound quality is decent for a built-in TV speaker system. Voices are generally clear, and the sound is perfectly adequate for everyday watching. However, if you want a more immersive cinema-like experience, I would recommend adding a soundbar or external speakers.

Overall, the Crystal UHD 2026 TV offers an excellent combination of picture quality, smart features, design, and ease of use. It is a great choice for watching movies, sports, streaming content, and regular television. For the price, I think it provides very good value and has made my everyday viewing experience much more enjoyable. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a reliable, modern 4K TV.

title: My New TV
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The Samsung U8000 TV has completely redefined our home entertainment experience, delivering premium quality at an incredible value. Right out of the box, the modern, minimalist design catches your eye. The ultra-slim bezels create an elegant, edge-to-edge display that looks stunningly sleek mounted on the wall or placed on a media console.When it comes to visual performance, the 4K display is breathtaking. The clarity is exceptionally sharp, bringing out fine textures and subtle details in every scene. The color expression is remarkably vivid, offering bright, punchy hues alongside deep contrast that makes movies and nature documentaries truly come alive. Even during fast-moving action sequences or intense gaming sessions, the refresh rate keeps up beautifully, providing a consistently crisp and fluid picture without any motion blur.Equally impressive is the smart platform. Samsung’s user interface is incredibly fast and intuitive, making it seamless to switch between live TV and favorite streaming applications. The voice control integration works flawlessly, allowing for hands-free navigation and quick content searches.To round it all out, the audio performance delivers clean, robust sound that remains distortion-free even at higher volumes. This television strikes the ultimate balance between top-tier innovation and everyday user-friendliness. The Samsung U8000 is a fantastic investment that has exceeded all my expectations for family movie nights and casual viewing alike!

Setup was easy and quick with the smart things app.

One thing that really stands out is the huge amount of free streaming content built right into the TV and apps. Having access to thousands of free channels without needing another subscription is a nice bonus and makes it easy to always find something to watch.

The tV  also does a solid job keeping fast action smooth, especially during sports and gaming. And even older shows or lower quality content look noticeably better because of the 4K upscaling feature.

Overall, this TV feels like a really good balance of quality, features, and value. It’s easy to use, looks great in a living room or bedroom, and works well whether you’re watching movies, gaming, or just relaxing with family at the end of the day.

title: Great picture
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The picture quality on the Samsung is excellent.  It also offers a variety of programmed picture modes to change your view as well as individual brightness, etc controls.  I naturally had to buy external speakers, but the speakers on the Samsung tv are superior to other brands I've purchased.  They're just not suitable for quality sound.  Once my Samsung external soundbar was connected, I could control the sound quality from the tv.  I wasn't able to do this with my prior Roku tv external speakers.  I'm not crazy about the volume control on the remote.  I had to go to You Tube to figure out how to do it as the instruction manual didn't specify it.  I'm using my TiVo remote to control the volume because of this.   I'm able to install all of my streaming apps and easily organize them on the Samsung home screen with no problem. There are so many options to tweek picture quality, that I think just about anyone can find the view that pleases them.  I've had numerous brands of televisions over the years, and overall, I would recommend the Samsung for picture quality, features, and ease of use.

title: Affordable TV with Great Features
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Getting Started:
The TV was incredibly easy to setup; I was able to physically remove the unit from the box solo. Logging into streaming platforms was easy and intuitive as well, especially if you already have a Samsung account which saves all your app logins from one Samsung TV to the next.

Design and Build:
As an affordable model, this TV impressed me greatly. The bezel is small and accentuates the excellent picture quality. It’s not ultra thin, but I think this is a plus as it feels less fragile when moving. The legs mounts were easy to install and despite their small form factor, feel sturdy and reliable. The remote control is small and bare bones, but functional albeit a tad unresponsive at certain angles.

Picture & Sound:
This TV features beautiful video quality and HDR functionality, with vibrant colors and excellent contrast. Sound is good, but would certainly be enhanced with a sound bar or speaker system.

Smart TV Features:
There’s lots to love here. As a gamer, the Motion Xcelerator system helps enhance the refresh rate to create a smooth gaming experience. The TV also features a game mode which improves the responsiveness even more. The built in voice assistant (tested Bixby) is reliable and works well paired with a Samsung branded phone. The inclusion of Samsung Knox security is a nice addition too, and assists with protection from unauthorized apps and/or security threats which most of us don’t even think about in regards to a TV, so a definite nice touch there. Taken together with the ease of logging into apps, both bluetooth and wifi capabilities, it truly is a versatile device and could easily be used as a living room TV or even a computer monitor. 

Overall Experience: 
This TV rocks! The look, feel, and setup are top tier at this price point with noticeably good gaming performance and an excellent overall value. The weak spot is definitely the remote control, but it’s not a deal-breaker whatsoever. I highly recommend this TV.

title: Great TV, But Not So User-Friendly
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Overall, I like my Samsung Crystal UHD U8000H. The picture is clear, the screen looks great, and as far as being a TV goes, it definitely does its job well. Once I have everything where I want it, I enjoy watching it. However, I do think Samsung could make the everyday experience a little more user-friendly.

My biggest frustration has been navigating the menus. Something as simple as switching over to my cable box took me longer than I expected because I had to figure out where to find the external source. I’ve also had trouble figuring out where to add or download other apps. I usually consider myself pretty capable of figuring out technology, but I’ve found myself Googling instructions for things that I feel should be easy to locate directly on the TV. Even then, the instructions I find online don’t always match what I’m seeing on my screen.

Then there’s the remote. I like that it is small and simple, but the lettering on it is extremely tiny. I find myself having to really look closely just to see what some of the buttons say. A little larger print would make a huge difference.

The U8000H is a good-looking TV with a very nice picture, and I’m happy with it overall. I just wish Samsung had made navigating sources, adding apps, and reading the remote as easy as enjoying the picture. Sometimes simple really is better.

title: Decent everyday tv
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] When I first got the Samsung 55" Crystal UHD, I was honestly surprised by how light it was. I carried it inside by myself while it was still in the box and getting it out was just as easy. I even mounted it on the wall without any help which I have never been able to do with a television this size. The only annoying part was the short power cord. It just was not long enough for where I wanted it, so I had to buy an extension to make it work.
Now that I have been using it in my living room for several weeks, I have a better feel for what I like and what I do not. The picture quality is still really good, but only after changing the settings. Standard mode does not look great, so adjusting the picture mode is pretty much required.
Connecting to the internet through the SmartThings app was simple. I use the remote on my phone sometimes and it works fine. The physical remote takes a little getting used to and it does not have voice commands which I miss, also this particular model doesn't offer the solar charging option remote. The volume controls are a bit confusing, it took several days before I realized how to turn the volume up or down without muting the tv. I can see myself eventually adding back speakers for better sound.
I still enjoy the free Samsung channels with the basic cable type guide. What I do not love is the display layout. There is no way to arrange the apps the way I want which gets frustrating. I also have the MGM Plus streaming service and I cannot use it directly on the Samsung network. The only option is casting from my phone which is not ideal.
Even with those quirks, the television works well in my living room. Once the settings are adjusted, the picture and sound are solid. It is easy to use overall and fits nicely in the space.

title: Don't make the mistake I did, believe the reviews.
body: I brought home from a retailer my purchased 43" Crystal QLED tv 3 days ago. I'm taking it back tomorrow. I researched this/many other products for almost a month. This, much more expensive brand/tv, is doing it after 3 days. It took me over 3 hrs to watch a 2hr recorded movie b/c every time I fast forwarded through commercials, it lost internet connection, & the picture froze. I had to turn it completely off from the wall, wait & start again. It was not my internet, the older tv was working perfectly (& further from the internet source). A clearer picture & slightly better sound is not worth the extra cost or unreliablity. Please take seriously personal reviews & don't think, "this happens with all tvs at times."

title: Best TV of 2026
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I recently purchased the Crystal UHD 2026 TV, and overall, I have been very impressed with the experience. From the moment I set it up, the TV felt like a significant upgrade from my previous television. The design is modern, slim, and clean, so it looks great whether it is mounted on the wall or placed on a TV stand.
The picture quality is one of the biggest strengths of this TV. Colors look bright and vibrant without appearing overly artificial, while the 4K resolution provides plenty of detail. Watching movies and TV shows is particularly enjoyable because the picture feels sharp and clear. I also noticed that scenes with a lot of detail, such as nature documentaries and action movies, look especially impressive. The contrast and overall picture balance are good for everyday viewing, although the experience can vary depending on the lighting in the room.

Another thing I really like is how easy the TV is to use. The interface is straightforward, and navigating between streaming services and other features feels smooth. Apps load quickly, and having access to popular streaming platforms makes it convenient to watch everything in one place. The remote is also simple to understand, which is helpful if you don't want to spend a lot of time figuring out complicated controls.

The sound quality is decent for a built-in TV speaker system. Voices are generally clear, and the sound is perfectly adequate for everyday watching. However, if you want a more immersive cinema-like experience, I would recommend adding a soundbar or external speakers.

Overall, the Crystal UHD 2026 TV offers an excellent combination of picture quality, smart features, design, and ease of use. It is a great choice for watching movies, sports, streaming content, and regular television. For the price, I think it provides very good value and has made my everyday viewing experience much more enjoyable. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a reliable, modern 4K TV.

The clarity is exceptionally sharp, bringing out fine textures and subtle details in every scene. The color expression is remarkably vivid, offering bright, punchy hues alongside deep contrast that makes movies and nature documentaries truly come alive. Even during fast-moving action sequences or intense gaming sessions, the refresh rate keeps up beautifully, providing a consistently crisp and fluid picture without any motion blur.Equally impressive is the smart platform. Samsung’s user interface is incredibly fast and intuitive, making it seamless to switch between live TV and favorite streaming applications. The voice control integration works flawlessly, allowing for hands-free navigation and quick content searches.To round it all out, the audio performance delivers clean, robust sound that remains distortion-free even at higher volumes. This television strikes the ultimate balance between top-tier innovation and everyday user-friendliness. The Samsung U8000 is a fantastic investment that has exceeded all my expectations for family movie nights and casual viewing alike!

title: Affordable TV with Great Features
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Getting Started:
The TV was incredibly easy to setup; I was able to physically remove the unit from the box solo. Logging into streaming platforms was easy and intuitive as well, especially if you already have a Samsung account which saves all your app logins from one Samsung TV to the next.

Design and Build:
As an affordable model, this TV impressed me greatly. The bezel is small and accentuates the excellent picture quality. It’s not ultra thin, but I think this is a plus as it feels less fragile when moving. The legs mounts were easy to install and despite their small form factor, feel sturdy and reliable. The remote control is small and bare bones, but functional albeit a tad unresponsive at certain angles.

Picture & Sound:
This TV features beautiful video quality and HDR functionality, with vibrant colors and excellent contrast. Sound is good, but would certainly be enhanced with a sound bar or speaker system.

Smart TV Features:
There’s lots to love here. As a gamer, the Motion Xcelerator system helps enhance the refresh rate to create a smooth gaming experience. The TV also features a game mode which improves the responsiveness even more. The built in voice assistant (tested Bixby) is reliable and works well paired with a Samsung branded phone. The inclusion of Samsung Knox security is a nice addition too, and assists with protection from unauthorized apps and/or security threats which most of us don’t even think about in regards to a TV, so a definite nice touch there. Taken together with the ease of logging into apps, both bluetooth and wifi capabilities, it truly is a versatile device and could easily be used as a living room TV or even a computer monitor. 

Overall Experience: 
This TV rocks! The look, feel, and setup are top tier at this price point with noticeably good gaming performance and an excellent overall value. The weak spot is definitely the remote control, but it’s not a deal-breaker whatsoever. I highly recommend this TV.

title: Great TV, But Not So User-Friendly
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Overall, I like my Samsung Crystal UHD U8000H. The picture is clear, the screen looks great, and as far as being a TV goes, it definitely does its job well. Once I have everything where I want it, I enjoy watching it. However, I do think Samsung could make the everyday experience a little more user-friendly.

My biggest frustration has been navigating the menus. Something as simple as switching over to my cable box took me longer than I expected because I had to figure out where to find the external source. I’ve also had trouble figuring out where to add or download other apps. I usually consider myself pretty capable of figuring out technology, but I’ve found myself Googling instructions for things that I feel should be easy to locate directly on the TV. Even then, the instructions I find online don’t always match what I’m seeing on my screen.

Then there’s the remote. I like that it is small and simple, but the lettering on it is extremely tiny. I find myself having to really look closely just to see what some of the buttons say. A little larger print would make a huge difference.

The U8000H is a good-looking TV with a very nice picture, and I’m happy with it overall. I just wish Samsung had made navigating sources, adding apps, and reading the remote as easy as enjoying the picture. Sometimes simple really is better.

title: Decent everyday tv
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] When I first got the Samsung 55" Crystal UHD, I was honestly surprised by how light it was. I carried it inside by myself while it was still in the box and getting it out was just as easy. I even mounted it on the wall without any help which I have never been able to do with a television this size. The only annoying part was the short power cord. It just was not long enough for where I wanted it, so I had to buy an extension to make it work.
Now that I have been using it in my living room for several weeks, I have a better feel for what I like and what I do not. The picture quality is still really good, but only after changing the settings. Standard mode does not look great, so adjusting the picture mode is pretty much required.
Connecting to the internet through the SmartThings app was simple. I use the remote on my phone sometimes and it works fine. The physical remote takes a little getting used to and it does not have voice commands which I miss, also this particular model doesn't offer the solar charging option remote. The volume controls are a bit confusing, it took several days before I realized how to turn the volume up or down without muting the tv. I can see myself eventually adding back speakers for better sound.
I still enjoy the free Samsung channels with the basic cable type guide. What I do not love is the display layout. There is no way to arrange the apps the way I want which gets frustrating. I also have the MGM Plus streaming service and I cannot use it directly on the Samsung network. The only option is casting from my phone which is not ideal.
Even with those quirks, the television works well in my living room. Once the settings are adjusted, the picture and sound are solid. It is easy to use overall and fits nicely in the space.

title: Don't make the mistake I did, believe the reviews.
body: I brought home from a retailer my purchased 43" Crystal QLED tv 3 days ago. I'm taking it back tomorrow. I researched this/many other products for almost a month. This, much more expensive brand/tv, is doing it after 3 days. It took me over 3 hrs to watch a 2hr recorded movie b/c every time I fast forwarded through commercials, it lost internet connection, & the picture froze. I had to turn it completely off from the wall, wait & start again. It was not my internet, the older tv was working perfectly (& further from the internet source). A clearer picture & slightly better sound is not worth the extra cost or unreliablity. Please take seriously personal reviews & don't think, "this happens with all tvs at times."

body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I've been using the 43-inch M70H for both everyday entertainment and gaming, and it's exceeded my expectations. After spending some time adjusting the picture settings, the image quality really comes to life. The brightness is excellent for daytime viewing, while the contrast provides deep blacks and vibrant colors that make movies and games look fantastic.
One thing that really stood out is the screen uniformity. Large bright scenes and darker scenes look clean and consistent without distracting patches or uneven lighting. The TV is also very responsive, making menu navigation feel smooth and gameplay enjoyable with very little noticeable delay.
I also appreciate how much control Samsung gives over picture calibration. Being able to fine-tune the image made it easy to find a look that feels natural and accurate for my room. Whether I'm watching shows, playing games, or streaming videos, the picture stays sharp and immersive.
Overall, this has been a reliable, high-quality TV that delivers an excellent viewing experience. It's easy to recommend to anyone looking for a well-rounded display with great picture quality and responsive performance.

title: Very good in it's class and range!
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] In it's class and price range the Samsung M70H Series Mini LED 4K tv is really exceptional. The color is rich and uniform across the screen and the contrast is deep and all facets of the picture have a good range of adjustment. The picture is very bright and the sound is more than acceptable so external speakers are not a necessity. The other feature which works well is the judder control. Using it motion is very smooth, even more so than tv's costing much more. The blacks are acceptable in day or brighter room lights but are not inky in lower light situations. If it had local dimming on the array (which it does not) this would be better. The only other thing that could use a bit of improvement is the off angle viewing which becomes washed out fairly quickly. So for straight on or nearly so viewing it is an easy budget conscious recommendation but if you have off angle seating... I would look elsewhere. Still all in all a good value and nice picture with good motion control.

body:

[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] We were looking to replace our bedroom television. The set was almost 20 years old and just not giving us the experience we wanted. Enter the Samsung 55” M70H Mini LED in 4K

title: Vibrant colors
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Honest Review – Great Sound, Strong Picture, But Needs Some Tweaking
After spending some time with this TV, I’d say it’s a solid overall experience with a few things worth noting.
First, the sound quality really stands out. I wasn’t expecting much from built-in speakers, but this one is surprisingly full and clear. Dialogue comes through crisp, and it has enough depth that I haven’t felt the need to immediately add a soundbar.
The picture quality is generally very good—bright, sharp, and easy to see even in a room with a lot of natural light. It handles daytime viewing well, which was important for my setup. That said, I’ve had a harder time getting the color settings just right. Depending on the content, tones can look a little off or overly saturated, and it takes some adjusting to find a balance that looks natural.
I also experienced an occasional screen glitch where part of the image briefly distorts or shifts horizontally. It doesn’t happen constantly, but when it does, it’s definitely noticeable and interrupts the viewing experience.
On the plus side, the TV itself looks sleek and modern, and setup was quick and easy.
Overall: great sound, strong brightness and clarity, but color calibration and occasional screen issues hold it back a bit. If those were ironed out, this would easily be a top-tier experience.    I did contact Samsung and they were able to help me resolve my problems! They were very helpful and nice!

title: Exceptional 4K Display That Exceeds Expectations
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Picture quality on this TV is outstanding across the board. The brightness is impressive — HDR content really pops, and it handles both bright rooms and darker setups well. Contrast is one of the standout features; the Mini LED backlighting delivers deep blacks without the blooming you'd expect at this price range. Resolution is crisp and detailed in 4K, and upscaling for lower-res content holds up better than expected. Color accuracy is vibrant and well-balanced right out of the box, with rich, natural tones that don't look oversaturated. Clarity during fast motion is smooth — whether it's sports or action-heavy content, there's minimal blur. Overall, this is an excellent display that punches well above its class.

I enjoy listening to music during my morning workout and watching my favorite documentaries in the evening. I love how nicely this television fits with my decor.  As an existing fan of Samsung products, it is no surprised that Samsung knocked it out of the park with a television that is user friendly, provides a great 4k experience and is compact and sleek in appearance.

title: Unreal
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] First, let me just say that upon receiving the box, it was extremely light.   I have had many t v s over the years fifty five inch up and I have never felt or handled the t v that was so lightweight at this size. It's so easy to set up and move if needed.

Next, Right out of the box, the setup was extremely easy and I even used the SmartThings app.\nAs this was the first t v I ever tried it with. Within 2 minutes, it was not only set up in all my accounts were there, but everything was signed in and it even set up the TV just like my projector and my other t v!

Next, I have seen great image quality on products from this brand but this one takes the cake. The blacks were much deeper.The colors were more vibrant , and I even had to tone down the brightness , because the t v itself would light up my entire living space in the evening and it was almost too bright. When?\nSmooth, TV's first came out versus tube TV's.I remember my eyes having to adjust to a great picture quality versus when I was used to.  And this is almost the same.  There is a difference vs even my led 4k tv.

Next, sound on t v's like this have always been hit or miss. On my older models, I would have to change the soundtrack to 2.1 channel versus 5.1 channel just because scenes with a lot of action would be too loud but scenes when people talk would be too soft.  Not only does this alleviate that , but the sound actually seems to come from certain sides of the t v , depending on where the dialogue is or the action is , which is very clear to understand but it also seems like the sound moves with the scene!

Lastly, I was very skeptical about using AI on a TV.But after trying this out , it's just like using a I on the phone only it's tailored to images, movies, music and videos.  I gave the AI several task of finding pictures.Short clips, movies and even things that I knew the title of but just described a part of a scene to see if it would find it and it never missed!

Very well made tv!

title: My 2nd Samsung  Tv
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I'm really happy with my Samsung TV overall. The picture quality is definitely the standout for me The brightness is excellent, especially in a bright room, and the contrast gives the image a really nice sense of depth. Colors look vibrant without being overdone, and everything just looks sharp clean, and detailed
I'm also very pleased with the screen uniformity. Bright and dark areas look consistent, and I haven't noticed anything distracting that takes away from the viewing experience,
The responsiveness of the TV did take a bit of getting used to. The menus, apps, and general interface feel a little different from what I was used to, so there was a bit of a learning curve. That said, once you spend some time with it, it becomes easier and more intuitive
My main disappointment is the sound. I would much rather have the TV audio go through my AV receiver and external speaker setup. The built-in speakers are fine, but if you already have a proper audio system, the integration could definitely be smoother and more straightforward
Overall though, I'm very pleased with it. The brightness, contrast, vibrancy, sharpness, and overall picture quality are all excellent. There's a bit of adjustment needed with the interface, and I'd prefer better integration with an external receiver for sound, but none of that really takes away from how good the picture is
Great picture and a very enjoyable TV overall

title: Love the picture, the remote and menus not so much
body: This is a re-write of my review, as requested by Samsung:  For the picture on this TV I would give it 5-stars.  The picture and the screen's abilities to provide an excellent picture are outstanding.  It is able to provide anything you might prefer from quite dim to absolutely brilliantly bright.  Contrast can be adjusted to the same level of extremes as the brightness.  The uniformity of the picture is also all that you could ask of a set, especially in this price range.  Being a 4K TV, its ability to upscale is something to really appreciate and is apparent when watching media that was made pre-1080I, as the upscaling feature does improve the lower resolution of those productions in most cases.  The sound is fairly decent considering the set is a simple two-speaker, down-firing system, with a relatively low-powered amplifier.  Sadly though, like so many manufacturers today have done, the only audio out is for optical devices only.  Long gone are any "legacy" hook-ups and I should point out here that not only includes the sound output, buy the video input as well.  You can no longer use RGB, component or even the traditional fall-back default of RCA composite connections.  There's HDMI in and Optical audio out.  There is a single USB A port that can be used to input from USB memory media devices for movies, videos, etc.  All of these things are pluses for this set and we like them.  Now, for what we don't like:  One, the included remote is sorely lacking in what it is able to control on the TV, mostly due to it being done in a "minimalist" style.  What I'm saying here is Samsung has attempted to move as much control from the included remote to the screen itself.  If you've been paying attention to what has been happening in new cars with the manufacturers removing buttons and knobs from the dashboards, and placing them on a screen on the dash instead, well they've done on this TV.  Samsung has tried to strike a similar aesthetic here on this TV and probably all of their sets.  To put it simply, we don't like what they've done.  The few buttons that remain on the remote are very poorly labeled, and some of them don't move in an intuitive manner.  For example, there are two very small rectangular buttons that stick up from the surface of the remote about 1/16th of an inch.  It took me quite some time to realize you needed to use these to change the channel, but you don't "push down" to get a response.  You must "catch" the top edge of these little buttons to "rock" or "nudge" them either forward or backward.  If you're anything like the average person you will frequently find your fingers simply sliding over the top of the button because they're very small, they do not stick up very far and the plastic is very smooth, almost slippery.  This is very much how the design of the entire included remote is done.  Not easy to use, almost indecipherable and actually small enough that you can easily have it fall out your hand if you aren't careful with it.  Now, our second dislike and it looms large for us.  This isn't our first 4K Samsung set.  Our first Samsung 4K set is now about 10 years old, but its menu system is far more intuitive, logical and understandable.  Our new MiniLED set's menus are very trying, not logical and many times the only way to actually pull something up that you want is to use the search function.  We are keeping the TV because we love the picture and sound, and we found an excellent work-around so that we can use our new set.  The remote from our 10 year old Samsung 4K set works perfectly with the new set, and the way it was laid out brings back the logic and control that was missing due to the included remote being almost useless for us.  With the old remote we now can access every feature on this new TV and do not have to hunt and depend on moving a little cursor around on the screen to back control.  Good TV, bad remote and software.

title: Brighter Than Most, But Falls Short Outdoors
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] We set this TV up on our beach property under a shaded structure, where cutting through heavy sunlight and reflections is our main goal. Compared to a standard 4K LCD TV, this model is noticeably brighter and performs significantly better in ambient light.

​However, it still falls a bit short of what we were hoping for in our specific setup. Even under shade, the outdoor glare and natural brightness are tough to overcome, and it doesn't quite cut through the reflections as much as we needed during peak daylight hours.

body:

Samsung's home screen is incredibly clunky compared to other operating systems. There is no way to disable the autoplay (or everything I've tried so far isn't working) so shortly after starting the TV it automatically starts playing one of the previous programs. This is one reason why I'm now considering taking this back and getting a different TV. 

You have to go through and sign up for all of the Samsung accounts in order to get fully logged in to this TV. I didn't realize when I purchased the TV that I would have to marry the company. The selection of apps that are available is very limited, and if you want to take cast from your phone there are a lot of tricks that you have to figure out. Maybe this TV is good for those who have already immersed themselves and Samsung products, but this television is definitely not intuitive enough for the average person just looking for a good TV that is easy to use.

The picture on the television seems fine, but that is about all that I like about it.

title: Poor user interface
body:
This is thee worst user interface I've ever used on any TV in my lifetime. I had a 65" Samsung TV and it was nice, that's why I bumped up to a 75". Big mistake. All the user controls are hidden in a maze of confusion that takes you minutes to find for adjustment. For live TV you literally have to go and make sure the guide is on which ever TV channels you're using. If you're watching Samsung TV and you switch to OTA content, want to change the channel, you literally have to go back into the maze, find the menu for OTA channels and click on that or your channel will change back to Samsung TV channels. Super horrible interface!!
Next, there's no optical out. WHAT IN THE WORLD‽‽
99% of the home theater systems use optical for their audio. But not this one, right? If your system doesn't support eARC audio, you're screwed...
Next, when you watch a streaming service, it automatically switches from whatever TV screen mode you're using, over to film maker mode. Yup... You now have to go back into the maze and manually turn your mode back to whatever you were using...
In short, whoever developed the user interface for this TV should, needs to be fired!!!
This will be the last Samsung TV that I'll ever buy, FACT!!
